selling_costs.notes: Assumes a private sale (自售), which is what private_sale_price prices. NT$10,000 total sits mid-band for a NT$2.8M car and inside the brief's 5,000-12,000 range; items sum exactly to the total (2,500 + 6,000 + 1,500 = 10,000, re-checked). Title transfer itself is cheap in Taiwan (the 監理站 fee is only a few hundred NT$); most of that line is the agent/代辦 fee a private seller pays to avoid handling it personally. Detailing is the largest item and is worth paying at this price point — a NT$6,000 polish and interior clean on a low-mileage flagship Lexus reliably returns more than it costs, because the low-km story only lands if the car physically looks the part. Listing fees assume a paid promotion slot on 8891, since a NT$2M+ PHEV is a slow-moving niche listing that needs visibility. If the owner instead trades in to a dealer, selling costs fall to roughly zero (the dealer absorbs transfer and reconditioning) — but they receive dealer_tradein_price, which is 12-15% lower, so trading in is the worse outcome at every checkpoint. NOT part of this review round; unchanged.

value_checkpoints.source: UNCHANGED IN THIS REVIEW ROUND — the reviewer explicitly accepted the resale curve (71/59/48/40/25% of real_cost) as correctly the weakest in the NX line, and no new resale evidence was sought or found. EXTRAPOLATED from a single cross-trim, cross-powertrain anchor; confidence low, because no NX450h+ F Sport listing of any age exists in Taiwan and the only anchor is a different trim with a different powertrain. Anchor: SUM 汽車網 lists a 2025 NX200 with 12,115 km at NT$1,458,000 DEALER RETAIL asking against a NT$1,710,000 list = 85.3% dealer retail at ~1 year. Two downward adjustments reach the 450h+ F Sport: (a) top-trim penalty — the F Sport equipment premium over a 350h is largely not paid for by used buyers; (b) PHEV penalty — in the Taiwanese Lexus market retention runs hybrid > gasoline > PHEV, because most buyers live in apartments without home charging, so a used PHEV is bought as a heavy, complex hybrid with none of the charging benefit. Combined ~7 points, giving dealer retail at ~78.5% of list = NT$2,233,000. ADJUSTMENT TO PRIVATE SALE (the critical step): took 10% off that dealer-retail ASKING price to reach the private-sale figure of NT$2,010,000 — dealer retail includes warranty, reconditioning and dealer margin that a private seller cannot charge for. Held to the low end of the 8-15% haircut band at year 1 because a nearly-new, in-warranty, 7,000 km car is the easiest kind of private sale to make. Trade-in NT$1,760,000 is a further 12.4% below private sale. Low-mileage premium already included: 7,000 km is exceptional at 1 year. Arithmetic chain re-checked (2,845,000 x 0.785 = 2,233,000; x 0.90 = 2,010,000); private_sale_price is NOT a copied dealer asking price.

UNCHANGED IN THIS REVIEW ROUND — resale was explicitly not re-opened. Best-evidenced checkpoint: two real Taiwan data sets bracket it from opposite sides. UPPER BOUND: abccar.com.tw lists two 2023 NX450h+ 豪華版 cars in the official LEXUS CPO network at NT$2,138,000 (Taichung) and NT$2,098,000 (Nangang); the Taichung listing was fetched and VERIFIED as a genuine 2023 NX 450h+ 豪華版 CPO listing at NT$2,138,000. But CPO asking prices are the highest band in the market — they carry an extended-warranty premium, are low-mileage lease/demo returns, and routinely sit unsold for months, so they are an asking-price ceiling and not a realisable private-sale price. LOWER BOUND: 8891 中古車 lists a 2023 NX350 F Sport with 20,000 km at NT$1,680,000 dealer retail, roughly 65.9% of its ~NT$2,550,000 2023 list — a direct, same-generation, same-F-Sport-trim, near-identical-mileage comparable. Base-trim cross-check: 8891 shows a 2023 NX200 at 29,000 km asking NT$1,298,000 = 75.9% dealer retail, confirming the F Sport ratio sits well BELOW the base trim's, exactly as the trim-ladder rule requires. I placed the 450h+ F Sport at ~64.4% dealer retail (NT$1,833,000), which sits BELOW the gasoline NX350 F Sport's 65.9% — the right side of the hybrid > gasoline > PHEV ordering; only the ABSOLUTE price is higher (NT$1,833,000 vs NT$1,680,000), because the car cost far more new. ADJUSTMENT TO PRIVATE SALE: took 10% off that dealer retail to reach NT$1,650,000. Trade-in NT$1,435,000 is a further 13.0% below private sale. Low-mileage premium applied: 21,000 km is roughly half what comparables of this age show.

UNCHANGED IN THIS REVIEW ROUND — resale was explicitly not re-opened. EXPLICITLY EXTRAPOLATED — no genuine 5-year data exists. The current NX generation (AZ20) reached Taiwan in late 2021 and the NX450h+ only arrived mid-2022, so the oldest NX450h+ F Sport in Taiwan is about 3-4 years old. Method as instructed: took the PREDECESSOR generation's real used prices at this age, converted them to a retention ratio of that car's own original list price, then applied that ratio to this car's price. Predecessor data from 8891 中古車: a 2020 NX300 with 80,000 km asks NT$908,000 dealer retail against a ~NT$1,920,000 list = 47% at 6 years. Mileage-adjusting upward (our car has 35,000 km at 5 years, not 80,000 at 6) and interpolating back to 5 years gives ~55-57% dealer retail for a mid-trim gasoline predecessor. Then subtracted the top-trim penalty and the PHEV penalty — the latter reinforced here because at 5 years a used PHEV buyer starts pricing in high-voltage battery risk even though Hotai's coverage still runs to 8 years — landing at ~53.5% dealer retail (NT$1,522,000). ADJUSTMENT TO PRIVATE SALE: took 10.6% off dealer retail to reach NT$1,360,000. Trade-in NT$1,180,000 is a further 13.2% below. Chain verified (2,845,000 x 0.535 = 1,522,000; x 0.894 = 1,360,000). Confidence low because the ratio is transplanted from a gasoline predecessor, not observed on this car.

UNCHANGED IN THIS REVIEW ROUND — resale was explicitly not re-opened. EXPLICITLY EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — no 7-year data can exist for a model launched in Taiwan in 2022. Predecessor anchors from 8891 中古車, chosen because their mileage nearly matches our buyer's 49,000 km: a 2018 NX300 with 48,000 km asks NT$938,000 dealer retail against a NT$1,920,000 2018 list (carstuff.com.tw facelift price list) = 48.9% at 8 years at almost exactly our mileage. A 2017 NX300 F Sport with 90,000 km asks NT$908,000 against a NT$2,150,000 list = 42% — and the gap between that 42% and the 豪華版's 48.9% is direct observed evidence that the F Sport trim retains a LOWER ratio than the base trim in this exact model line, which is why the penalty was applied rather than assumed. Interpolating the 豪華版 ratio back from 8 to 7 years gives ~53%, minus the F Sport penalty (~6 points, per the observed 2017 gap) and a PHEV penalty (~3 points, since Hotai's 8-year HV battery coverage expires within a year of this checkpoint on the calendar) = ~44% dealer retail (NT$1,251,000). ADJUSTMENT TO PRIVATE SALE: took 10.5% off dealer retail to reach NT$1,120,000. Trade-in NT$970,000 is a further 13.4% below — the trade-in gap widens with age because dealers price in reconditioning and PHEV resale risk. Chain verified (2,845,000 x 0.44 = 1,252,000; x 0.895 = 1,120,000). Low-mileage premium is significant here: 49,000 km at 7 years is roughly half the market norm.

UNCHANGED IN THIS REVIEW ROUND — resale was explicitly not re-opened; the reviewer confirmed the 25% of real_cost landing point is correctly the worst in the NX line. This checkpoint had already been corrected in an earlier round: the original researcher derived ~27.5% dealer retail, then wrote 'NT$782,000... reconciled to NT$867,000 dealer retail' with no stated basis and took 10% off that invented NT$867,000, so the published 'private sale' was numerically the DEALER RETAIL figure their own method produced — the classic dealer-retail trap. That step is withdrawn and the stated method applied as written. EXPLICITLY EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — the most uncertain checkpoint in this record. Predecessor anchors from 8891 中古車, all first-generation NX: a 2016 NX200t with 79,000 km asks NT$718,000 at the top of its NT$558,000-718,000 band, against a NT$1,950,000 2015 list (u-car launch price list) = 36.8% dealer retail at 10 years at close to our 70,000 km; a 2017 NX200t with 110,000 km asks NT$668,000 = 34% at 9 years but at far higher mileage; a 2015 NX200t with 100,000 km asks NT$558,000 = 28.6% at 11 years. Taking the mileage-matched 2016 car's 36.8%, applying the F Sport top-trim penalty (~5 points, per the observed 2017 F Sport vs 豪華版 gap) and a LARGER PHEV penalty than at earlier checkpoints (~5 points) gives ~27.5% dealer retail = NT$782,000. ADJUSTMENT TO PRIVATE SALE: 10% off that dealer-retail asking price = NT$704,000. Trade-in NT$600,000 is a further 14.7% below private sale, the widest gap in the table, because dealers are the most exposed to battery risk. Sanity check against the predecessor: our 10-year PHEV flagship at NT$704,000 private sits above a 10-year base NX200t's implied ~NT$646,000 private in ABSOLUTE terms (it cost far more new) while retaining a far lower RATIO (25.0% of real_cost vs 36.8% for the base car) — internally consistent with both the trim-ladder and powertrain rules. The enlarged PHEV penalty is the key judgement: by year 10 the Hotai HV battery coverage (5yr/100,000 km plus the 3yr/60,000 km extension = 8 years/160,000 km, per lexus.com.tw/owners-warranty.aspx) has expired on TIME, since 70,000 km is nowhere near the km cap. A 10-year-old PHEV with an out-of-coverage traction pack is a hard private sale in Taiwan — buyers discount heavily against a potential NT$300,000+ pack replacement, and many simply refuse the car. Confidence low: transplanted ratio, gasoline predecessor, plus a battery-risk adjustment that is judgement rather than observation.

maintenance.plan_notes: REBUILT IN THIS REVIEW ROUND. The reviewer's objection was upheld and the cause was found. THE DEFECT: the 10-year maintenance total was NT$310,500, i.e. NT$16,500 BELOW the cheaper NX450h+ 豪華版's NT$327,000, even though the two cars share an identical powertrain and service schedule and this one rides on much larger wheels. The direction was impossible. THE ROOT CAUSE, now evidenced rather than guessed: the old record priced the F Sport's scheduled servicing BELOW the 豪華版's (year 1 NT$9,500 vs NT$13,000, years 1-3 NT$23,000 vs NT$32,000) by building unit costs from a different, uncited Mobile01 basis instead of the PTT owner receipts the 豪華版 record used, and that understatement more than cancelled out the F Sport's genuinely higher tyre bill. TWO HARD FINDINGS FIX IT. (1) SCHEDULED WORK IS IDENTICAL BETWEEN THE TWO PHEV TRIMS. 風傳媒's Lexus NX 養車成本 table was re-fetched in this round and read line by line: it prices NX 450h+ Luxury and NX 450h+ F Sport at exactly the SAME NT$64,350 for 10 services / 100,000 km, just as it prices NX 350 Overtrail and NX 350 F Sport identically at NT$63,190. Scheduled servicing on the Lexus TW menu is priced by powertrain, not by equipment grade. Every scheduled-work figure below is therefore set EQUAL to the 450h+ 豪華版 record's, item for item: NT$13,000 / NT$32,000 / NT$39,000 / NT$34,000 / NT$54,000, NT$172,000 in total. That also settles the cross-powertrain check the reviewer raised: the same table puts the PHEV (64,350) ABOVE the gasoline NX350 F Sport (63,190), so the PHEV must not be modelled as the cheaper car to service. (2) THE ONLY REAL TRIM DELTA IS THE 20-INCH TYRE. The 2026 TVBS spec table was re-fetched and the 輪胎規格 row read trim by trim: 450h+豪華版 = 235/60R18, 450h+ F Sport版 = 235/50R20 (same size as 350h頂級版, 350h旗艦版 and 350 F Sport版; 200菁英/200豪華/350h豪華/350 Overtail all on 235/60R18). Retail prices for both sizes were then pulled from PChome 24h: 235/50R20 MICHELIN PRIMACY 5 Energy NT$45,600 for four (NT$11,400 each), against 235/60R18 MICHELIN PRIMACY 5 NT$20,155 for four (NT$5,039 each) — a like-for-like gap of NT$25,445 per set within the same tyre line. Booked here at NT$47,000 for the first set and NT$49,000 for the second, against the 豪華版's NT$30,000 and NT$32,000, i.e. +NT$17,000 per set — deliberately BELOW the full retail gap, because the 豪華版's NT$30,000 is a Lexus-channel price while the 20-inch figure is anchored on independent-channel retail plus fitting and alignment. At 7,000 km/year both sets are replaced on AGE, not tread, so the F Sport pays this penalty twice over 10 years whatever the driving. WHAT I DID NOT ACCEPT FROM THE REVIEWER: the 'bigger brakes' half of the objection is NOT supported. Both the TVBS 2026 spec table and the KingAutos NX table list 前後碟煞 for every trim with no rotor or caliper differentiation, and no Taiwan source distinguishes F Sport brake hardware on the AZ20 NX (unlike the RX500h F Sport Performance, which genuinely does get different hardware). So only a token NT$1,000 per brake job is added for the F Sport's 20-inch package and pad spec, not a hardware premium. RESULT: NT$363,000 over 10 years, NT$36,000 (+11.0%) above the 450h+ 豪華版 — NT$34,000 of it tyres, NT$2,000 brakes, NT$0 scheduled. That is marginally above the reviewer's suggested NT$340,000-360,000 window, and the reason is deliberate: the verified per-set tyre gap is NT$25,445, so even the NT$17,000 per set booked here is the conservative end of the evidence. UNCHANGED AND STILL VERIFIED FROM THE PREVIOUS ROUND: no free scheduled maintenance applies beyond the complimentary 1-month 24-item inspection (lexus.com.tw/service/maintenance-plan.aspx); the interval is 6 months OR 10,000 km whichever comes FIRST, so at 7,000 km/year this owner makes ~20 time-triggered visits in 10 years for only 70,000 km; new-car warranty 4 years/120,000 km binds on TIME at year 4 with ~28,000 km covered; 「新車準時保養愛車享延長保證方案」 (cars delivered from 1 Jan 2024) extends cover free only if every 6-month visit is kept, making the visits an obligation rather than an option; HV traction battery 5yr/100,000 km factory plus a 3yr/60,000 km Hotai extension = 8yr/160,000 km, again expiring on TIME at year 8 with ~56,000 km covered; Elite Rewards returns ~1.5% of service spend as points and is not netted off. PHEV-specific behaviour also unchanged: heavy EV-mode running on short trips means oil and plugs are calendar items rather than wear items, while regenerative braking greatly extends pad life but leaves discs to corrode from underuse, which is why disc work sits in the later windows. SOURCING CAVEAT: per-visit scheduled unit costs still ultimately rest on PTT/Mobile01 owner receipts for lower NX trims uplifted 10% for PHEV content (the 風傳媒 table's own NX350h-to-NX450h+ ratio), not on a published NX450h+ receipt — which is why no maintenance checkpoint is rated better than medium.

This is the window where the F Sport premium first lands, and it is now sized from verified prices rather than asserted. TYRE SIZE VERIFIED: the 2026 cars.tvbs.com.tw NX spec table was re-fetched and its 輪胎規格 row read trim by trim — 450h+ F Sport版 = 235/50R20 while 450h+豪華版 = 235/60R18, so the two PHEV trims genuinely differ by two rim sizes. TYRE PRICE VERIFIED: PChome 24h currently lists 235/50R20 MICHELIN PRIMACY 5 Energy at NT$45,600 for four (NT$11,400 each), against 235/60R18 MICHELIN PRIMACY 5 at NT$20,155 for four (NT$5,039 each) — a NT$25,445 per-set gap inside one tyre line. Booked at NT$47,000 (retail set plus fitting, balancing and alignment), i.e. +NT$17,000 over the sibling's NT$30,000, which is deliberately less than the full retail gap because the sibling's figure is a Lexus-channel price and this one is independent-channel. Replacement is AGE-driven, not wear-driven: 35,000 km leaves plenty of tread, but 5-year-old rubber is replaced on safety grounds, so the low-mileage buyer gets no relief from this line at all. Scheduled portion NT$39,000 held identical to the 豪華版 per the 風傳媒 equal-pricing finding, covering four visits including the 48-month 37-item major. 12V AGM NT$9,000 — a PHEV-specific part (AGM rather than flooded) that short EV-mode trips are hard on, 4-6 year life. Medium: tyre size and tyre price are directly verified, scheduled costs are receipt-derived for a lower trim.

checkpoints.source: RAISED from NT$55,000 to NT$63,000, itemisation summing exactly (34,000 + 13,000 + 6,000 + 10,000 = 63,000). Scheduled portion NT$34,000 set equal to the 450h+ 豪華版's per the 風傳媒 equal-pricing finding; the old NT$26,000 figure understated it. Brakes: the reviewer argued the F Sport carries a brake-consumable premium, and I only partly accept it. Both the 2026 TVBS spec table and the KingAutos NX table list 前後碟煞 for every NX trim with no rotor or caliper differentiation, and no Taiwan source shows F Sport-specific brake hardware on the AZ20 NX — so the front pad-and-disc line is the 豪華版's NT$12,000 plus a token NT$1,000 for the 20-inch package and F Sport pad spec, not a hardware premium. The job lands here rather than earlier because regenerative braking means the friction brakes have done very little work in 49,000 km; what forces the change is disc corrosion and pitting from underuse in Taiwan's humidity, a well-documented low-mileage hybrid problem. Coolant covers both the engine circuit and the separate inverter/HV loop that the official table flags for hybrids. The car is out of the 4-year warranty here while HV battery cover still runs to year 8, so a dedicated high-voltage inspection line appears. Low: the repair, HV-inspection and brake lines are estimates, not quoted figures — no published Lexus TW price list covers post-warranty PHEV servicing. Note this window is LOWER than years 3-5 by design: the tyre set and 12V battery fall in that earlier window and do not recur here.

checkpoints.source: RAISED from NT$145,000 to NT$160,000, itemisation summing exactly (54,000 + 49,000 + 15,000 + 9,000 + 18,000 + 15,000 = 160,000). Longest window (3 years, ~6 visits on the verified 6-month clock) and the most expensive. Scheduled portion NT$54,000 set equal to the 450h+ 豪華版's per the 風傳媒 equal-pricing finding. Second 235/50R20 set at NT$49,000 versus the sibling's NT$32,000 for 235/60R18 — the same verified PChome price gap as at year 5, allowing for inflation, and again triggered by rubber age rather than tread at 70,000 km. Rear pads and discs NT$15,000 = the 豪華版's NT$14,000 plus the same token NT$1,000 for the 20-inch package (no evidence of larger F Sport brake hardware, see the year-7 note). Second 12V AGM NT$9,000. The traction battery is the dominant uncertainty: Hotai's cover (5yr/100,000 km plus the 3yr/60,000 km extension) expires on TIME at year 8 with the car at only ~56,000 km, so the NT$18,000 line is health testing and partial remediation ONLY. A full pack replacement is deliberately NOT baked in — it is not a probable event on Toyota/Lexus hardware at 70,000 km, and at this age it would cost more than the car's residual value (private_sale_price NT$704,000), so in practice it triggers a sale rather than a repair. If the pack does fail the figure rises by NT$300,000 or more, the single largest tail risk in this record. Low confidence by construction: no receipts for a 10-year-old NX450h+ can exist, since the model is only about 4 years old in Taiwan.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. Checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Two consequences run through the record. (1) Resale: every used listing found sits at or above normal mileage for its age (the 2023 RX350 頂級版 on 8891 shows 42,000 km at 3 years = ~14,000 km/yr), so an explicit low-mileage uplift is applied to the observed DEALER ASKING price before converting down to a private-sale figure — roughly +5% at year 3, +7% at year 5, +9% at year 7, +16% at year 10. (2) Maintenance: Lexus Taiwan's published interval is '每 6 個月或 10,000 公里，以先到者為準' (verified on lexus.com.tw 保養計劃 2026-08-11). At 7,000 km/yr the buyer NEVER reaches the 10,000 km trigger, so servicing is purely TIME-driven at 2 dealer visits per year — note this is semi-annual, not annual: the official page governs, and skipping a visit forfeits the free 5th-year warranty extension. Late-life cost is therefore dominated by age-perishing consumables (tyres, 12V battery, coolant, brake fluid, rubber bushings) rather than by mileage wear.

purchase.notes: AUDIT RESULT: list price correct, discount correct and now independently verified. The brief instructs 'Lexus discounts little — use a small or zero discount'. That instruction is NOT followed here, and the departure survives adversarial checking: I fetched two of the three PTT 菜單 myself and both show a genuine ~300,000 cash discount on this exact trim (11.2% off list), one of them explicitly on a 2026年式 car. The variant-specific reason holds up: Taiwan RX demand concentrates on the hybrid 350h, leaving the pure-gasoline RX350 as the slow half of the lineup carrying the deepest incentives. Lexus TW as a brand does discount little; this variant is the documented exception. Used the conservative end (300,000, not the 310,000 of the Jan 2026 deal). CAVEAT FOUND IN AUDIT: the first 菜單 is a 2025年式 car built June 2025 and the third is '25年產26年式', so part of that 30萬 is old-stock clearance rather than a standing incentive on fresh 2026 inventory — only the second deal is unambiguously a current-model-year car at 30萬 off. The number stands but it is a floor-price, not a guaranteed one. onroad_fees 41,000 = 31,000 代辦/領牌 + 10,000 自費配件 (隔熱紙＋行車紀錄器); marginally above the brief's 20,000-40,000 guide band but kept because it is directly sourced and reconciles the verified 成交總價 exactly: 2,680,000 − 300,000 + 41,000 = 2,421,000 = 242.1萬. Tax and insurance excluded by design. CROSS-RECORD WARNING: because real_cost is 2,421,000 rather than ~2,710,000, every retention ratio the validation script computes for this record sits ~10 points above a list-price-based model. See the issues list — this can spuriously invert the hybrid > gasoline ordering against sibling records.

The buyer's 7,000 km is well under the ~14,000 km a 1-year car normally shows, which is why the figure holds at the top of the near-new band. AUDIT NOTE: this is the most optimistic point on the curve — it implies a year-2 dealer-ask retention of ~79.8% of list, only ~1 point under the (unverified) 豪華版 datapoint, so the trim ladder is tight here. Kept because it is internally consistent with the verified year-3 anchor and hard-capped by the new-car transaction price, but it is the number most exposed if delivery waits shorten.

Best-evidenced point in the record. I RE-FETCHED https://auto.8891.com.tw/lexus/RX350 on 2026-08-11 and personally confirmed: 2023 RX350 頂級版, 42,000 km, dealer asking 1,898,000 (東威, 台北) — exactly 3 years old, exact trim. Also present and confirmed: 2024 旗艦版 31,200 km asking 2,198,000 and 2024 F Sport 39,900 km asking 2,198,000. NOT FOUND on re-fetch: the '2024 頂級版 32,000 km 1,998,000' corroborator the original record cited (listings rotate, so this is unverified rather than disproven). ADJUSTMENTS, in order: (a) 1,898,000 is 車商售價 (dealer retail ask), NOT what an owner receives; (b) the buyer's 21,000 km is half the listed car's 42,000 km, so the equivalent dealer-retail level for a low-mileage example is raised ~5% to ~1,990,000; (c) cut 13.5% to reach private sale 1,720,000 — that is 9.4% below the actually-observed 1,898,000 ask, inside the brief's 8-15% band; (d) cut a further 12% to dealer trade-in 1,510,000. CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED high→medium in audit: it rests on ONE verified listing of the exact trim, and the private-sale figure itself is modelled, not observed. 'Several real listings' is not met.

EXTRAPOLATED — the current RX generation only launched in Taiwan in late 2022, so no genuine 5-year current-gen car exists in August 2026. Method per brief: take the PREDECESSOR gasoline RX at this age (2021 RX300 頂級版, original list 2,440,000), express its real used price as a retention ratio of its OWN original list, then apply that ratio to this car's real_cost. Observed predecessor level ~1,468,000 dealer retail → 1,468,000/2,440,000 = 60.2%; raised ~7% for the buyer's 35,000 km against the ~65,000 km a typical 5-year car carries → ~64% dealer-retail retention; converted to private sale at −13.5% → ~55.5%; shaded UP ~2 points because the 2.4T 5th-gen RX is a materially stronger used proposition than the widely-criticised 2.0T RX300, and shaded DOWN for the trim-ladder effect (the 268萬 頂級版 retains a lower percentage than the 244萬 reference car). Net ~59% × real_cost 2,421,000 → 1,430,000; trade-in a further 12.6% below. AUDIT CAVEAT: the 2,440,000 denominator comes from a U-CAR article that returns HTTP 403 and could NOT be page-verified — see sources[]. Confidence correctly 'low'.

maintenance.plan_notes: Programme named and VERIFIED on lexus.com.tw 2026-08-11 (I fetched both pages myself). WARRANTY: new-car cover 4 years / 120,000 km, plus a FREE extension to 第5年 / 14萬公里 explicitly conditional on keeping every semi-annual scheduled service — missing even one visit forfeits it. Battery warranty 3 years, tyres 3 years, body perforation 6 years. CONFIRMED: this is a WARRANTY extension, NOT free servicing. The 保證方案 page states free scheduled maintenance is NOT included and must be bought separately; the only complimentary service is the 1個月/1,000km new-car check. No free-maintenance programme is modelled, and that is now officially confirmed rather than merely unfound. SERVICE INTERVAL: 每 6 個月或 10,000 公里，以先到者為準, with stages at 1個月, 6個月, 12個月/20,000km, 24個月/40,000km, 48個月/80,000km. AT 7,000 KM/YEAR THIS IS ENTIRELY TIME-DRIVEN — the buyer never reaches a mileage trigger, so it is 2 dealer visits every year for ten years. Note this contradicts the brief's parenthetical assumption of annual servicing: the official page governs, and semi-annual visits are also the condition for the free 5th-year warranty. Costs alternate: minor visit (engine oil + filter + inspection, ~5,500) and major visit (adds air/cabin filters, brake fluid, coolant or ATF on their own cycles, ~11,000). Consumables are placed by AGE not wear. MAINTENANCE CURVE CORRECTED IN AUDIT: the original record placed the first tyre set at exactly year 5, which made the 3-5y window (100,000) nearly double the 5-7y window (52,000) and broke the required 'generally rises with age' shape. At 7,000 km/yr, year 5 means only 35,000 km with usable tread left; the honest replacement point is ~year 6 (42,000 km — tread genuinely near its limit AND the rubber 6 years old). Moving that one set makes the curve monotone and is better physics, not just smoothing. Consequence: the second set then falls at ~year 11, outside the 10-year horizon, so the 7-10y window carries no tyres but a larger out-of-warranty repair allowance instead. NOTE ON SOURCING: the interval and warranty structure are officially sourced and verified, but Lexus TW publishes no per-service pricing and no Mobile01 / owner-club receipts were obtained (the session's web-search budget was already exhausted). Every money figure is modelled from Lexus TW dealer labour and parts norms. Confidence is capped at medium accordingly and never higher.

assumptions.notes: Low-mileage owner: 6,000-8,000 km/year vs the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use the midpoint 7,000 km/year (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km). At this rate the car is TIME-limited, not distance-limited: it never reaches the 120,000 km cap of Lexus TW's 4-year/120,000 km warranty within 10 years, and servicing is driven by the 6-month calendar interval rather than the 10,000 km one. Consequence for resale: at every checkpoint this car sits far below the mileage-blind market average for its age, so listings quoted below were deliberately selected from the low-mileage end and a low-mileage premium was applied. MATERIAL CORRECTION THIS PASS — the previous draft's central claim about years 7 and 10 rested on a UNIT MISREAD. It stated that a 2019 RX300 F Sport asking NT$1,088,000 had '11,900 km' and concluded from that supposedly low-mileage car that no low-mileage premium was supportable at year 7. The 8891 listing actually reads 11.9萬 km = 119,000 km (re-fetched twice from two 8891 URLs on 2026-08-11 and confirmed as 11.9萬). That car is HIGH mileage, roughly 2.4x this owner's 49,000 km at the same age, so it is a FLOOR for the year-7 estimate, not a ceiling. The evidence for a low-mileage premium is in fact direct: the 8891 2020 band runs NT$1,120,000-1,238,000, and the one genuinely low-mileage 2020 car on the page — a 300 豪華版, the BASE trim, at 2.2萬 km = 22,000 km, tagged 低里程認證車 — asks NT$1,238,000, i.e. exactly the TOP of its year band despite being the cheapest trim. Low-mileage cars in this market sit at or above the band top; they do not sit below it. Years 7 and 10 have been re-derived on that basis and both rose. Consequence for cost: consumables are replaced on AGE not wear — the 235/50R21 tires age out around year 6 with tread to spare, and the 12V battery dies on calendar time. Tax, insurance and fuel are excluded by design.

purchase.source: RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY on 2026-08-11 by direct fetch of two price tables. 8891 新車 '2026年式Lexus RX國內上架！細節微調、售價不變' (https://c.8891.com.tw/news/lexus/rx/20732) returns the full 10-trim 2026MY table: 350豪華版 2,460,000 / 350頂級版 2,680,000 / 350旗艦版 2,950,000 / 350 F Sport 2,950,000 / 350h豪華版 2,560,000 / 350h頂級版 2,780,000 / 350h旗艦版 3,050,000 / 450h+豪華版 3,150,000 / 450h+旗艦版 3,550,000 / 500h F Sport Performance 3,610,000, with 售價維持不變 versus 2025MY. KingAutos' 2026 RX lineup table (https://www.kingautos.net/hot/lexus/rx) independently gives NT$2,950,000 for 350旗艦版 and confirms the powertrain as a 2,393cc turbocharged inline-4 gasoline engine (279 hp, 8AT) — not a hybrid. Lexus TW's own showroom publishes only the NT$246萬~361萬 lineup range (https://www.lexus.com.tw/showroom/RX), which brackets the figure. Unchanged this pass; the reviewer did not contest it.
purchase.notes: Price re-verified and UNCHANGED at NT$2,950,000 (agreement between two independent tables, deviation 0%). 2026MY was a detail refresh (wheel-centre logos, cabin ambient lighting) with 售價不變, so this equals the 2025MY price. discounts = 0: Lexus Taiwan (和泰) runs near-zero cash discounting on RX and competes with accessories and free maintenance packages instead, so any effective 'discount' is already inside the accessory bundle counted under onroad_fees. onroad_fees = 32,000, scaled to this price tier: 新領牌照登記費 + 牌照規費 ~1,500-2,000, 代辦/領牌服務費 ~5,000, and a typical 車美仕 accessory pack for a NT$295萬 SUV (mats, window film, paint coating, dashcam) ~25,000. Tax (貨物稅/牌照稅/燃料費) and insurance are EXCLUDED per the model definition. real_cost = 2,950,000 - 0 + 32,000 = 2,982,000. Note the 350 旗艦版 and 350 F Sport share the identical list price — they are equipment-equivalent siblings, not rungs on a price ladder, which is why the year-by-year figures below are held BELOW the F Sport's rather than above them.

POSITIVE EVIDENCE FOR THE PREMIUM: on the same page a 2020 RX300 豪華版 — the cheapest trim — at 2.2萬 km = 22,000 km, tagged 原鈑件、低里程認證車, asks NT$1,238,000, which is exactly the TOP of the NT$1,120,000-1,238,000 2020 band, and 1,238,000 / 2,270,000 list = 54.5% retention at 6 years for a low-mileage BASE trim. Applied to real_cost 2,982,000 = ~NT$1,413,000 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: -12% to NT$1,240,000 private sale, a further -13% to NT$1,080,000 dealer trade-in. CROSS-TRIM CHECKS: NT$1,240,000 now exceeds the cheaper 頂級版's NT$1,160,000 in absolute NT$ as the price ladder requires, while the retention ratio 41.6% stays BELOW 頂級版's 47.9% per the trim rule, and it stays below the equally-priced F Sport's NT$1,250,000 because F Sport carries genuine used-market scarcity demand that the comfort-oriented 旗艦版 does not. Explicit cross-generation extrapolation.

Proxy is the 4th-gen RX200t at 2016MY (10 years old today), 旗艦版 launch list NT$2,590,000 — re-fetched and CONFIRMED directly this pass on 7Car, which states 售價259萬 for the 旗艦版 test car and that RX200t came in 豪華/頂級/旗艦 three grades (https://www.7car.tw/articles/read/26825); WeWanted corroborates (https://www.wewanted.com.tw/car_exhibition.php?id=1322). WHY A PREMIUM APPLIES HERE: that band is mileage-blind and at ten years old the typical Taiwanese RX shows 150,000-200,000 km, versus this owner's 70,000 km — the widest mileage gap of any checkpoint. The 2020 low-mileage observation above establishes that low-mileage cars price at or above their year-band top, so the band top is a floor, not a ceiling. RETENTION RATIO derived: band top 858,000 lifted ~10% for the mileage advantage = ~NT$940,000, and 940,000 / 2,590,000 = 36.3% of the proxy's own list (the flagship trim penalty is already embedded because the proxy is itself a flagship). The share of the NT$561,000 new-price gap over 頂級版 that is recovered at resale now declines monotonically across the tail (year 5 19.6%, year 7 15.0%, year 10 14.3%), which is the expected shape. Extrapolated across generations AND across engines (2.0T predecessor vs 2.4T subject), hence low confidence.

maintenance.plan_notes:
Lexus Taiwan does NOT offer a free scheduled-maintenance programme — RE-VERIFIED by direct fetch on 2026-08-11. The only genuinely free item is the 新車保養服務 one-month / 24-item first inspection; every later visit is paid, with a 25項尊榮安檢 included in the visit price (https://www.lexus.com.tw/service/maintenance-plan.aspx). Official intervals re-confirmed as 1個月 / 6個月·10,000km(16項) / 12個月·20,000km(29項) / 24個月·40,000km(34項) / 48個月·80,000km(37項). What Lexus TW does run is the 新車準時保養愛車享延長保證方案 (vehicles delivered from 2024-01-01): complete 8 CONSECUTIVE on-time 6-month services using 原廠機油及定保套餐 and you receive a free extended warranty of 1 year / 20,000 km on top of the standard 4-year / 120,000 km new-car warranty; miss one visit and the extension must be bought from ~NT$25,900 (https://www.lexus.com.tw/news_detail.aspx?nw=563&fn=1, https://www.lexus.com.tw/owners-warranty.aspx). At 7,000 km/year the 10,000 km trigger is never binding: the schedule is purely time-driven, so the owner pays for 2 visits/year for ten years. period_cost is the spend SINCE the previous checkpoint, not cumulative.

THE 10-YEAR TOTAL HAS BEEN REBUILT AND FALLS FROM NT$379,000 TO NT$334,000. The reviewer was right that the old figure sat ~NT$48,000 above the two other RX350 gasoline trims with no stated justification, and re-sourcing the spec sheet shows the justification the previous draft implied does not exist. THE TIRE-SIZE ARGUMENT IS DEAD: the previous draft priced a big tire premium on the belief that 21-inch rims distinguish this trim, contrasting it with 豪華版's 235/60R19. Re-fetching the KingAutos 2026 spec table (https://www.kingautos.net/hot/lexus/rx) shows 頂級版, 旗艦版 and F Sport ALL run 21吋 / 235/50R21 — only the entry 豪華版 sits on 19吋 / 235/60R19. Identical tire, so no tire-driven cost gap over 頂級版 is defensible. The same table shows 前後碟煞 across every trim with no brake differentiation, confirming the reviewer's point that 旗艦版 carries no bigger-brake justification either.

TIRE PRICE ALSO CORRECTED DOWN, from NT$52,000 + 2,500 alignment to NT$44,000 + 3,000. The previous draft's NT$52,000 was an unfetched market guess. The PTT receipt thread was re-fetched this pass and its tire line is Yokohama AE61 in 225/60/18 at NT$6,800 each after discount, with outside shops quoting NT$18,000-20,000 per SET (https://www.ptt.cc/bbs/car/M.1725460760.A.02F.html) — an 18-inch tire, correctly rejected as a direct proxy, but it anchors the scale from which a 21-inch premium SUV tire is estimated at NT$10,000-11,000 each fitted. That lands a set at ~NT$44,000, which is also what the sibling F Sport record carries for the identical 235/50R21; the two now agree rather than differing by NT$8,000 for the same part.

THE ONE REAL DELTA OVER 頂級版 IS THE DRIVELINE, AND IT IS SMALL. The KingAutos table lists 頂級版 as FWD and 旗艦版 as AWD (the used listings agree — 8891's 2024 旗艦版 is badged 4WD, abc's 2023 旗艦版 is badged AWD). AWD adds rear-differential and transfer-case oil to the fluid schedule, budgeted at NT$3,500 in the 3-5y window and NT$4,000 in the 5-7y window, with a further share inside the 7-10y fluid line. That is worth roughly NT$3,000-6,000 net over ten years and is the entire remaining gap: the rebuilt total of NT$334,000 sits NT$3,000 above 頂級版's NT$331,000 and NT$3,500 above F Sport's NT$330,500, versus NT$48,000 before. Everything else — 2.4L turbo engine, 8AT, service cadence, brakes, tires — is common to all three.

TIRE TIMING is unchanged and matches the 頂級版 record: at 7,000 km/year the original set has only ~35,000 km at year 5 with tread to spare, so a low-mileage owner replaces on AGE at about year 6, inside the 5-7 window. The second set then falls due around year 11-12, outside this horizon, so no second set is budgeted at year 10 and that window carries age-driven repair instead. Note this diverges from the sibling F Sport record, which places sets at years 5 and 10 and therefore books two; for identical tires at identical mileage both cannot be right, and the year-6 single-set reading is used here because it matches 頂級版 and is the more honest low-mileage physics. Per-visit rates follow the same minor (~NT$5,500) / major (~NT$8,000-11,000) alternation as the sibling records. No Lexus TW per-service price list is published, so every money figure is modelled from owner receipts and dealer norms; confidence is capped accordingly.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, well under the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). This matters twice. (1) Resale: the live 8891 comparables for this generation carry 31,000-42,000 km at 2-3 years and the predecessor-generation cars at 5-10 years carry 100,000-184,000 km, i.e. roughly double this car's mileage at the same age, so the mileage-blind market average understates what this car is worth. A low-km premium is applied and stated per checkpoint. At the 10-year point that premium is now built into the anchor rather than applied on top: a 2016 RX 2.0 at 76,792 km was found live on SUM today, which is within 10% of this car's 70,000 km at year 10, so no separate premium is layered on. NOTE: an earlier draft of this record misread 8891 mileages written in 萬 units (3.99萬 km read as 3,990 km instead of 39,900 km) and therefore believed its comparables were already ultra-low-mileage; the comparables are in fact normal-mileage cars, which is what justifies the premium. (2) Maintenance: at 7,000 km/year the car never reaches a mileage-triggered service, so servicing is purely TIME-driven — but the Lexus Taiwan official schedule is 6 months / 10,000 km, not 1 year. An earlier draft claimed an annual manual interval on the authority of a PTT thread and dismissed the 6-month visit as a dealer upsell; the official Lexus TW maintenance-plan page it cited lists 1 month, then 6 months/10,000 km, 12 months/20,000 km, 24 months/40,000 km, 48 months/80,000 km. At 7,000 km/year the 6-month TIME trigger fires twice a year, so two visits per year are costed: one main service plus one lighter half-year service. Consumables are age-driven as much as wear-driven, but the 235/50R21 set is now placed ONCE at ~year 6 (42,000 km, where tread is genuinely near its limit AND the rubber is 6 years old) rather than twice at years 5 and 10 — the second set then falls at ~year 12, outside this horizon. Tax and insurance are excluded by design.

value_checkpoints.source: REBUILT — an earlier draft's anchor was a misattributed listing. It claimed 'a 2025 RX350 at 1,900 km listed at NT$2,480,000'. Re-fetching https://auto.8891.com.tw/lexus/RX350 today shows no 2025 RX350 at all; the listing it describes is a 2024 RX500h F Sport Performance at 1.9萬 km (19,000 km) asking NT$2,688,000 — a different model with a NT$3,610,000 list price. That anchor is discarded. Rebuilt instead by interpolating above the one verified same-trim point, re-confirmed live today: 2024 RX350 F Sport, 3.99萬 km (39,900 km), NT$2,198,000 車商售價 = 74.5% of list at 2 years. Taiwan luxury-SUV dealer retail at 1 year runs ~83-85% of list mileage-blind; this car's 7,000 km against a typical ~15,000 km 1-year-old adds ~2 points, giving dealer retail ~NT$2,470,000 (83.7% of list). ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 2,470,000 less 9% = 2,250,000 private sale (tight spread — a 1-year-old in-warranty Lexus is fast-moving inventory), then a further 10% = 2,025,000 dealer trade-in. Not a raw dealer asking price. Confidence stays low because no 1-year-old RX350 is actually observable on the board today; this point is interpolated, not seen.

Genuine current-generation data, re-fetched and mileage-corrected today from https://auto.8891.com.tw/lexus/RX350: 2024 RX350 F Sport, 3.99萬 km = 39,900 km, NT$2,198,000 車商售價 (2 years old, 74.5% of list); 2024 RX350 旗艦版, 3.12萬 km = 31,200 km, NT$2,198,000; 2023 RX350 頂級版, 4.2萬 km = 42,000 km, NT$1,898,000 (3 years old, 70.8% of that trim's NT$2,680,000 list). All three re-confirmed live on today's re-check. The 2024 F Sport point is independently corroborated by an abc好車網 dealer listing at the identical NT$2,198,000 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2260595). IMPORTANT CORRECTION carried forward: an earlier draft read these mileages as 3,990 / 3,120 / 4,200 km — a 10x error from misreading 萬 — and so wrongly treated them as ultra-low-mileage cars. They are normal-mileage cars at 31,000-42,000 km, which is what makes a genuine low-km premium available to this 21,000 km car. Mileage-blind 3-year F Sport dealer retail set at 68.5% of list (just below the 頂級版's observed 70.8%, per the trim-ladder rule) = 2,020,000; low-km premium of +6% for 21,000 km against the ~42,000 km observed comparables gives NT$2,150,000 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: 2,150,000 less 11% = 1,915,000 private sale; less a further 12% = 1,685,000 dealer trade-in.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation — the 5th-gen RX only launched in Taiwan in November 2022, so no genuine 5-year-old example of this car exists. Method: took the 4th-gen RX F Sport (list NT$2,610,000 per U-CAR; see caveat) and found its real 5-year-old trade on SUM 汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch.php?v=3&brand=LEXUS&model=RX): a 2021 RX300 F-Sport at 27,277 km asking NT$1,599,000, i.e. a 61.3% retention ratio at 5 years on a comparably low-mileage car. Shaded down to ~58% to reflect (a) faster percentage decay on a more expensive car and (b) the trim-ladder effect, giving NT$1,715,000 dealer-retail-equivalent for this car. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: less 11% = 1,525,000 private sale; less a further 12% = 1,340,000 dealer trade-in. Ratio applied to this car's real_cost basis. RE-CHECK 2026-08-11: today's SUM fetch returned a partial slice of the 63 listings that did not include the 27,277 km car, so that specific anchor could not be re-confirmed this pass. What today's slice DID show for 5-year-old F Sport variants corroborates the level rather than contradicting it: 2021 RX F-Sport, 106,856 km, NT$1,530,000 (村信汽車, 高雄) and 2021 RX F-Sport, 123,000 km, NT$1,398,000 (賜海汽車, 台中). The NT$1,715,000 dealer-retail-equivalent used here is +12% over the 106,856 km car, which is a reasonable low-mileage premium for a 35,000 km car against a 107,000 km one. The point is left unchanged. CAVEAT: the NT$2,610,000 predecessor list price could not be re-verified — U-CAR (https://news.u-car.com.tw/news/article/32062) returned HTTP 403 again today, so the denominator of this ratio rests on an unconfirmed secondary figure. Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation; no genuine 7-year-old 5th-gen RX exists. Predecessor evidence VERIFIED LIVE today on 8891 中古車 RX300 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/lexus/rx300): 2019 RX300 F Sport 2.0L, 11.9萬 km = 119,000 km, NT$1,088,000 = 41.7% of its NT$2,610,000 list at 7 years. That car carries 119,000 km against this buyer's 49,000 km at 7 years, so a +22% low-mileage premium is applied multiplicatively to the 41.7% observation, giving ~50.9% for a low-km 7-year F Sport, then shaded to ~48% for this pricier top trim = NT$1,420,000 dealer-retail-equivalent. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: less 12% = 1,250,000 private sale; less a further 13% = 1,085,000 dealer trade-in. Wider spreads than at year 1 because older cars carry more condition risk and sell slower. CAVEAT CORRECTED THIS PASS: a previous draft said the supporting points (2020 RX300 F Sport 101,000 km NT$1,328,000; 2020 RX300 豪華版 22,000 km NT$1,238,000; 2022 RX300 F Sport 123,000 km NT$1,398,000) were not on the board and could not be confirmed. They ARE on the board today — all three re-fetched live from the same 8891 RX300 page — so that caveat was wrong and is withdrawn. They now do real work in the year-10 derivation below. Confidence stays low because the NT$2,610,000 denominator is still unverified (U-CAR 403). Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

RE-SOURCED TODAY in response to the cross-trim review, which flagged the prior NT$1,090,000 (37% of real_cost) as a flattening tail — only a 5-point retention drop from year 7 against 8-12 points for every other RX trim — and as a ladder inversion above the base 頂級版. BOTH OBJECTIONS ARE ACCEPTED; the prior 42.5%-of-list derivation is discarded, and NO F Sport scarcity argument is claimed. NEW EVIDENCE, all fetched live today. (1) Genuine 10-year-old cars ARE observable, which the prior draft did not use: SUM 汽車網 (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch.php?v=3&brand=LEXUS&model=RX) lists a 2016 RX 2.0L at 76,792 km asking NT$838,000 (上藝汽車, 新北) and a 2016 RX 2.0L at 136,914 km asking NT$798,000 (冠立汽車, 台南); 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/lexus/rx200t) lists a 2016 RX200t 頂級版 at 183,800 km asking NT$699,000 (杰運高雄). The 76,792 km car is the best-matched 10-year comparable in the whole dataset — this buyer reaches year 10 at 70,000 km — so the low-mileage premium is INSIDE the anchor and is deliberately not applied a second time (the prior draft's incoherent '+18% on a 42.7% average' step is gone). Those three cars also measure the low-mileage premium directly: 838,000 vs 699,000 = +19.9% for 76,792 km against 183,800 km. (2) DECAY FACTOR MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Matched-mileage pair: 2016 RX 2.0 at 136,914 km NT$798,000 against the 2019 RX300 F Sport at 119,000 km NT$1,088,000 = 73.3% over three years. Low-mileage pair: the 2016 car at 76,792 km NT$838,000 against the 2020 RX300 豪華版 at 22,000 km NT$1,238,000 (8891) = 67.7% over four years, i.e. 90.9%/year, i.e. 75.1% over three years. The two agree closely; 75.1% is used. (3) TRIM-LADDER RULE CONFIRMED, NOT EXEMPTED. At 6 years the 2020 RX300 F Sport (101,000 km, NT$1,328,000) is 50.9% of its NT$2,610,000 list while the 2020 RX300 豪華版 (22,000 km, NT$1,238,000) is 56.5% of its NT$2,190,000 list — the cheaper trim retains the higher ratio even while carrying a fifth of the mileage. There is no observable F Sport scarcity premium in ratio terms, so none is written in. DERIVATION: year-7 dealer-retail-equivalent NT$1,420,000 x 75.1% = NT$1,066,000, rounded to NT$1,065,000 dealer-retail-equivalent at year 10. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: less 13% = NT$930,000 private sale (this is the private figure, not a dealer asking price); less a further 14% = NT$800,000 dealer trade-in. Widest spreads of any checkpoint — 10-year cars sit on dealer lots longest. RESULT AND CHECKS: 31.5% of real_cost, a 10.8-point fall from the year-7 42.3%, inside the 8-12 point band the rest of the line shows, and below the base 頂級版's ~35.5% so the ladder inversion is resolved. It sits ~2.7 points above the 旗艦版 at the same NT$2,950,000 list; the stated reason is that F Sport is the only RX350 gasoline trim with AWD (verified today on https://cars.tvbs.com.tw/spec/lexus/2026-lexus-rx — 豪華版/頂級版/旗艦版 are all FWD), and an AWD RX is the more sought-after used car in Taiwan, which is the same reason this record already sits above 旗艦版 at year 7. CAVEAT: the 4th-gen list prices remain the unverified link — U-CAR (https://news.u-car.com.tw/news/article/27742 and /32062) returned HTTP 403 again today. That only affects the ratio cross-check, not the main derivation, which now runs on observed price-to-price decay rather than on a list-price denominator. Still extrapolated across generations and no 10-year-old RX F Sport exists in any generation (the 4th-gen F Sport arrived for 2017, so the oldest is 9 years), hence low confidence.

maintenance.plan_notes: REBUILT THIS PASS. The review objected that NT$330,500 was LOWER than the base 頂級版's NT$331,000 and that the NT$500 gap read as invented rather than sourced. Both points are accepted and the schedule has been re-derived item by item; the total is now NT$378,000, about NT$47,000 (+14%) ABOVE the 頂級版, and every window's items sum exactly to its period_cost. ONE PREMISE OF THE OBJECTION IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE: the F Sport does NOT run bigger wheels than the 頂級版. Both the TVBS 2026 RX spec table (https://cars.tvbs.com.tw/spec/lexus/2026-lexus-rx) and the KingAutos 2026 RX page (https://www.kingautos.net/hot/lexus/rx), fetched today, show 頂級版, 旗艦版 and F Sport all on 235/50R21 on 21-inch rims; only 豪華版 differs, on 235/60R19. So the tyre-size premium the reviewer expected does not exist against the 頂級版, and inventing one would have been the wrong fix. WHAT ACTUALLY MAKES THIS TRIM DEARER TO RUN IS AWD. The same TVBS table shows F Sport is the ONLY RX350 gasoline trim with all-wheel drive — 豪華版, 頂級版 and 旗艦版 are front-wheel drive. That adds, against the FWD 頂級版: (a) rear differential oil plus transfer-case (PTU) oil, serviced twice across ten years, ~NT$16,000; (b) higher kerb weight on the brakes, ~NT$4,000 across pads and discs; (c) a performance-compound tyre and the fact that an AWD car must have all four tyres replaced together and circumference-matched, so the pair-change escape hatch is unavailable, ~NT$2,000; (d) a larger ageing-parts allowance in the 7-10 year window because the propshaft, PTU and rear diff are extra failure surface a FWD RX simply does not have, ~NT$12,000; plus an explicitly booked NT$12,000 out-of-warranty repair allowance in the 5-7 year window. Items (a)-(c) are the genuinely trim-driven NT$22,000; the rest is risk allowance and is labelled as such. TYRE SCHEDULE, RE-DERIVED FROM A REAL QUOTE: one set, not two. At 7,000 km/year the 235/50R21 set reaches ~42,000 km at year 6, which is where tread is genuinely near its limit AND the rubber is six years old — replacing at year 5 / 35,000 km (the prior draft) is early on both counts, and it was what produced the previous record's broken cost curve (a NT$84,000 year-5 window followed by a cheaper NT$49,500 year-7 window). Moved to year 6, the second set falls at ~year 12, outside this horizon, so the 7-10 year window carries no tyres. PRICE: a real Taiwan retail quote was found today — DUNLOP SPORT MAXX LUX 235/50/21, four tyres fitted, NT$31,968 at 車麗屋 via PChome 24h (https://24h.pchome.com.tw/search/?q=235%2F50R21). That is the market FLOOR for this size, on a mid-tier pattern from a chain store. The NT$48,000 booked here assumes an OE-grade premium replacement (Michelin / Bridgestone class, roughly NT$10,000-11,000 per corner) plus four-wheel alignment, balancing and TPMS service, which is what an F Sport owner servicing at a Lexus dealer actually pays. Honest range for this line: NT$32,000 (verified, chain store, Dunlop) to NT$52,000 (dealer-fitted OE). SERVICE CADENCE, unchanged and officially sourced: Lexus Taiwan's schedule (https://www.lexus.com.tw/service/maintenance-plan.aspx) is 1 month, then 6 months / 10,000 km, 12 months / 20,000 km, 24 months / 40,000 km, 48 months / 80,000 km. At 7,000 km/year the mileage trigger never fires, so servicing is purely TIME-driven at a 6-MONTH interval — two dealer visits every year, twenty over ten years, alternating a light visit (~NT$5,500 rising with inflation) and a major visit (~NT$10,000-11,000). FREE MAINTENANCE: Lexus Taiwan does NOT offer one. The only complimentary item is the 1-month / 24-item new-car inspection. The official programmes that DO exist and are reflected here: (1) the new-car warranty of 4 years / 120,000 km (https://www.lexus.com.tw/owners-warranty.aspx), which is why the 0-1y and 1-3y windows carry no repair contingency; (2) 「新車準時保養愛車享延長保證方案」 (https://www.lexus.com.tw/news_detail.aspx?nw=563&fn=1) — 8 consecutive on-time scheduled services on genuine oil and the official 定保套餐 earn a free warranty extension of 1 year / 20,000 km for cars delivered from 2024-01-01, so a compliant owner is covered to roughly year 5 (the 8-service requirement is itself consistent with a 6-month cadence over 4 years, not an annual one); (3) Lexus Elite Rewards and Hotai Points maintenance rebates (~1.5%), which are discounts rather than free work and are NOT monetised here. Owner-reported price points used as the labour/parts base: essential main service NT$4,000-5,000, light half-year service NT$2,600, a 70,000 km required service NT$3,800, a 20,000 km-class major service around NT$14,000 (https://disp.cc/b/Car/fJfl). Gasoline model, so there is no hybrid or high-voltage inspection cost anywhere in this plan. The curve now rises monotonically across all five windows (13,000 / 34,000 / 58,000 / 122,000 / 151,000); the previous non-monotonic dip at year 7 is gone because it was an artefact of the wrong tyre timing, not a real consumable cycle. Rim refinishing for the F Sport's dark 21-inch alloys is booked once, in selling_costs, and is not double-counted here. period_cost is the spend SINCE the previous checkpoint, not cumulative.

That claim is contradicted by the official Lexus TW maintenance-plan table and is not adopted; a forum post does not outrank the manufacturer's published schedule.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use the 7,000 km/year midpoint, so assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Two consequences run through the whole record. (1) Servicing is time-driven, not mileage-driven: Lexus TW's official schedule is 6個月/10,000km, 12個月/20,000km, 24個月/40,000km, 48個月/80,000km, whichever comes FIRST — at 7,000 km/year the time trigger always fires first, so the owner pays for 2 visits/year and never reaches a km trigger (only 70,000 km at year 10, i.e. the 80,000 km major is never mileage-triggered). Big-ticket consumables are therefore on an AGE clock: 235/50R21 tires time out long before they wear out, and the 12V battery dies of age. (2) Resale is quoted from low-mileage listings, which sit above the mileage-blind average, with the premium scaled by age — negligible at year 1, largest at year 10 where 70,000 km is under half of a typical 150,000 km 10-year-old car. Tax and insurance are excluded by design and appear nowhere in this record. TRIM CONTEXT (added on adversarial review): 頂級版 is NOT the top of the RX350h range — the 2026 ladder is 豪華版 256萬 < 頂級版 278萬 < 旗艦版 305萬 (TVBS spec table). Retention ratios in this record are therefore constrained to sit BELOW the 豪華版 base trim and ABOVE the 旗艦版, per the Taiwan trim-ladder rule that equipment grade is largely lost at resale.

purchase.source: List price INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED on adversarial review against two sources fetched directly: 8891 新車 2026年式 price table (https://c.8891.com.tw/news/lexus/rx/20732) returns the full 10-trim table with RX350h 頂級版 = 278萬 and states 售價維持不變 for the 2026 model year; 地球黃金線/TVBS 2026 RX spec table (https://cars.tvbs.com.tw/spec/lexus/2026-lexus-rx) independently returns the same 278萬, plus 2487cc and 235/50R21. Both also return the surrounding ladder (350 豪華版 246萬, 350h 豪華版 256萬, 350 頂級版 268萬, 350h 旗艦版 305萬), and Lexus TW's showroom range 246~361萬 (https://www.lexus.com.tw/showroom/RX) brackets it exactly. VERDICT: 2,780,000 is CORRECT, no change — the scout's and the researcher's figure both stand. Discount RAISED from the researcher's 200,000 to 260,000 on cross-record consistency grounds (see notes). onroad_fees raised 35,000 -> 40,000 so they scale with price.
purchase.notes:
TWO CORRECTIONS APPLIED HERE ON ADVERSARIAL REVIEW; the list price itself was confirmed correct and left alone.

(1) DISCOUNT 200,000 -> 260,000. The brief's 'Lexus discounts little' heuristic does not survive contact with real 菜單, and the researcher was right to depart from it — but the figure chosen was internally inconsistent with the rest of the batch. The same-model, same-powertrain BASE trim record (lexus-rx350h-luxury, RX350h 豪華版) uses a 260,000 discount off a 256萬 list = 10.2%, itself backed by a fetched 菜單 showing 30萬 off. The researcher put the DEARER 頂級版 at 200,000 off 278萬 = 7.2%. That is backwards: the same Hotai/Lexus dealer network does not give a smaller cash discount on the more expensive trim of the same car. The researcher's OWN sourced evidence for this exact trim supports the higher figure — PTT 菜單 at 折19萬 (https://www.ptt.cc/bbs/car/M.1733189425.A.493.html), 折28萬 (https://www.pttweb.cc/bbs/car/M.1760544279.A.1DD, the most recent sheet), 折15萬, and a 248萬 cash deal (https://www.ptt.cc/bbs/car/M.1750670118.A.D01.html). Observed range 150,000-280,000. 260,000 matches the sibling record's absolute discount, sits inside the verified range, and is below the most aggressive sheet. This removes the cross-record incomparability the researcher flagged as their own #1 open question.

(2) ONROAD_FEES 35,000 -> 40,000. The brief says onroad_fees scale with price (~20,000-40,000 at this level). The researcher used 35,000 — identical to the cheaper RX350 豪華版 (246萬) sibling and below the RX350h 豪華版 (256萬) sibling's 45,000. A 278萬 car cannot carry lower 領牌+代辦+配件 than a 246萬 one. Set to 40,000: the top of the brief's stated band, above both cheaper siblings, and short of the 45,000 the 豪華版 record used (which is outside the brief's band). Covers 領牌 + 代辦 + the gifted-tier 配件 (行車紀錄器/腳踏墊/E-Tag); the 隔熱紙+鍍膜 package the 菜單 price at 38,000-47,000 is treated as owner discretionary and excluded.

Tax and insurance excluded by design — the 4.8萬 乙式 insurance quoted in the PTT sheet is deliberately NOT included. real_cost = 2,780,000 - 260,000 + 40,000 = 2,560,000.

selling_costs.notes: UNCHANGED on review — this was one of the cleaner parts of the record. Private-sale scenario, consistent with private_sale_price being the headline resale figure. 過戶 at a 監理站 is a low fixed cost; the real spend is pre-sale detailing, which matters more on a 250萬+ luxury SUV where buyers inspect closely. Platform listing fees on 8891/abc好車網 in this price band run 2,000-3,000. Total 10,000 sits mid-band against the brief's 5,000-12,000, and is the only figure in the batch's RX records that is comfortably inside that band (the 豪華版 siblings used 11,500 and 14,000, the latter out of band). If the owner trades in to a dealer instead, most of this disappears — but so does the private-vs-tradein gap, which is far larger (roughly 250,000 at year 1, 120,000 at year 10).

value_checkpoints.source: CORRECTED DOWN on adversarial review (was 2,100,000) to satisfy the trim-ladder rule. Real anchor, fetched and confirmed: 2025 RX 350 旗艦版 asking 248萬 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2294103) against a 295萬 list = 84.1% DEALER RETAIL at ~1 year; 2024 RX 350h 旗艦版 asks 238萬 and 259.8萬 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2284829, https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2209780). Those are 旗艦版 asks and a dealer ASK sits above transaction, so I set this trim's 1-year dealer retail asking at ~225萬 = 81.0% of the 278萬 list rather than borrowing 84% wholesale. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED (the dealer-retail trap): retail asking 2,250,000 -> private sale 2,000,000 is an 11.1% haircut, because dealer retail carries the dealer's margin, warranty/整備 cost and negotiating room that a private seller cannot charge for; private 2,000,000 -> dealer trade-in 1,750,000 is a further 12.5%. Both inside the brief's 8-15% and 10-15% bands. TRIM-LADDER CHECK: 2,000,000 / 2,780,000 = 71.9%, which sits 1.1 points BELOW the RX350h 豪華版 sibling's 73.0% while the absolute price stays 130,000 ABOVE it (1,870,000) — the correct shape. Small low-mileage premium only; at 1 year 7,000 km barely differentiates. Confidence medium: no 1-year 350h 頂級版 listing exists, the ratio is borrowed across trims.

CORRECTED DOWN (was 1,860,000) and confidence DOWNGRADED from high to medium. Best-evidenced checkpoint: four real dealer RETAIL asks for this exact trim and generation (2023年式 RX350h 頂級版, 5th gen, now ~3.3 years old) — 189.8萬 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2276730), 208.8萬 at 5,000 km (8891 中古車, https://auto.8891.com.tw/lexus/rx), 213.8萬 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2206330), and 218萬 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2183772 — I fetched this one directly and confirmed it is a 2023 Lexus RX 350h 頂級版 asking NT$2,180,000). Per the brief I lean to the low-mileage end (the buyer is at 21,000 km), but I set the retail basis at ~203萬 rather than the researcher's 210萬 for three reasons: the four asks span 189.8-218萬 (a 15% spread), the 2023 list was 282萬 versus 278萬 today so the ratio must be rebased down ~1.4% (https://c.8891.com.tw/m/article/tag/Lexus-RX-2023%E5%83%B9%E6%A0%BC), and an ASK is not a transaction. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: retail 2,030,000 -> private sale 1,780,000 is a 12.3% haircut; private -> dealer trade-in 1,560,000 is a further 12.4%. TRIM-LADDER CHECK: 64.0% of list, 1.2 points below the 豪華版 sibling's 65.2%, absolute 110,000 above it. Car is still inside the reported 4-year factory warranty here, which is why the ratio is this strong. Confidence medium not high: every input is a dealer ASK, the spread is 15%, and the private figure is a derived haircut rather than an observed private transaction — 'high' was not earned.

CORRECTED UP on review (was 1,450,000). EXTRAPOLATED, not observed — the 5th-gen RX launched in Taiwan in late 2022/Jan 2023, so the oldest car is ~3.5 years old and NO genuine 5-year data for this generation exists. Method per the brief: take the PREDECESSOR generation (4th-gen RX450h) at the matching age, express it as a retention ratio of ITS original list, apply that ratio here. Predecessor anchor: 2022 RX450h 頂級版 asking 199.8萬 as a LEXUS CPO car (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2146839) against its 314萬 list (https://c.8891.com.tw/article/tag/Lexus-rx450h-%E5%83%B9%E6%A0%BC) = 63.6% dealer retail at ~4 years; CPO carries roughly a 10% premium over ordinary trade, giving ~57-58% at 4 years and ~54% rolled forward to 5. Adding back a low-mileage premium (35,000 km versus a typical 60,000-75,000 km 5-year-old) gives a dealer RETAIL asking price of ~170萬 = 61.2% of the 278萬 list. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: retail 1,700,000 -> private sale 1,500,000 is an 11.8% haircut; private -> trade-in 1,310,000 is a further 12.7%. WHY RAISED: the researcher's 1,450,000 was 52.2% of list, i.e. 3.3 points BELOW the 豪華版 sibling's 55.5%. The trim rule says the higher trim retains SLIGHTLY less, not dramatically less; a 3.3-point penalty overstates it and broke the smoothness of the curve. 54.0% is 1.5 points below the base trim, which is the right magnitude. The visible step down from year 3 (64.0%) is real: the reported 4-year factory warranty has expired by year 5, a genuine cliff in the Taiwanese used-luxury market. Confidence low — extrapolated off a different (3.5L V6) hybrid whose residuals were additionally depressed by being replaced in 2022.

Adjusted slightly down (was 1,230,000). EXTRAPOLATED — no 7-year data for the current 5th-gen RX can exist. Predecessor anchors at exactly this age (2019年式 4th-gen RX450h, now ~7 years old): 頂級版 asking 189.8萬 as a LEXUS CPO car — I fetched https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/2036666 directly and confirmed it is a 2019 Lexus RX450h 頂級版 at NT$1,898,000, LEXUS CPO/民族營業所 — against its 308萬 facelift list = 61.6% retail; and 旗艦版 asking 158.8萬 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/car/1804314) against its 338萬 list = 47.0% retail. Trim list prices from the 2019 小改款 RX price table (https://2gamesome.com.tw/article/view/374). Stripping the ~10% CPO premium off the 頂級版 gives ~55% ordinary trade; the 旗艦版 gives 47%. NOTE this pair is itself a clean instance of the trim rule — the dearer 旗艦版 retains a clearly LOWER ratio, which is the same direction the correction to this record applies. Taking ~50% as the ordinary-trade 7-year ratio and adding a low-mileage premium for 49,000 km (versus a typical 90,000-105,000 km 7-year-old) gives a dealer RETAIL asking price of ~138萬 = 49.6% of list. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: retail 1,380,000 -> private sale 1,210,000 is a 12.3% haircut; private -> trade-in 1,050,000 is a further 13.2%. TRIM-LADDER CHECK: 43.5% of list versus the 豪華版 sibling's 44.9% — 1.4 points below, absolute 60,000 above. Confidence low: extrapolated, and the two predecessor data points disagree by 14 percentage points.

CORRECTED DOWN on review (was 960,000) — this was the clearest trim-ladder violation in the record. EXTRAPOLATED; no 10-year data for the 5th-gen RX can exist. Predecessor anchors at exactly this age (2016年式 4th-gen RX450h, now ~10 years old): 頂級版 asking 128.8萬 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/1900355) and 旗艦版 asking 118.8萬 (https://www.abccar.com.tw/Car/1826919). Measured against the 2019 facelift list prices as the closest published reference (308萬 頂級版 / 338萬 旗艦版, https://2gamesome.com.tw/article/view/374; the 2016 pre-facelift list was somewhat lower, making these ratios slightly conservative), that is roughly 42% and 35% dealer retail — again the dearer trim retaining less. Taking ~36% as the ordinary-trade 10-year ratio and adding the LARGEST low-mileage premium of any checkpoint (70,000 km is under half the ~150,000 km a typical 10-year-old Taiwanese SUV carries, and at this age mileage dominates price) gives a dealer RETAIL asking price of ~101.5萬 = 36.5% of list. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: retail 1,015,000 -> private sale 885,000 is a 12.8% haircut; private -> trade-in 765,000 is a further 13.6%. WHY LOWERED: the researcher's 960,000 was 34.5% of list against the 豪華版 sibling's 33.0% — the top trim retaining MORE, exactly the inversion the brief warns about, and at the age where equipment grade is worth least. 31.8% is 1.2 points below the base trim while the absolute stays 40,000 above it (845,000). Confidence low: extrapolated off a different hybrid powertrain, and the 2016 list is inferred from the 2019 facelift table. Residual risk not priced in: a 10-year-old hybrid carries traction-battery anxiety that can depress the private figure further even when the pack is healthy.

maintenance.plan_notes:
THE BRIEF'S PREMISE IS WRONG AND THE RESEARCHER WAS RIGHT TO SAY SO — retained on review. Lexus Taiwan does NOT run a free scheduled-maintenance programme in the German-brand sense. Every 定期保養 below is owner-paid. The programme that exists is 「新車準時保養愛車享延長保證方案」: complete 8 consecutive on-time 定保 using the 定保套餐 from delivery and the car earns a FREE EXTENDED WARRANTY. On the 6-month interval this owner hits 8 visits at exactly year 4, so it is achievable on this driving profile — but it buys warranty, not free servicing, so it cuts later-period REPAIR risk rather than the maintenance line. Not modelled as a cost saving because its exact term was not verifiable on an official Lexus TW page.

Official schedule (https://www.lexus.com.tw/service/maintenance-plan.aspx): 新車/1個月 free 24-point check; then 6個月/10,000km (16 checks), 12個月/20,000km (29), 24個月/40,000km (34), 48個月/80,000km (37) — whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/year the TIME trigger always fires first, so this owner pays for 2 visits every year for 10 years (20 paid visits) and never once reaches a mileage trigger. Hybrid-specific items (動力控制冷卻系統洩漏檢查, Hybrid 動力控制冷卻液面) fall at the 24- and 48-month services and are included in the visit costs.

THE 21-INCH TIRE PREMIUM IS THE DEFINING COST DIFFERENCE OF THIS TRIM. Verified directly on the TVBS 2026 RX spec table (https://cars.tvbs.com.tw/spec/lexus/2026-lexus-rx): 頂級版 runs 235/50R21, 豪華版 runs 235/60R19. That single spec is why this record's 10-year maintenance total (350,000) runs ~23% above the RX350h 豪華版 sibling's (285,000) — roughly 48,000-50,000 per set here versus 32,000-34,000 there, twice over. It is the honest reason the higher trim costs more to keep, and it is why a low-mileage owner does NOT get a cheap ownership experience: the tires are binned on age with most of their tread intact.

RESTRUCTURED ON ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. The researcher put the first tire set at year 5 and produced a non-monotonic curve (year 5 = 92,000 then year 7 = 55,000). Two fixes: (a) the first set now falls in the 5-7 window, i.e. replacement at ~5.5-6 years of age, matching both the real ageing window for premium rubber and the same-model 豪華版 sibling's treatment; (b) the year-10 window no longer double-counts — the researcher stacked a 25,000 suspension/bushing line, a 15,000 hybrid-peripheral line AND a separate 20,000 general out-of-warranty reserve, where the suspension work is exactly what such a reserve is for. Folded into a single 25,000 reserve. Result is a strictly rising curve: 12,000 / 30,000 / 48,000 / 105,000 / 155,000.

Per-visit costs are owner-reported Taiwanese figures, not a published price list: a minor 半年定保 runs roughly 4,000-5,000 and an annual/major 定保 roughly 8,000-10,600 (a PTT owner reports ~10,6xx total with ~4,0xx mandatory and the rest dealer-recommended). Modelled at the mandatory-plus-some-extras middle, not the maximum upsell. Because the money is forum-sourced while only the interval structure is official, no maintenance checkpoint is rated above medium.

Warranty assumption affecting years 5, 7 and 10: the Lexus TW new-car warranty is commonly reported as 4 years / 120,000 km, which could NOT be confirmed on an official Lexus TW page — treat as unverified. It sets where out-of-warranty repair allowances start.

EXCLUDED: traction-battery replacement. At 70,000 km by year 10 the pack is very unlikely to need replacing and Toyota/Lexus packs in Taiwan routinely pass this point; pricing a replacement that probably will not happen would overstate the model. It remains the single largest tail risk (a pack is a six-figure item).

checkpoints.source: CORRECTED DOWN from the researcher's 92,000. Covers 3-5y: 4 paid visits (~36,000, including the 48-month major at ~18,000 — the biggest scheduled item in the whole Lexus TW table, the only one adding 自排變速箱油/燃油濾清器/引擎冷卻液, and at 7,000 km/year it arrives on the 4-year clock with only 28,000 km covered), plus a first 12V AGM battery at ~7,000 on age, plus a ~5,000 first out-of-warranty allowance. checkpoints.source: CORRECTED UP from the researcher's 55,000 — this is where the first tire set actually lands. Covers 5-7y: 4 paid visits at the owner-reported 4,000-5,000 minor / 8,000-10,600 annual rates gives ~28,000. TIRES are the headline: 235/50R21 confirmed for this trim on the TVBS 2026 RX spec table (https://cars.tvbs.com.tw/spec/lexus/2026-lexus-rx), roughly 11,000-12,000 per corner fitted in Taiwan, ~48,000 for four. At 49,000 km the tread is nowhere near worn — the set is binned on AGE at ~5.5-6 years, which is the single clearest illustration that low mileage does not buy cheap ownership. Added ~15,000 for front pads plus disc skimming (late but due at 49,000 km with regenerative braking, and the first brake spend in the model), ~5,000 for the e-CVT transaxle fluid, and ~9,000 as an out-of-warranty repair allowance since the reported 4-year warranty lapsed in the previous window. Confidence medium: visit count and tire size are officially grounded, the brake and repair figures are judgement rather than receipts.

checkpoints.source: CORRECTED DOWN from the researcher's 185,000. Covers 7-10y — longest window (3 years, 6 paid visits) and the least certain. Scheduled side ~49,000 including the 96-month repeat of the big service (變速箱油/冷卻液/燃油濾清器 per https://www.lexus.com.tw/service/maintenance-plan.aspx). Age-driven consumables dominate the rest: a SECOND set of 235/50R21 (~50,000) around year 10-11 regardless of mileage, a second 12V battery (~8,000), front and rear discs and pads (~18,000), long-life coolant (~4,000). WHY LOWERED: the researcher stacked a 25,000 suspension/bushing line, a 15,000 hybrid-peripheral line AND a separate 20,000 general out-of-warranty reserve. Suspension bushings, inverter coolant and the electric water pump are precisely what a general reserve on a 10-year-old car is for — carrying them as named line items on top of the reserve double-counts. Folded into one 25,000 reserve, which is still above the 20,000 the 豪華版 sibling uses, correctly reflecting the heavier top-trim hardware. Net total 155,000 versus the sibling's 130,000; the 25,000 gap is almost exactly the 21-inch tire premium, which is the right answer. EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: traction-battery replacement. Confidence low: 7-10 years out, no receipts exist for a 5th-gen RX at this age, and the total could plausibly land anywhere from 120,000 to 230,000 depending on whether any single large failure occurs.
