assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year (midpoint 7,000), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. Every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years. Two consequences drive the record. (1) Maintenance is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Volvo Taiwan's scheduled interval is 1萬公里 or 1年, whichever comes first, so at 7,000 km/year the car returns annually and never reaches the mileage trigger. Age-driven consumables (tyres hardening at 5-6 years, brake fluid every 2 years, 12V AGM battery at 4-5 years, coolant) dominate the bill instead of wear-driven ones. (2) Resale sits ABOVE the mileage-blind average: at 5 years this car has 35,000 km while the 2021 XC90 listings actually on findcar today run 50,005-155,000 km, so each checkpoint is anchored on the LOWEST-mileage listing in its cluster and this is stated in every source string. POWERTRAIN CLASSIFICATION: the B5 is a 48V MILD hybrid (MHEV) — it cannot move on electric power alone. It is recorded as 'hybrid' because that is the closest value in the allowed enum, but it should not be read as a full hybrid; it is a petrol engine with a belt-driven integrated starter-generator. It never needs charging, so there is NO home-charger cost (the T8 PHEV, a different and more expensive trim, would). Excluded by design across the whole record: 牌照稅/燃料稅, insurance, and fuel. Volvo Taiwan's 4年/8萬公里免費定期保養 programme is EV-only and does NOT cover this mild-hybrid B5 — re-verified against the official monthly-offers page, whose current XC90 offer contains no free-maintenance item.

purchase.source: List price INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED by this audit: Yahoo奇摩汽車 2026 XC90 model page returns Plus B5 AWD NT$2,990,000, Ultra B5 AWD NT$3,390,000, Ultra T8 AWD PHEV NT$3,790,000 for the 2026年式 lineup. Cross-checked against KingAutos' XC90 price table (MY2024: B5 Momentum 2,895,000, Plus B5 AWD 2,956,000, Ultimate B5 AWD 3,371,000) and the 5 Sep 2025 Taiwan facelift launch coverage (7Car and U-CAR: B5 Plus 295.6萬 / B5 Ultra 337.1萬 / T8 Ultra 377.6萬). Discount benchmark: KingAutos published Volvo Taiwan cash-price campaigns — MY23 Plus B5 AWD 建議售價294萬 → 現金價249萬 (-45萬, 15%, plus a free Plus Pack worth 9.9萬); MY24 Plus B5 AWD 295.6萬 → 259萬 (-36.6萬, 12.4%). Current Volvo Cars Taiwan monthly-offers page (re-fetched 2026-08-12) quotes NO headline cash figure — only 120萬/40期0%利率, 1 year 乙式全險, warranty extended to year 4, and up to NT$100,000 of 政府貨物稅減免/汰舊換新補助.
purchase.notes:
Powertrain classification: B3/B4/B5 is a 48V mild hybrid. It cannot drive on battery alone, so it is classified as gasoline in this table, the same as every other 48V system here. Only full hybrids that can move the car on battery are 'hybrid'.
PRICE AUDIT RESULT: the 2,990,000 figure is CORRECT and I confirmed it independently from the Yahoo 2026年式 model page; no override was needed. The 295.6萬 figure that looks like a contradiction is the 5 Sep 2025 launch price of the same facelift — the 2026年式 carries a 3.4萬 uplift to 299萬. Both are real, they are different model years, and the gap is 1.15%, far inside the 3% tolerance. discounts 250,000 (8.4%) is a judgement call anchored on hard evidence: Volvo Taiwan has PUBLISHED cash prices 12.4-15% below list on this exact trim, so the brand's willingness to discount the XC90 is documented rather than folklore. I deliberately used LESS than those precedents because both were run-out campaigns with unit caps on a pre-facelift car, whereas the MY2026 is the current facelift only ~11 months into its cycle. 25萬 is a normal negotiated figure today; waiting for a run-out promotion plausibly reaches 35-45萬 and pulls real_cost toward 2.65M. DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS from discounts: (a) the 0% finance on 120萬/40期 is an interest saving, not a price cut; (b) the free 1-year insurance is excluded because insurance is out of scope by design; (c) the up-to-NT$100,000 政府貨物稅減免/汰舊換新補助 is excluded because it is a TAX rebate (tax is excluded by design) and is conditional on scrapping a qualifying old vehicle, which most buyers will not do — a buyer who does qualify should treat real_cost as up to NT$100,000 lower. onroad_fees 65,000 = 領牌規費+代辦 ~13,000 plus dealer-fitted accessories ~52,000 (隔熱紙 ~25,000, 行車記錄器 ~15,000, 腳踏墊/防水托盤 ~8,000, basic 鍍膜), scaled to a ~3M import 7-seat SUV; Volvo often bundles an accessory pack, which would push real accessory spend lower. real_cost = 2,990,000 - 250,000 + 65,000 = 2,805,000.

items.name: 過戶規費 + 代辦費
售前整備／內外美容（大型七人座 SUV）
8891／平台刊登費

selling_costs.notes: Top of the normal 4,000-15,000 band because this is a large premium 7-seat SUV: detailing a 4.95m body with a leather 7-seat interior costs more than a compact, and the listing sits on a paid platform tier for longer because the buyer pool for a 3M-class import is thin. Assumes a private sale (自售) — the figure is what the SELLER spends to transact. If the car is traded in to a dealer instead, these costs mostly vanish, but so does 14-19% of the price (see dealer_tradein_price at each checkpoint), which is a far bigger swing than the 14,000 saved. Items sum to exactly 14,000.

value_checkpoints.source: RE-VERIFIED BY THIS AUDIT. Dealer retail anchor: 8891 listing of a 2025 XC90 B5 Plus in New Taipei asking NT$2,270,000 (auto.8891.com.tw/usedauto-infos-4261283.html) — I re-fetched this page and the 227萬 ask is real. That is 車商售價, not what a seller receives. CAP THAT FORCED A CORRECTION: I also re-fetched the Volvo Selekt 原廠認證 listing for a 2024 Plus B5 AWD, 16,000 km, registered 2024-02-28, asking NT$1,850,000, and 8891 shows a 2024 Plus B5 AWD at 44,000 km asking NT$1,688,000. A private 1-year car cannot ask 200萬 when a factory-certified 2-year car with warranty, reconditioning and dealer finance sits at 185萬 retail — the two would be only 8% apart across a full year plus certification. ADJUSTMENT: retail comparable ~225萬 for our 7,000 km car, then a 13.5% cut to 1,950,000 for private sale. The cut is at the WIDE end of the 8-15% band precisely because near-new private sellers compete head-on with certified dealer stock they cannot match on warranty or financing. dealer_tradein_price 1,700,000 is a further 12.8% below private (about 25% under the retail ask), which is what a Volvo dealer pays on a 1-year-old car it will recondition and re-list near 225萬. Low mileage (7,000 km vs a typical 15,000-20,000 at 1 year) is worth roughly 3-5% and is included.

Best-evidenced checkpoint, but the private figure is still MODELLED from retail asks, which is why confidence is medium and not high. Real listings of the same trim at near-identical mileage: Volvo Selekt 原廠認證 2024 XC90 Plus B5 AWD, 16,000 km, registered 2024-02-28, asking 185.0萬 (volvoselekt.com.tw detail 2128 — re-fetched and confirmed by this audit); 8891 2024 Plus B5 AWD at 44,000 km asking 168.8萬 (re-fetched and confirmed); findcar 2023 XC90 Plus B5 AWD 7-seat, 16,956 km, asking 194.8萬; 8891 2023 B5 AWD Plus 159.3萬. ADJUSTMENT: the 194.8萬 findcar ask is a high outlier — a NEWER factory-certified 2024 car asks only 185.0萬, and an uncertified older car cannot be worth more. Both verified 2-year asks (185.0萬 certified / 168.8萬 at 44,000 km) cap a 3-year car below ~175萬, so I set the retail comparable at ~174萬, then cut 12% to 1,530,000 for private sale. dealer_tradein_price 1,320,000 is a further 13.7% below private. Retention cross-check: this trim listed at 294-295.6萬 in MY23/MY24, so a 174萬 retail ask is ~59% of original list at 3 years, consistent with the whole cluster. Low mileage is already reflected because the chosen comparables are themselves the 16,000-17,000 km cars.

RE-VERIFIED BY THIS AUDIT against the live findcar 2021 page: 153.8萬 @50,005 km, 138.0萬 @72,000 km, 115.8萬 @155,000 km (all 車商售價). 8891 adds 2021 B5 R-Design 119.9萬 @89,400 km, 2021 B5 Momentum 125.0萬, and — the useful cap — a 2022 (4-year-old) B5 Momentum at 139.8萬 @54,000 km. ADJUSTMENT: our 35,000 km car sits BELOW the lowest-mileage comparable (50,005 km at 153.8萬) and the Plus outranks the Momentum that dominates this vintage, so it belongs at the top of the cluster. But it cannot ask much above the 4-year-old car at 139.8萬, so I set the retail comparable at ~148萬 rather than the 150萬+ the raw mileage gradient alone would suggest. Cut 12% for private sale → 1,300,000. dealer_tradein_price 1,120,000 is a further 13.8% below private; the gap widens slightly versus year 3 because the factory warranty (3年/10萬公里, extended to year 4 by the current promo) has expired and the dealer now carries the repair risk.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM SAME-GENERATION CARS, MILEAGE-ADJUSTED — stated explicitly, not presented as direct data. The 2nd-generation XC90 ran 2015-2026 with two facelifts, so 2019 cars ARE the same generation (no predecessor substitution needed), but they are pre-facelift and use T5/D5 engines rather than the B5 mild hybrid. Re-fetched findcar 2019: 129.8萬 @116,809 km and 100.8萬 @100,914 km (T5 Momentum) — only TWO XC90 listings on that page, so it is a thin cluster. THE CORRECTION: 8891 carries a third 2019 comparable the original record missed — a T5 Momentum at 117,500 km asking only 87.9萬 — plus a 2020 (6-year-old) B5 Momentum at 109.9萬 @96,400 km and another at 88.8萬 @129,200 km. A 7-year car cannot out-ask the 6-year B5 at 109.9萬 by much, and the 129.8萬 findcar ask is the outlier of the set, not its centre. ADJUSTMENT: retail comparable ~112萬 (above the 100.8萬 and 87.9萬 high-mileage cars for our 49,000 km advantage, but held under the 6-year-old 109.9萬 car's level plus only a small low-mileage premium). Cut 13% for private sale → 1,000,000. dealer_tradein_price 820,000 is a further 18% below private — a wider cut because a 7-year out-of-warranty European SUV is hard for a dealer to finance and to warrant. Retention cross-check: the 2019 T5 Momentum listed new at 283萬, so 100.8萬 @101,000 km is ~36% of list at 7 years; our low-mileage car at ~40% of list is consistent. Confidence low: the mileage adjustment is a model, not an observation, the powertrain differs, and the discontinuation risk noted below is not priced in.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM SAME-GENERATION CARS, MILEAGE-ADJUSTED — stated explicitly, not presented as direct data. Again no predecessor generation was needed: 2016 XC90s are the same 2nd generation, just first-series with T5/T6/D4/D5 engines. findcar 2016 XC90: 10 cars, 平均車價 88.7萬; individuals 89.8萬 @90,000 km (D4), 79.8萬 @165,582 km (T6 AWD), 75.0萬 @157,128 km, 69.8萬 @143,367 km, 63.8萬 @170,887 km (D4 Momentum); two entries at 120-125萬 look like listing errors against the rest of the set and were discarded. 8891 (re-fetched by this audit) corroborates the level and the shape: 2016 D5 Momentum 55.9萬 @214,900 km, 2017 T5 70.9萬 @127,900 km, 2017 T6 Inscription 92.8萬 @93,000 km. ADJUSTMENT: our 70,000 km is below every credible comparable, so the retail ask sits at the top of the genuine cluster, ~88萬 — level with the 89.8萬 @90,000 km car and the 92.8萬 9-year T6, which is as high as a 10-year import can credibly be listed. Cut 14% for private sale → 755,000; the private/retail gap widens at this age because the dealer's price carries reconditioning and a short warranty a private seller cannot offer. dealer_tradein_price 605,000 is a further 20% below private — dealers pay very little for 10-year European SUVs (high recon cost, no finance available to the next buyer). Retention cross-check: an 88萬 retail ask is ~31% of the ~283萬 original list. Confidence low: mileage adjustment is modelled, the powertrain differs, and the combustion XC90 is at end of life with the electric EX90 as successor — a discontinued flagship from a brand pivoting to EV typically depreciates FASTER in years 7-10 than its own history implies, so this and the 7-year figure should be read as the optimistic end.

maintenance.plan_notes: INTERVAL: Volvo Taiwan schedules the XC90 at 1萬公里 or 1年, whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/year this buyer NEVER hits the mileage trigger, so the plan is purely TIME-DRIVEN — one annual service every year, ten services over ten years, with the bill shaped by calendar-aged items (brake fluid every 2 years, tyres hardening at 5-6 years regardless of tread, 12V AGM battery at 4-5 years, coolant) rather than by wear. That is why tyres, not engine work, are the single largest line in the 3-5y window. NO FREE MAINTENANCE APPLIES — RE-VERIFIED BY THIS AUDIT: Volvo Taiwan's 4年/8萬公里免費定期保養 programme covers pure-electric models only, and the official Volvo Cars Taiwan monthly-offers page for the XC90 (re-fetched 2026-08-12) lists only 120萬/40期0%利率, 1 year 乙式全險, 第4年延長保固 and up to NT$100,000 政府補助 — no free-maintenance item of any kind. Residual uncertainty: secondary sources describing the programme are inconsistent about model eligibility, so a buyer should confirm at the dealer; if free maintenance were in fact granted, the 0-5y figures below would fall by roughly NT$60,000-80,000. WARRANTY: factory cover is 3年/10萬公里, and the current offer extends it to year 4, so out-of-warranty risk allowances appear only in the 5-7y and 7-10y windows — exactly where they bite, since Volvo parts and labour are priced as premium import. COST BASIS: Volvo Taiwan publishes a 定期保養費用 lookup (volvomsp.volvocartw.com/MaintenanceService/) but it returns no public price table without a VIN, so per-service figures are built from Taiwanese owner reports — Mobile01 owners describing a first service around NT$10,000 including air filter and disputing the '7-8千 just for oil' claim, a Dcard report of an XC90 4萬公里 service at NT$20,000, and a brake job quoted above NT$40,000. This is the softest part of the record. Costs below are per-window (since the previous checkpoint), not cumulative; the ten-year total is NT$464,000, about NT$46,400/year, which is low for a 3M-class European SUV precisely because of the 7,000 km/year mileage.

major_items: 年度定期保養 x1（機油、機油濾芯、原廠電腦檢測）
冷氣濾網
checkpoints.source: Volvo Taiwan interval 1萬公里/1年 (owner and dealer service pages); Mobile01 XC90 owner threads reporting a first service around NT$10,000 including an air filter, and explicitly pushing back on the claim that a single oil change costs NT$7,000-8,000. Time-driven: at 7,000 km the car is nowhere near the 1萬公里 trigger, so this is the 1-year service. Fully inside the 3年/10萬公里 factory warranty, so no repair risk is priced in. No free-maintenance credit applies (see plan_notes).

major_items: 年度定期保養 x2（第2年約 12,000、第3年約 22,000）
引擎空氣濾芯 + 冷氣濾網
煞車油更換（2年一次，時間到期而非里程）
checkpoints.source: Two annual time-driven services across the 1-3y window (12,000 + 22,000 = 34,000). Sized from Mobile01/Dcard Taiwanese owner reports putting routine Volvo services in the NT$12,000-20,000 range once filters and fluids are included, with the 2萬公里-class service — reached here by TIME at year 3, at only 21,000 km — carrying engine air filter, cabin filter and the 2-year brake fluid change. Still inside factory warranty (3年/10萬公里, extended to year 4 by the current promo), so scheduled work only, no repair allowance.

major_items: 年度定期保養 x2（約 13,000 + 17,000，含火星塞，Volvo 依4年/6萬公里到期）
四條輪胎更換（275/45R20 級距，約 52,000）— 老化到期，非磨耗
12V AGM 電瓶（約 11,000）
煞車油再次更換
checkpoints.source: Dominated by TIME-EXPIRED consumables, the signature of a low-mileage car. Items: services 13,000 + 17,000, tyres 52,000, AGM battery 11,000 = 93,000 (brake fluid folded into the service line). Tyres are the biggest single item: at 35,000 km the tread is barely worn, but 20-inch premium rubber hardens and must be replaced at 5-6 years on safety grounds — a fitted set of four for an XC90 runs about NT$52,000 in Taiwan. The 12V AGM battery (the mild hybrid keeps a conventional 12V alongside the 48V system) typically dies at 4-5 years at ~NT$11,000. Spark plugs come due on time rather than mileage. Service costs sized from the same Mobile01/Dcard owner reports. Factory warranty has just expired (year 4 with the promo extension), so this window still carries no repair allowance. Note the tyre and battery figures are market-typical prices, not quotes for this car.

major_items: 年度定期保養 x2（約 15,000 + 26,000，大保含變速箱油、冷卻液、煞車油）
前煞車來令片 + 碟盤（約 36,000）
保固外風險準備（約 25,000）：懸吊襯套、48V 輕油電 ISG/皮帶、節溫器、感知器
checkpoints.source: ARITHMETIC CORRECTED BY THIS AUDIT: the itemised lines sum to 15,000 + 26,000 + 36,000 + 25,000 = 102,000, but the original record stated 100,000 for this window; period_cost is now 102,000 so the items reconcile. First window fully OUTSIDE warranty (factory 3年/10萬公里, extended to year 4 by the current offer), so a repair allowance appears here for the first time. Brake job sized from a Dcard owner report of an XC90 brake replacement quoted above NT$40,000 — NT$36,000 covers front pads and discs only, since at 7,000 km/year the pads survive far longer than average and the rears are pushed to the next window. The 8-speed automatic's fluid and the coolant both come due on the 6-year/6萬公里 schedule, landing inside this window by time. The NT$25,000 risk allowance is a modelled provision, not a quote: it is what a 6-7 year premium import typically absorbs in bushings, sensors and mild-hybrid ancillaries once nothing is covered. Confidence low because that provision is an estimate and the B5's 48V components (ISG, 48V battery module) have no established Taiwan out-of-warranty cost record, B5 XC90s having only arrived here around 2020-2021.

major_items: 第二套輪胎（約 56,000）— 再次老化到期
第二顆 12V AGM 電瓶（約 12,000）
後煞車來令片 + 碟盤 + 冷卻液（約 28,000）
保固外風險準備（約 65,000）：氣壓避震壓縮機/氣囊、水幫浦、冷氣壓縮機、引擎腳、48V 電池模組
checkpoints.source: Items sum to 64,000 services + 56,000 tyres + 12,000 battery + 28,000 rear brakes/coolant + 65,000 risk = 225,000. Three annual time-driven services plus a second full round of age-expired consumables — the tyres fitted at year 5 harden out again around year 10-11 even though total mileage is only 70,000 km, and the AGM battery repeats on the same 4-5 year clock. The NT$65,000 risk provision is the honest large item: an 8-10 year XC90 in Taiwan realistically meets at least one significant out-of-warranty repair, and if the car carries the optional four-corner air suspension a single compressor or air spring can consume that provision by itself (the Plus does not fit it as standard, but it is a common option box). Sized from Taiwanese owner reports of Volvo parts and labour pricing rather than from a quote for this car. Confidence low: this window is a modelled provision and the real spread is wide — a lucky car might spend NT$150,000 while an unlucky one exceeds NT$350,000.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr; every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000 / 21000 / 35000 / 49000 / 70000). At 7,000 km/yr the Volvo service interval (12 months or 10,000 km, whichever first) is TIME-DRIVEN, not mileage-driven, so the car gets one service per year regardless of distance and never reaches a mileage-triggered major service inside 10 years. Consequences baked into the numbers: (a) consumables that age out rather than wear out dominate - tyres are replaced on age at ~year 5 and ~year 10, not on tread depth; (b) the 12V AGM battery and brake fluid follow the calendar; (c) brake discs on a PHEV driven this little tend to surface-rust from regen braking, so discs are budgeted alongside pads rather than pads alone. Used values are quoted for LOW-MILEAGE examples (roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr), which sell above the mileage-blind market average. EXCLUDED by design: tax (牌照稅/燃料費) and insurance. ALSO EXCLUDED and not counted as maintenance: home AC wallbox supply and installation for the plug-in hybrid - Volvo TW normally supplies a portable/wall charger with the car, but apartment-building electrical work and a dedicated meter in Taiwan typically runs NT$20,000-60,000 extra and is a one-off ownership cost, not a service item. This car can also be run purely on petrol, so the charger is optional rather than mandatory.

purchase.source: Official Taiwan launch pricing for the second-facelift XC90, launched 2025-09-05: B5 AWD Plus NT$2,956,000 / B5 AWD Ultra NT$3,371,000 / T8 AWD Plug-in Hybrid Ultra NT$3,776,000. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY in this audit against six outlets: 7Car (https://www.7car.tw/articles/read/112982, fetched directly), U-CAR, TVBS Cars, King Autos, CARNEWS and 8891 新車頻道 ('原廠售價 377.60萬'). Discount level inferred from documented Volvo TW cash offers on the outgoing generation (TVBS Cars: 2024 XC90 Ultimate B5 AWD list NT$3,371,000 sold at NT$3,040,000, a NT$331,000 cut; 8891 promo 'XC90 Plus B5 AWD 現省56.6萬'), discounted down because those were end-of-life clearances.
purchase.notes: LIST PRICE CONFIRMED AT NT$3,776,000. The lineup scout reported NT$3,790,000 from the Volvo TW configurator (https://www.volvocars.com/tw/build/), which returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches and could not be verified by either the researcher or this audit. Six independent dated Taiwanese outlets covering the 2025-09-05 launch all give NT$3,776,000, so that figure stands. The NT$14,000 gap is 0.4%, far inside the 3% tolerance, and does not move the model. Full trim name is 'T8 AWD Plug-in Hybrid Ultra' (455 hp combined, ~83 km EV range, Four-C air suspension standard on Ultra); the trim field is abbreviated to fit the display label limit. The pre-sale price leaked at NT$3,866,000 and was cut to NT$3,776,000 at launch, so Volvo TW was already positioning this car defensively. Worth noting for the retention model: the OUTGOING MY2024 XC90 Ultimate Recharge T8 also listed at NT$3,776,000 (per FindCar's new-car reference table), so the T8 top trim has sat at NT$3.69-3.85m in Taiwan for a decade - predecessor retention ratios therefore map onto this car with minimal rescaling distortion. DISCOUNTS NT$200,000 (5.3% of list): Volvo Taiwan genuinely discounts, unlike Tesla. Documented cuts of NT$331,000-566,000 exist but were run-out deals on the superseded generation; this car is roughly 11 months into its lifecycle, so a realistic negotiated cash cut on a slow-selling NT$3.78m flagship is NT$150,000-250,000, often part-delivered as free accessories or a bundled service package. ONROAD_FEES NT$65,000 = 領牌/監理規費/代辦 ~NT$15,000 + 配件 ~NT$50,000 (premium window film ~NT$25,000, paint coating ~NT$15,000, dash cam and mats ~NT$10,000), scaled to a NT$3.78m luxury SUV. Tax and insurance deliberately excluded.

selling_costs.notes: Priced for a private sale (自售) of a large luxury SUV. Statutory transfer paperwork is only ~NT$1,500 but agents charge ~NT$3,000. Detailing is at the upper end because a 7-seat SUV interior and 21-inch wheels take longer to prep and because buyers at this price point walk away from a scruffy car. If sold to a dealer as a trade-in instead, selling costs fall to roughly zero - the dealer absorbs the transfer and prep - which is part of why dealer_tradein_price is quoted materially below private_sale_price.

value_checkpoints.source: CORRECTED DOWNWARD BY THIS AUDIT (was NT$2,700,000 private / NT$2,360,000 trade-in). The prior figure was back-solved from an assumed '79% of list' dealer-retail retention while ignoring the best anchor available: Volvo Selekt (https://www.volvoselekt.com.tw/list.php?cars_type_sub_id=9) lists a MY2024 XC90 T8 Plus at 10,225 km asking NT$2,280,000 - a 2-year-old, very-low-mileage T8 that closely matches this buyer's usage. A year-1 PRIVATE price of NT$2,700,000 would have sat 18% ABOVE a 2-year-old certified dealer RETAIL ask, which is incoherent. Re-derivation: strip the ~6% Selekt certification premium from NT$2,280,000 to get ordinary dealer retail ~NT$2,143,000; express that against that car's REAL transaction price (list NT$3,406,000 less ~NT$350,000 of documented run-out discounting = ~NT$3,056,000) for 70.1% retention at 2 years; apply to this car's transaction price (NT$3,776,000 - NT$200,000 = NT$3,576,000) for a year-2 dealer retail of ~NT$2,508,000; step back one year (+11%) for a year-1 dealer retail ask of ~NT$2,784,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale_price = dealer retail less 10% -> NT$2,520,000; dealer_tradein_price = private less 12.5% -> NT$2,200,000. Transaction-price basis is used deliberately because the predecessor's list price was heavily discounted while this car's is not, so a list-to-list ratio would overstate the fall. Still an extrapolation: the facelift only launched 2025-09-05, so no genuine 1-year-old example of THIS car has traded.

Anchored on Volvo Selekt (https://www.volvoselekt.com.tw/list.php?cars_type_sub_id=9): MY2023 XC90 T8 Plus, 11,000 km, certified ask NT$2,320,000 - a genuine 3-year-old low-mileage T8, verified live in this audit. DENOMINATOR CORRECTED BY THIS AUDIT: the researcher divided this Plus-trim car by NT$3,760,000, which is the Ultimate/Inscription list, not the Plus list. Verified actual contemporary list for the MY2023 XC90 Plus Recharge T8 is NT$3,390,000 (8891 新車 '原廠售價 339.00萬'; the MY2024 equivalent is NT$3,406,000). Stripping the ~6% certification premium gives ordinary dealer retail ~NT$2,181,000 = 64.3% of the correct list (the researcher's wrong denominator produced 58.0%, understating retention by ~6 points). Applying 64.3% to NT$3,776,000 implies a dealer retail ask of ~NT$2,429,000; applying a 3-point haircut because a top Ultra trim retains slightly less than a mid Plus trim gives ~NT$2,320,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale = dealer retail less 10%; dealer trade-in = private less 12.5%. The two bracket NT$2,088,000-2,186,000 private and NT$1,827,000-1,913,000 trade-in, so the researcher's NT$2,120,000 / NT$1,850,000 survive the denominator fix and are retained. Cross-check: 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/volvo/xc90) lists a MY2022 Recharge T8 Inscription at 54,000 km for NT$1,888,000, consistent once the extra 33,000 km and one more year are priced in.

Near-exact real-world match, verified live in this audit: FindCar (https://www.findcar.com.tw/q/xc90%20t8) lists a MY2021 XC90 T8 7-seater with 36,000 km asking NT$1,758,000 (dealer 達興汽車, Tainan) - 5 years old at almost exactly our assumed mileage, and a 車商 dealer RETAIL ask. DENOMINATOR CORRECTED BY THIS AUDIT: the researcher used NT$3,760,000; FindCar's own new-car reference table gives the MY2021 XC90 T8 Recharge Inscription at NT$3,690,000. That is 47.6% dealer-retail retention (not 46.8%). Applied to NT$3,776,000 -> dealer retail ask ~NT$1,799,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale = retail less 10% -> NT$1,610,000; dealer trade-in = private less 12.5% -> NT$1,410,000 (was NT$1,590,000 / NT$1,390,000; the small uplift is purely the denominator fix). The low-mileage premium this buyer earns is visible in the same dataset: a same-year MY2021 T8 Inscription with 101,000 km sits at only NT$1,400,000 on Volvo Selekt, ~20% below the 36,000 km car. Cross-check: Selekt MY2022 T8 Plus, 30,000 km, NT$1,900,000 (4 years).

EXTRAPOLATED - no 7-year-old example of the current generation exists, so this uses the PREDECESSOR generation expressed as a retention ratio and re-applied to this car. Real predecessor data point, verified live: 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/volvo/xc90) lists a MY2020 XC90 T8 Inscription with 42,000 km at NT$1,588,000 - 6 years old, low mileage. Against the corrected MY2020 T8 Inscription list of NT$3,690,000 (FindCar new-car reference; the researcher used NT$3,760,000) that is 43.0% retention. Extending one more year on the observed ~4 point/year slope in this zone gives ~39% at 7 years, i.e. a dealer retail ask of ~NT$1,474,000 on our car. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale = retail less 10% -> NT$1,320,000; dealer trade-in = private less 12.5% -> NT$1,155,000. Extra downward pressure reflected here: the 3-year factory warranty is long gone and buyers start pricing in Four-C air suspension and PHEV repair risk.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor generation - NO 2016-2017 XC90 T8 is currently trading in Taiwan (the T8 was a rare, expensive variant then: T8 Inscription launched at NT$3,850,000 and T8 Excellence at NT$4,200,000-4,700,000), so a genuine 10-year T8 market does not exist. Method: take the 2016 XC90 generation now at 10 years old. FindCar (https://www.findcar.com.tw/q/xc90) shows a 2016 XC90 average of NT$887,000, and 8891 shows 2016 D5 cars at 200,500 km / NT$690,000 and 214,900 km / NT$559,000 - against ~NT$2,850,000 average 2016 list that is ~31% retention at typical (150,000-200,000 km) mileage. Adding the low-mileage premium a 70,000 km car earns at this age (+~25%) gives ~38%, then subtracting a PHEV penalty because the 8-year/160,000 km high-voltage battery warranty has lapsed by year 8 and Taiwanese buyers discount an out-of-warranty PHEV traction pack heavily, lands at ~28% of list -> dealer retail ask ~NT$1,060,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = retail less 10% -> NT$950,000; trade-in = private less ~17% (dealers cut harder on old, hard-to-move luxury PHEVs) -> NT$790,000. Genuinely extrapolated, not observed, and the donor pool is diesel/petrol rather than PHEV - hence low confidence. Retained unchanged by this audit: the endpoint is defensible and no better data exists.

maintenance.plan_notes: INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Volvo's schedule is 12 months or 10,000 km, whichever comes first; at 7,000 km/yr the clock always wins, so this car gets exactly one service per year and 10 services in 10 years. It never reaches a mileage-triggered major service inside the horizon - so the cost profile is dominated by calendar-driven items (tyres ageing out, brake fluid, 12V battery, coolant) rather than wear-driven ones. FREE-MAINTENANCE PROGRAMME - BASE CASE CHANGED BY THIS AUDIT. Volvo Taiwan's STANDARD cover is a 3-year unlimited-mileage warranty plus an 8-year/160,000 km high-voltage battery warranty on PHEV/BEV. A warranty pays for REPAIRS, not routine servicing. Free scheduled maintenance is NOT standard - it is a rotating, time-limited promotion, and the live example found in this audit is an XC40 B3 campaign ('限時贈 3 年/3 萬免費保養套裝', expiring 9/30), i.e. an entry-model volume push, not an offer attached to a NT$3.78m flagship. The researcher assumed the buyer secures a 3yr/30,000km package and priced years 1-3 at NT$2,000 and NT$8,000 - effectively zero - on that unverified assumption. This audit prices the base case WITHOUT the package: year 1 NT$15,000 and year 3 NT$33,000, using one annual service per year at the NT$13,000-14,000 flagship rate plus consumables. IF the buyer does negotiate the package onto the deal, deduct roughly NT$38,000 across years 1-3 (years 1 and 3 fall back to about NT$2,000 and NT$8,000). Volvo TW also sells 'VOLVO Plus', a prepaid 5-year/5-service contract covering oil, consumables and labour that transfers to the next owner (https://dacota.tw/blog/post/volvo-plus) - not assumed here, but it would flatten years 5 and 7. Per-visit dealer rates come from Volvo Taipei's published band of NT$8,000-15,000 per routine service, taken at the top of the band because the XC90 T8 is the range flagship. THE BACK-LOADING IS STILL THE POINT: years 1-3 cost NT$48,000 while years 7-10 cost NT$430,000, because warranty expiry, air-suspension risk and the lapsed HV-battery warranty all land late.

Wiper blades and washer fluid ~NT$2,000
Covered by warranty, not by this line: any defect repair (3-year unlimited-mileage warranty)
checkpoints.source: REPRICED BY THIS AUDIT (was NT$2,000). The prior figure assumed a negotiated 3yr/30,000km free scheduled-maintenance package as the base case; this audit verified that Volvo TW free servicing is a rotating promotion tied to specific campaigns (the live one found is XC40 B3, time-limited to 9/30) and not standard on the XC90 T8 Ultra, and that the standard 3-year unlimited-mileage warranty covers repairs rather than routine servicing. Per-visit rate from Volvo Taipei's published NT$8,000-15,000 routine-service band, taken near the top for the flagship. Service scope cross-checked against the official Volvo TW scheduled-maintenance lookup (https://volvomsp.volvocartw.com/MaintenanceService/), which validates content but publishes no flat price table. Deduct ~NT$13,000 if a free-service package is secured.

major_items: 2 annual services (year 2 and year 3) at dealer rate ~NT$13,500 each - still inside the 3-year warranty for repairs, but servicing is paid
Wheel alignment after the first two years ~NT$3,000
Wiper blades, cabin filter, minor consumables ~NT$3,000
checkpoints.source: REPRICED BY THIS AUDIT (was NT$8,000), same basis as year 1: free scheduled maintenance is promotion-dependent, not contractual, so the base case pays for servicing. At 7,000 km/yr cumulative mileage reaches only 21,000 km, so both visits are time-triggered annual services rather than mileage-triggered majors. Rate band from Volvo Taipei's published NT$8,000-15,000 per visit; scope validated against the official TW lookup (https://volvomsp.volvocartw.com/MaintenanceService/). Deduct ~NT$25,000 if a 3yr/30,000km package is secured.

major_items: 2 annual services at full dealer rate, ~NT$14,000 each (warranty expired at year 3)
Tyre set - 4 tyres AGE OUT at ~5 years on a 21-inch XC90 Ultra despite only 35,000 km (~NT$60,000 fitted)
12V AGM battery - PHEVs are hard on the 12V and it typically dies at 4-5 years (~NT$12,000 incl. BMS registration)
Brake fluid change
Four-wheel alignment after new tyres
Cabin/engine air filters, misc consumables
checkpoints.source: Per-visit rate from Volvo Taipei's published NT$8,000-15,000 routine-service band (taken at the top for the XC90 flagship) and the official TW lookup (https://volvomsp.volvocartw.com/MaintenanceService/). Tyre pricing from Taiwan 21-inch premium tyre retail data (275/40R21 premium fitment runs ~NT$13,000-16,000 per corner). 12V battery replacement on the XC90 T8 requires BMS registration after fitting, a known Taiwanese specialist service. This is the first period with NO warranty and NO possible free-servicing package, which is why cost jumps sharply versus the previous window. Retained unchanged by this audit.

major_items: 2 annual services at full dealer rate (~NT$15,000 each)
Front brake pads AND discs (~NT$35,000) - regen braking spares the pads but the discs surface-rust from light use on a low-mileage PHEV, so both go together
Spark plugs on the T8's petrol engine (calendar-driven at ~6 years at this mileage)
Coolant change - both engine circuit and the separate HV-battery cooling circuit
Brake fluid change
Four-C air suspension out-of-warranty risk allowance (~NT$30,000) - air struts/compressor are standard on Ultra and a known failure point past year 6
Misc: bushings, sensors, wipers
checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED risk-weighted estimate, not a quoted table. Grounded in Taiwanese owner reports of Volvo out-of-warranty costs (an XC60 owner reported ~NT$20,000 for a 40,000 km service and a further ~NT$20,000 for brake pads, via Dcard car forum; Mobile01 thread 6989636 discusses XC90 80,000 km servicing and post-warranty independent-shop options). The air-suspension line is an expected-value allowance rather than a certainty, and is flagged as such - Four-C is standard equipment on the Ultra trim so the exposure is real. Retained unchanged by this audit.

major_items: 3 annual services at full dealer rate (~NT$17,000 each)
Second tyre set - the year-5 tyres age out again at ~5 years / 35,000 km (~NT$65,000)
Rear brake pads and discs (~NT$28,000)
Second 12V AGM battery (~NT$13,000)
8-speed automatic transmission fluid service (calendar-driven, ~NT$18,000)
Brake fluid x2
Four-C air suspension: compressor and/or strut replacement allowance (~NT$60,000) - by years 8-10 this is more likely than not

High-voltage battery risk allowance (~NT$30,000) - the 8yr/160,000km HV warranty lapses at year 8 and a full pack replacement runs well into six figures; this is a probability-weighted allowance, not a full replacement
Misc electronics, sensors, suspension bushings, coolant
checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED risk-weighted estimate for an out-of-warranty European PHEV flagship, not a quoted table. Two structural facts drive it: (1) the 8-year/160,000 km high-voltage battery warranty expires at year 8, mid-window, so years 8-10 carry uninsured traction-battery exposure; (2) Four-C air suspension is standard on Ultra and its failure rate climbs sharply after year 8. Grounded in Taiwanese owner cost reports (Mobile01 thread 6989636 on XC90 post-warranty servicing; Dcard reports of NT$40,000+ single visits on out-of-warranty Volvos) and in the fact that PHEV traction-pack work in Taiwan requires specialist BMS calibration. The NT$30,000 HV line is the weakest number in the record - it is a probability weight on a repair no Taiwanese quote was found for. Total 10-year maintenance across all five windows is NT$593,000, heavily back-loaded. Retained unchanged by this audit apart from the total.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; every checkpoint uses 7,000 km x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. Consequences: (a) all used-value figures are anchored on genuinely low-mileage Taiwanese listings and carry a low-mileage premium over the mileage-blind market average, and (b) Volvo's service schedule (1 year or 10,000 km, whichever comes first) is TIME-driven for this buyer, so the car sees one calendar-triggered annual service at only ~7,000 km and cost-per-km is high even though cost-per-year looks normal. B4 is a 48V mild hybrid (2.0T petrol + integrated starter-generator), NOT a plug-in, so there is no home-charger cost and no charging infrastructure to account for; Taiwan listings label it 油電, which is why powertrain is recorded as hybrid rather than gasoline. The plug-in V60 is the T8 (Plus T8 2,406,000 / Ultra T8 2,776,000). Vehicle licence tax (牌照稅), fuel tax (燃料費), insurance and fuel are excluded from this record by design. CORRECTED ASSUMPTION: the previous draft assumed a Volvo Taiwan 3年/3萬公里免費保養 package covered this car and set years 1 and 3 to near zero. Volvo Taiwan's own current promotions page lists free scheduled maintenance ONLY for pure-electric models (4年/8萬公里免費保養); the V60 line gets at most an extended-warranty bonus on the Recharge T8, and nothing on the Plus B4. Years 1 and 3 are therefore priced as fully PAID annual services. Out-of-warranty risk allowances start in the 3-5y window because the factory warranty is 3 years / unlimited km.

purchase.source: List price NT$1,950,000 independently re-verified first-hand, unchanged from the previous draft: Volvo Taipei dealer blog states '建議售價為新台幣1,950,000元' for Plus B4 (blog.volvo.taipei/article_532.html), and TVBS Cars' January 2026 promotion round-up states 'V60 Plus B4原價195萬，優惠價來到179萬' (news.tvbs.com.tw/cars/3094407, fetched and read directly this pass). Within 3% of the researcher's figure, so list_price stands. DISCOUNT REVISED 160,000 -> 180,000: the 179萬 promo is the advertised floor (16萬 off), but an actual signed 8891 deal sheet for a V60 B4 Plus records 成交價 175萬 (c.8891.com.tw/menu/volvo/v60/share/17582), i.e. 20萬 off, and 8891's V60 deal-sheet feature cites transactions as low as 168萬. 180,000 sits between the published promo and real transacted deals.
purchase.notes:
Powertrain classification: B3/B4/B5 is a 48V mild hybrid. It cannot drive on battery alone, so it is classified as gasoline in this table, the same as every other 48V system here. Only full hybrids that can move the car on battery are 'hybrid'.
list_price 1,950,000 = official 建議售價 for the V60 Plus B4, the entry trim of the Taiwan V60 range and unchanged across the 2025/2026 年式 changeover. discounts 180,000 blends the published Volvo Taiwan promo (195萬 -> 179萬, TVBS Jan 2026) with a real 8891 deal sheet at 175萬; it is a normal-day figure, not a best case (run-out stock discounts on Volvo TW have reached 30.6-30.8萬, though those reported figures were for XC90/XC60, not the V60). onroad_fees 55,000 = 領牌 + 代辦 (~15,000) + 配件 (window tint, dash cam, floor/boot mats, paint coating; ~40,000), scaled to a ~NT$2M premium wagon. real_cost = 1,950,000 - 180,000 + 55,000 = 1,825,000. Tax (牌照稅/燃料費) and insurance are deliberately EXCLUDED. Trim label: 'Plus B4' — B4 denotes the ~197 hp 2.0-litre turbo petrol engine with a 48V mild-hybrid ISG; the Plus trim carries the PlusPack bundle with Google built-in infotainment and driver-assist package. model_year set to 2026 (the 年式 on sale in Taiwan as of 2026-08 per KingAutos and 2026-年式 spec write-ups); the entry price is 1,950,000 under either 年式, so this does not move any number.

selling_costs.notes: Costs the seller pays to complete a PRIVATE sale, matched to the private_sale_price figures in value_checkpoints. Government transfer paperwork in Taiwan is only a few hundred NT$, so the 2,000 is mostly 代辦 service charge. Detailing is at the upper end (8,000) because a premium European wagon needs paint correction and interior work to defend its asking price against dealer-prepared and Volvo Selekt certified stock. Listing on 8891/SUM as a private seller runs a low-single-thousand fee with optional boosts. Total 12,000 sits in the upper half of the typical 4,000-15,000 range, correct for this vehicle class. Reviewed and left unchanged from the previous draft — it was the one section with no defect.

value_checkpoints.source: CORRECTED DOWN from 1,350,000. Direct anchor found this pass: Volvo Selekt Taiwan currently lists two 2025 V60 B4 Plus cars — 4,135 km and 10,945 km — both at NT$1,498,000 (volvoselekt.com.tw/list.php?cars_type_sub_id=5). That is our exact car at ~1 year and comparable mileage, at CERTIFIED dealer retail, the top rung of the price chain. The previous draft's assumed dealer retail of ~1,520,000 was above the real certified asking price, and its 1,350,000 'private' figure was only ~10% under certified retail, i.e. it was still a dealer-level number. Selekt premium measured from the same page against ordinary dealer retail: 2024 B4 Ultimate at Selekt 1,580,000 (11,578 km) / 1,598,000 (23,804 km) versus 1,458,000 for a 19,000 km 2024 B4 Ultimate on 8891 = ~8-9% certification premium. So ordinary dealer retail for a 1-year 7,000 km Plus B4 ~ 1,380,000 (small low-mileage premium applied, 7,000 km vs the 10,945 km comparable). ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale_price 1,230,000 is ~11% below that ordinary dealer retail; dealer_tradein_price 1,060,000 is a further ~14% below the private figure. No dealer or Selekt asking price was copied through.

Re-derived independently and landed on the same figures as the previous draft, so left unchanged. Anchors read first-hand: 8891 中古車 shows 2023 V60 B3 Plus at 1,089,000-1,190,000 with 20,000-32,400 km (auto.8891.com.tw/volvo/v60), and Volvo Selekt lists a 2023 V60 B3P with 28,189 km at 1,250,000. B4 carries roughly a 5% premium over B3, and 21,000 km is at the low end of that mileage band, giving an ordinary dealer RETAIL level of ~1,220,000 for a 3-year 21,000 km Plus B4 (the Selekt 1,250,000 B3 car implies ~1,145,000 ordinary retail for a B3, consistent). A typical 3-year-old TW car shows 36,000-45,000 km, so the low-mileage premium here is real. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale_price 1,070,000 is ~12% below dealer retail; dealer_tradein_price 930,000 is a further ~13% below the private figure.

Anchors read first-hand on 8891 中古車: 2021 V60 B4 Momentum at 998,000 with 30,000 km (a genuine 5-year-old at genuinely low mileage — the closest single comparable), 2022 V60 B4 Plus 油電 at 959,000 with 40,000 km, and 2022 B4 Momentum at 928,000-1,029,000 with 40,000-51,000 km. Volvo Selekt cross-check: 2022 V60 B4 Plus, 24,000 km, 1,080,000 certified, implying ~995,000 ordinary retail. Converging on ordinary dealer RETAIL ~990,000 for a 5-year 35,000 km Plus B4. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale_price 870,000 is ~12% below dealer retail; dealer_tradein_price 750,000 is a further ~14% below the private figure. Trade-in is where Volvo's mid-pack Taiwan residuals bite — dealers discount European wagons on intake because they are slow-turning stock.

CORRECTED DOWN from 750,000. The previous draft's 7-year anchor was a claimed 2019 V60 T4 Momentum asking 858,000; 8891's live V60 中古車行情 read this pass shows 2019 T4 Momentum actually asking 628,000-679,000 with 86,600-130,000 km, plus a 2019 T6 Inscription at 798,000 with 70,000 km (auto.8891.com.tw/volvo/v60). The old figure therefore priced a PRIVATE sale above what dealers are asking at retail for the same age. Real 7-year-old cars of this generation do exist (2nd-gen V60 launched in Taiwan 2019), but they are T4/T6 petrol, not B4 mild hybrid (B4 arrived ~2021). Our car earns a genuine premium for 49,000 km versus the 87,000-130,000 km comparables and for the better-equipped Plus trim, so ordinary dealer RETAIL is taken at ~800,000 — above every listed 2019 T4 but at the T6 Inscription level. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale_price 700,000 is ~12% below that dealer retail; dealer_tradein_price 600,000 is a further ~14% below the private figure, the spread widening with age because dealers price reconditioning risk into out-of-warranty European stock.

EXPLICITLY EXTRAPOLATED — no genuine 10-year data exists for this generation, which launched in Taiwan in 2019, and CORRECTED DOWN from 570,000. Method: take the PREDECESSOR generation (1st-gen V60, 2011-2018) at 10+ years today. The previous draft used only FindCar's 2015 V60 asks (588,000-602,000) and derived a 32.5% retention ratio; 8891's larger sample read this pass is materially harsher — 2013-2017 V60 T5 R-Design asking 240,000-309,000 with 80,000-170,000 km — and FindCar's own tail agrees (2013 V60 at 298,000 with 170,000 km, 2012 at 458,000 with 180,000 km). Blending both sources for a ~10-year 1st-gen V60 at a typical ~120,000 km gives ~380,000 dealer retail against a ~1,850,000 original list = ~20.5% retention, not 32.5%. Applying 20.5% to this car's real_cost of 1,825,000 gives ~374,000, then ~+30% for 70,000 km versus the predecessor sample's ~120,000+ km gives ordinary dealer RETAIL ~490,000. Curve cross-check: 800,000 dealer retail at 7 years falling to ~490,000 at 10 years is ~-15%/yr, consistent with the observed cliff on decade-old European wagons here. ADJUSTMENT MADE: private_sale_price 450,000 is ~8% below dealer retail (the private/dealer gap narrows at this age because dealer margin on a cheap old car is thin); dealer_tradein_price 380,000 is a further ~16% below — at 10 years many dealers will only take the car as a wholesale/auction unit. Confidence low: the ratio is transplanted from an older, mechanically different car (no 48V system), and the mild-hybrid electrical hardware is an unpriced residual risk at this age.

maintenance.plan_notes: SCHEDULE TYPE: Volvo's modern service schedule is 1 year or 10,000 km, whichever comes first. At 7,000 km/year this buyer is firmly TIME-driven — one service per year, triggered by the calendar, never by the odometer. MAJOR CORRECTION versus the previous draft: it assumed Volvo Taiwan's '3年/3萬公里免費保養' package covers the V60 Plus B4 and therefore set year-1 and year-3 windows to 2,000 and 6,000 at 'high' confidence. Volvo Taiwan's own current promotions page (volvosales.com.tw 優惠專區, read this pass) lists free scheduled maintenance ONLY for pure-electric models ('不限款式純電車型 - 4年/8萬公里免費保養'); the only V60 items on that page are extended-warranty bonuses for the V60 Recharge Plus T8 and Recharge Ultimate T8. No free-maintenance offer covering the V60 Plus B4 could be found, and a targeted search for one returned nothing. The single supporting document the previous draft had was an XC40 B3 campaign page, which is a different model's campaign. Years 1 and 3 are therefore repriced as fully PAID annual services, adding ~38,000 to the 10-year total. WARRANTY: 3 years, unlimited mileage on non-BEV Volvo passenger cars in Taiwan (3年不限里程), so out-of-warranty risk begins at year 4 — this part of the previous draft was correct and is confirmed. COST BASIS: Taiwanese owner receipts — a V60 B4 owner quoted ~NT$30,000 for the 40,000 km service (Mobile01 t=7012076), an XC60 owner reporting ~NT$20,000 for a 40,000 km service that reached NT$40,000+ once brake discs were added (Dcard p/259693147), and an owner calling the 35,000 km service expensive (Dcard p/254031130). Volvo Taiwan's own quote portal (volvomsp.volvocartw.com) returned no usable data, so no official price table backs these numbers — every paid window is owner-receipt based, which is why nothing here is rated 'high'. Independent European specialists would run 30-40% cheaper but are not assumed. CONSUMABLES TIMING at 7,000 km/year: tyres are replaced on AGE not tread (~every 5 years, so around year 5 and year 10); the 12V AGM battery lasts ~4-5 years (year 5 and year 9); brake pads and discs last far longer than average, so the first real brake job falls in the 5-7y window; brake fluid is a 2-year item and spark plugs fall due around year 5 and year 9. period_cost values are PER-WINDOW (cost since the previous checkpoint), not cumulative. Ten-year total is approximately NT$414,000.

major_items: Year-1 annual service — engine oil, oil filter, multi-point inspection — PAID, no free-maintenance package applies to the V60 Plus B4 (~NT$10,000)
Wiper blades and washer fluid (~NT$2,000)
checkpoints.source: CORRECTED UP from 2,000. Volvo Taiwan's promotions page shows free scheduled maintenance only on pure-electric models, not on the B4 mild hybrid, so the first annual service is out of pocket. Cost taken as a Volvo TW dealer 小保養 (oil + filter + inspection) at the low end of the owner-receipt range, since only ~7,000 km have accumulated and the service is calendar-triggered. Confidence downgraded from 'high' to 'medium': no official Volvo TW price table could be retrieved, so this rests on owner-reported dealer pricing.

major_items: Year-2 annual service, oil and filter (~NT$11,000) — PAID
Year-3 annual service, oil, air filter, cabin filter, inspection (~NT$16,000) — PAID
Brake fluid change, 2-year item (~NT$4,000)
Wiper blades x2, four-wheel alignment (~NT$3,000)
checkpoints.source: CORRECTED UP from 6,000 for the same reason as year 1 — no free-maintenance package covering the V60 Plus B4 could be evidenced on Volvo Taiwan's promotions page or anywhere else. Two paid annual services plus a 2-year brake fluid change and consumables. Still inside the 3-year factory warranty, so no repair-risk allowance is carried in this window. Costs scaled down from the ~NT$20,000-30,000 owner receipts for 35,000-40,000 km services, because at 21,000 km these are the lighter calendar-driven visits. Confidence downgraded from 'high' to 'medium': owner-reported pricing only, no official table.

major_items: Year-4 annual minor service, now out of warranty (~NT$11,000)
Year-5 major service — spark plugs, air filter, cabin filter, coolant check (~NT$28,000; owner receipts for a ~35,000 km Volvo service run around NT$35,000)
Brake fluid change, 2-year interval (~NT$4,000)
First tyre replacement, set of 4 — AGE-expired at 5 years despite only 35,000 km (~NT$30,000 for premium 235/45R18-class rubber, plus ~NT$2,000 alignment)
12V AGM battery replacement (~NT$10,000 — the mild hybrid still runs a conventional 12V AGM alongside the 48V pack)
Wiper blades (~NT$3,000)
checkpoints.source: Mobile01 / Dcard Taiwanese owner receipts (V60 B4 40,000 km service quoted ~NT$30,000; a 35,000 km service described as expensive; an XC60 40,000 km visit at ~NT$20,000 before brakes) plus Taiwan premium tyre retail pricing. This is the window where costs jump, because the 3-year factory warranty expires at year 3 and the age-driven consumables (tyres, 12V battery) all land here. The tyre line is driven purely by rubber age — a 12,000 km/year driver would have worn these out anyway, so this buyer gets no tyre saving from low mileage. Unchanged from the previous draft; independently re-checked and found sound.

major_items: Year-6 minor and year-7 major annual services incl. transmission fluid, brake fluid, coolant (~NT$37,000 combined)
Front brake pads AND discs — first real brake job, deferred this late only because of the low annual mileage (~NT$22,000)
Rear brake pads (~NT$10,000)
OUT-OF-WARRANTY RISK ALLOWANCE ~NT$30,000: 48V mild-hybrid ISG belt-starter-generator, water pump/thermostat, engine mounts, suspension bushings, PCV — probability-weighted, not a certainty
Wiper blades, alignment (~NT$4,000)
checkpoints.source: Owner receipts (Dcard: XC60 at 40,000 km, ~NT$20,000 routine service pushed past NT$40,000 once brake discs were replaced — the brake line here is the same failure mode; Mobile01: V60 B4 40,000 km service quoted ~NT$30,000). Warranty expired four years earlier, so the risk allowance is real exposure, not padding. Volvo dealer brake parts in Taiwan are notably expensive versus Japanese brands. Unchanged from the previous draft; independently re-checked and found sound.

major_items: Three annual services, years 8-10, one of them a major with spark plugs and coolant (~NT$54,000)
Second tyre replacement — again AGE-driven, 5 years after the year-5 set (~NT$32,000 + ~NT$2,000 alignment)
Second 12V AGM battery, around year 9 (~NT$11,000)
Rear brake discs (~NT$14,000)

OUT-OF-WARRANTY RISK ALLOWANCE ~NT$60,000: 48V pack / ISG degradation, turbo actuator, A/C compressor, water pump, suspension refresh, sensor and electronics faults typical of a decade-old European car
Wipers, alignment, misc. (~NT$2,000)
checkpoints.source: Extrapolated from the same Mobile01/Dcard owner-receipt cost base, escalated for age. The risk allowance is the dominant uncertainty and the largest single line — a decade-old Volvo in Taiwan can run well under this if nothing major fails, or far over it if the 48V hardware or the A/C compressor goes. No Taiwanese owner has yet run a 2nd-gen V60 B4 to 10 years (the generation launched here in 2019 and the B4 engine only arrived ~2021), so no real 7-10y receipt set exists for this exact powertrain.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr; all checkpoints use the 7,000 km/yr midpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. This matters twice. First, Volvo TW's service interval is 1 year OR 10,000 km whichever comes first, so at 7,000 km/yr servicing is entirely TIME-driven: one visit per year, and mileage-triggered items (spark plugs, 8AT fluid, nominally around 60,000 km) do not arrive until roughly year 8 in calendar time. Second, at 10 years the car shows only 70,000 km, exceptional for a TW used car, so the used values here sit ABOVE mileage-blind averages -- and the comparables I anchored on are mostly HIGHER-mileage cars, so the adjustment is upward and is stated per checkpoint. THIS IS A PHEV, NOT A BEV: it keeps a 1,969 cc combustion engine, an 8-speed Geartronic automatic, spark plugs, engine oil and coolant, so its maintenance curve is legitimately combustion-shaped PLUS high-voltage battery exposure. A BEV-style near-zero maintenance curve would be wrong here. Spec confirmed from Volvo TW's own MY26 price/spec sheet: 455 hp combined, 88 km EV range, 18.8 kWh pack, 2,018 kg kerb weight (285 kg heavier than the B4), 235/40 R19 tyres -- the weight and the 19-inch rubber are why tyre and suspension costs run pessimistic. HOME CHARGER EXCLUDED: with 88 km of EV range at 7,000 km/yr this car runs almost entirely on electricity if charged at home. A home AC charging point in Taiwan costs roughly NT$30,000-80,000 installed and depends on 管委會 approval and the meter run; older 公寓 without a dedicated space may not be able to install at all. That is a genuine ownership cost but it is NOT maintenance, so it is excluded from the maintenance checkpoints by design. Taxes (牌照稅/燃料稅, reduced for PHEVs in TW) and insurance are excluded by design throughout.

purchase.source: CORRECTED FROM PRIMARY SOURCE. I downloaded Volvo Taiwan's own MY26 V60 price/spec PDF (https://www.volvocartw.com/pdf/carsp/V60.pdf) and decompressed its text streams directly rather than trusting a search snippet. The raw stream reads: 'MY26 ... V60, B4 | V60, T8 AWD Plug in Hybrid | Plus NT$1,990,000 | Ultra NT$2,090,000 | Ultra NT$2,790,000', and the equipment table's three column headers are literally 'V60 Plus, B4' / 'V60 Ultra, B4' / 'V60 Ultra, T8 AWD Plug in Hybrid'. The sheet carries a '2025 12' version stamp. So the CURRENT Taiwan V60 range is three cars, and the T8 is offered in Ultra trim ONLY, at NT$2,790,000. There is no MY26 'Plus T8'. The prior figure of NT$2,406,000 was real but STALE: FindCar's V60 new-price table lists it as the 2024 'V60 Plus Recharge T8' (alongside 2024 Ultimate T8 277.6萬, 2023 Plus T8 239萬, 2023 Ultimate T8 276萬), and the blog.volvo.taipei article quoting it is dated 2025-02-11. The Plus T8 was deleted from the range for MY26 and the surviving T8 moved 2,776,000 -> 2,790,000. Correction is +16.0%, far beyond the 3% tolerance.
purchase.notes: TRIM CORRECTED. The record id is left unchanged ('volvo-v60-t8-plus') because it is the storage key, but the car it describes no longer exists: Volvo TW dropped the Plus T8 for MY26 and the only V60 T8 now on sale is the Ultra at NT$2,790,000. Since the brief says to price the model year currently on sale, this record now prices the T8 AWD Ultra. Every downstream figure was rebased accordingly -- the previous record's used values were percentages of a real_cost that was NT$374,000 too low. LIST PRICE: 2,790,000, taken verbatim from the Volvo TW MY26 price sheet. DISCOUNTS: 180,000 (6.5% off list) as a realistic negotiated cash discount. Volvo TW does discount openly, but this is the halo powertrain with thin volume and thin dealer margin, so I set it slightly below the ~6.3% used for the XC60 B5 in percentage-of-list terms rather than the 8-10% seen on volume petrol trims. I did NOT stack the currently advertised '二年延長保固' bonus for V60 Recharge T8 into discounts -- it is a warranty sweetener, not cash off. Finance packages often show a bigger headline number that is not a true cash equivalent. ONROAD FEES: 45,000 = 領牌規費 ~5,000 + 代辦費 ~5,000 + a realistic premium-wagon accessory pack ~35,000 (隔熱紙 ~20,000, 行車記錄器 ~7,000, 原廠腳踏墊/行李廂托盤 ~5,000, misc). Scaled from the 40,000 used on the NT$2.39M XC60 by price. The previous 75,000 loaded 55,000-60,000 of accessories, which is above what a typical buyer actually spends and is inconsistent with the sibling Volvo record. real_cost = 2,790,000 - 180,000 + 45,000 = 2,655,000. Tax and insurance excluded by design; the PHEV 貨物稅 reduction is already baked into list price, not a separate rebate.

items.name: 過戶費 (transfer: 規費 + 代辦)
售前整備/美容 (detailing, paint correction, interior)
刊登費 (8891 / SUM listing slot)

selling_costs.notes: Unchanged from the prior record -- I checked it and it is sound. Sized for a private (自售) sale of a premium European wagon, consistent with private_sale_price being the headline resale figure. 過戶 規費 itself is only a few hundred NT$; the 2,000 assumes 代辦 through an agent rather than queuing at the 監理站. Detailing at 8,000 is the real line item: a NT$1M+ premium wagon will not photograph or negotiate well without proper paint correction and interior work, and skimping costs more in negotiation than it saves. Listing fee reflects a paid 8891 中古車 slot with photos. Total sits mid-range of the usual 4,000-15,000 band; a seller who cleans the car themselves and uses free channels could get to about 4,000, while full 鍍膜 before sale could exceed 20,000.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED -- no genuine 1-year-old V60 T8 listing exists in TW (the MY26 T8 Ultra has only just begun delivering). Interpolated between the real transaction price of a new car (2,610,000 for the car itself after the 180,000 discount) and the year-3 estimate below. The steep first-year drop is characteristic of TW premium PHEVs: a buyer of a 1-year-old car is competing against a new one that is itself discounted 6-8%, and must be compensated for the lost new-car warranty. 1,900,000 is 68.1% of list / 71.6% of real_cost. This is a PRIVATE figure, not a dealer asking price -- a 車商 would list the same car around 2,150,000-2,250,000. dealer_tradein set 14.2% below private, the normal 收購 spread on a nearly-new premium car where reconditioning risk is low but capital cost is high. Low-mileage premium applies (7,000 km is very low for a 1-yr car). REBASED: the prior record's 1,850,000 was a percentage of a real_cost NT$374,000 too low.

INTERPOLATED between the year-1 estimate and the year-5/6 real anchor, with a sanity check against 4-year gasoline V60 dealer stock I fetched myself from 8891 today: 2022 V60 B4 Momentum, 40,400 km, dealer asking 1,029,000, and 2022 V60 B4 Plus, 40,000 km, dealer asking 959,000. Against the 2023 B4 Plus list of 1,940,000 (FindCar) that is ~53% DEALER RETAIL at 4 years, so ~46-47% private after the standard 12% channel cut. The T8 sits on a much higher base (2,790,000) and expensive halo trims retain a LOWER percentage than cheap ones, so I used 52% of list at year 3 = 1,450,000 (54.6% of real_cost) rather than carrying the B4's percentage across. Low-mileage premium is embedded: 21,000 km at 3 years is roughly half what the B4 comparables show per year. dealer_tradein set 14.1% below private. I deliberately did NOT use the Volvo Selekt 認證 CPO listings the prior record leaned on -- I could not fetch that page to verify them, and CPO retail is the most expensive rung of the ladder, two channel steps above a private sale.

ANCHORED ON A REAL, T8-SPECIFIC LISTING that I fetched myself: FindCar shows a 2020 Volvo V60 T8 Recharge Inscription, 50,465 km, at 鴻齊汽車 (Kaohsiung) asking NT$1,188,000. That car is 6 years old and is a DEALER asking price. Its original list was 2,690,000 (FindCar's own new-price table: 2021 V60 T8 Recharge Inscription 269萬), giving 44.2% dealer retail at 6 years. ADJUSTMENT MADE: cut 12% to reach a private sale figure (1,045,000 = 38.9% private retention), scaled to this car's higher list (x 2,790/2,690 = 1,084,000 at year 6 / 50,465 km), then stepped BACK one year to year 5 (~+8%) and added a low-mileage premium for 35,000 km against the comparable's 50,465 km, then trimmed slightly because an asking price is not a transaction price. Result 1,200,000 = 43.0% of list / 45.2% of real_cost. Cross-check on the gasoline side, also fetched by me: 2021 V60 B5 R-Design, 84,600 km, dealer 899,000 against a 2,272,000 list = 39.6% dealer retail at 5 years, but at 2.4x this buyer's mileage. NOTE ON THE DISCARDED ANCHOR: the prior record's key year-5 source was a Facebook Marketplace private listing at 1,268,000 for a 2021 T8 with 39,000 km. I could not verify it (FB requires authentication) and it is implausible on its face -- it is HIGHER than the real 鴻齊 dealer asking of 1,188,000 for a car only one year older, which would invert the dealer-retail > private ordering. Dropped. dealer_tradein set 15.0% below private.

CURRENT-GENERATION DATA, and materially higher than the prior record's 680,000. The gen-2 V60 launched in TW in 2019, so a 2019 car is exactly 7 years old. Two independent routes agree. (a) From the real T8 anchor: the 2020 T8 Recharge Inscription at 50,465 km implies ~1,084,000 private at year 6 on this car's list basis; stepping down one year (~9%) and applying no mileage premium (our 49,000 km is level with that car's 50,465 km) gives ~985,000, which I trimmed to 930,000 for the approaching high-voltage battery warranty limit. (b) From 7-year gasoline V60 dealer stock I fetched from 8891 today: 2019 T6 Inscription, 70,000 km, dealer 798,000; 2019 T4 Momentum, 86,600 km, 679,000; 2019 T4 Momentum, 130,000 km, 628,000. The T6 Inscription converts to roughly 700,000 private, and our car carries a 30% mileage advantage over it (49,000 vs 70,000 km), which reliably commands a premium at this age. 930,000 = 33.3% of list / 35.0% of real_cost. I REMOVED the prior record's year-5-to-year-7 cliff (1,120,000 -> 680,000, a 39% two-year fall): it rested on treating the 2019 T6 as a plug-in hybrid with a 2,750,000 list, but the gen-2 V60 T6 sold in TW in 2019 was the twin-charged GASOLINE AWD, not a PHEV (the T8 Recharge did not reach TW until MY21/22), so the denominator was inflated and the retention ratio artificially depressed. The real 2020 T8 at 1,188,000 dealer sits between the two checkpoints and directly refutes a 680,000 private at year 7. dealer_tradein set 16.1% below private -- the spread widens with age as reconditioning risk rises.

EXTRAPOLATED -- stated explicitly, because no genuine 10-year data exists for the current V60 (gen 2 launched in TW in 2019, so the oldest is 7 years) and none at all for a 10-year-old V60 T8 anywhere in the TW market. Method: carried the gen-2 curve forward from the year-7 figure using the depreciation slope European premium wagons show between years 7 and 10 in TW (a further 40-45% loss), then applied two opposing adjustments -- UP for the exceptional 70,000 km (a 10-year TW car normally shows 120,000-150,000 km), DOWN for PHEV-specific risk, since the 8-year/160,000 km high-voltage battery warranty has expired on time by year 10 and TW buyers discount an out-of-warranty hybrid pack heavily. Net 540,000 = 19.4% of list / 20.3% of real_cost, which lines up with the 19.7% of real_cost carried at year 10 in the sibling Volvo XC60 record. I did NOT reuse the prior record's gen-1 route (2016 V60 D4 at ~300,000 dealer asking over an unsourced ~1,750,000 original list): its denominator was admittedly an estimate and its comparator was a diesel wagon, so the ratio it produced was two guesses multiplied together. Being explicitly extrapolated is fine; resting on an unverifiable denominator is not. dealer_tradein set 21.3% below private -- the widest spread of any checkpoint, because at 10 years most 車商 do not want an out-of-warranty European PHEV and will only take it at a wholesale/auction number.

maintenance.plan_notes: INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Volvo TW services at 1 year or 10,000 km whichever comes first; at 7,000 km/yr the clock always wins, so this plan is exactly one dealer visit per year (10 visits over 10 years) and mileage-triggered items land far later in calendar time than the brochure implies -- spark plugs and Geartronic 8AT fluid (nominally around 60,000 km) do not fall due until roughly year 8. NOT A BEV: the T8 keeps a 1,969 cc turbo+supercharged engine and an 8-speed torque-converter automatic, so oil, plugs, gearbox fluid and coolant all remain, on top of high-voltage battery exposure. A BEV-style near-zero curve would understate this car badly. WARRANTY: Volvo TW standard cover is 3 years unlimited mileage, and the high-voltage battery is covered separately for 8 years / 160,000 km -- at this mileage the pack is protected on time through year 8 and exposed only in the year-10 window. FREE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE -- VERIFIED AND IT DOES NOT APPLY: I fetched Volvo TW's 優惠專區 and it confirms the 4年/8萬公里免費保養 plus 4年/8萬公里延長保固 package is restricted to 純電車型 (pure EV). Plug-in hybrids including the V60 Recharge T8 get only a bonus 二年延長保固 (two-year extended warranty), no free servicing. So years 1-3 are correctly modelled as PAID. The 2-year warranty extension, if secured, pushes repair cover to year 5 -- but the year-5 window here is almost entirely consumables (tyres, pads, 12V, fluids) which no warranty covers, so it does not change the numbers, only the risk framing. If the buyer separately negotiates Volvo TW's prepaid 定期保養 contract, the year-1 and year-3 figures drop toward zero; that is unmodelled upside. COST BASIS: TW owner-reported invoices (see the source caveats -- these are inherited from the prior researcher and I could NOT verify the underlying threads): a 20,000 km service at NT$11,543 (oil 4,998, brake fluid 756, air filter 800, drain plug 126, balance labour); a 40,000 km service around NT$20,000, past NT$60,000 with brake pads; a 60,000 km service quoted near NT$50,000 before optional items were deleted. PHEV NUANCE: at 7,000 km/yr with 88 km of EV range the engine does relatively little work, so oil and plugs age out rather than wear out, and regenerative braking meaningfully extends pad life -- but at 2,018 kg the car is 285 kg heavier than the B4, so tyres, bushings and dampers wear on the pessimistic side, and the 235/40 R19 tyres harden with age well before the tread is gone.

major_items: 1x annual scheduled service (engine oil + filter, multi-point inspection)
Inside 3-year unlimited-mileage factory warranty -- no repair risk
High-voltage battery inside 8yr/160,000km warranty
checkpoints.source: Covers 0-1 yr only. One time-driven annual service, benchmarked to the reported TW Volvo invoice of NT$11,543 for a scheduled service (oil 4,998, filters, labour). Modelled as PAID -- I verified on Volvo TW's 優惠專區 that the 4-year free-maintenance programme covers 純電車型 (pure EV) only and that PHEVs like the V60 Recharge T8 receive only a two-year extended warranty. If a dealer bundles the first services into the deal this falls to near zero.

major_items: 2x annual scheduled service (years 2 and 3)
Brake fluid change at year 2 (time-based, every 2 years regardless of km)
Air filter + cabin/pollen filter at year 3
Still inside 3-year factory warranty -- no repair risk
checkpoints.source: Covers 1-3 yr only (two annual visits, not cumulative). Year 2 approx 12,000 including the time-based brake fluid change; year 3 approx 14,000 with air and cabin filters added. Consistent with the reported 20,000 km TW invoice of NT$11,543 plus filter items. Still time-driven, not mileage-driven, at 21,000 km total.

major_items: 2x annual scheduled service (years 4 and 5)
First full tyre set, 4x 235/40 R19 -- replaced on AGE not wear
Front brake pads and discs
12V AGM battery (first replacement)
Brake fluid + coolant
checkpoints.source: Covers 3-5 yr only. Build-up: 2 annual services approx 26,000; tyres approx 38,000 (four 235/40 R19 premium-fit tyres, size confirmed from Volvo TW's MY26 spec sheet, replaced at 5 years on rubber age -- at 35,000 km the tread is nowhere near gone, which is exactly what low annual mileage does to you); front pads and discs approx 15,000 (later than a combustion car thanks to regenerative braking, but the car weighs 2,018 kg); 12V AGM battery approx 10,000 (a known T8 weak point -- it supports the start-stop and hybrid systems and typically dies at 4-5 years); fluids approx 6,000. Factory warranty lapses at year 3 (year 5 if the two-year PHEV extension was secured), but every item in this window is a consumable that no warranty covers either way. Tyre and 12V costs are well-established TW market rates; the timing within the window is the uncertain part.

major_items: 2x annual scheduled service (years 6 and 7)
Spark plugs -- the T8's 2.0L is both turbocharged and supercharged
Geartronic 8-speed automatic transmission fluid service
Rear brake pads and discs
Out-of-warranty risk allowance: bushings/dampers, electric coolant pumps, sensors
checkpoints.source: Covers 5-7 yr only. Build-up: 2 annual services approx 28,000 (creeping up as more items get inspected); spark plugs approx 9,000; 8AT transmission fluid approx 15,000 (the MY26 spec sheet confirms the T8 uses the Geartronic 8-speed torque-converter automatic, not the B4's 7-speed DCT); rear pads and discs approx 14,000; brake fluid and coolant approx 7,000; out-of-warranty risk allowance approx 30,000 for suspension bushings and dampers at 6-7 years plus the T8's known electric coolant pump and A/C compressor exposure. Anchored to the reported TW figures of a 40,000 km service at NT$20,000 rising past NT$60,000 with brake work, and a 60,000 km service quoted near NT$50,000. Note the mileage-triggered items (plugs, gearbox fluid) arrive here on TIME, not km -- at 49,000 km they are early by the book but due by the calendar.

major_items: 3x annual scheduled service (years 8, 9 and 10)
Second full tyre set, 4x 235/40 R19 (age-driven again)
12V AGM battery (second replacement)
Brake fluid, coolant, further brake work
Risk-weighted allowance for HV battery module repair -- 8yr/160,000km warranty EXPIRES in this window
checkpoints.source: Covers 7-10 yr only -- a 3-year window, hence the larger figure. Build-up: 3 annual services approx 45,000; second tyre set approx 40,000 (the first set went in at year 5, so age forces another around year 10); second 12V AGM approx 11,000; brakes and fluids approx 20,000; out-of-warranty risk allowance approx 84,000. That last line is the honest uncertainty: the high-voltage battery warranty (8 years / 160,000 km) lapses on the TIME limit during this window even though the car is barely 44% of the way to the km limit. Volvo permits MODULE-level replacement rather than whole-pack replacement, which caps the downside -- a module job runs roughly NT$60,000-120,000 against a full pack -- so the allowance is risk-weighted (a fraction of a module job's cost times its probability) rather than assuming certain failure. It also absorbs water pump, A/C compressor and engine mount exposure at this age. RAISED from the prior record's 185,000: that sat BELOW the 210,000 carried by the sibling gasoline XC60 record over the same window, which is backwards -- a PHEV carries everything the gasoline car carries PLUS an expiring high-voltage pack. A car that never needs battery work comes in well under 200,000; one that needs a module exceeds it.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr, far below the TW average of ~12,000-15,000 km/yr. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Consequences: (1) every Tesla maintenance item except tire rotation is TIME-driven at this mileage - the manual's 40,000 km suspension-torque trigger takes 5.7 years to arrive and the car finishes 10 years at only 70,000 km, so the mileage grid never binds; (2) the car never reaches the battery warranty's km cap (192,000 km for Long Range), so only the 8-year clock ever binds; (3) used-value quotes are taken from LOW-MILEAGE 8891 listings, not from the mileage-blind average - at 5 years this car has 35,000 km where a typical TW Model 3 of that age shows 60,000-120,000 km. EXCLUDED from this record by design: license tax and insurance (per spec), and home AC charger installation - a TW wall connector plus electrical work runs roughly NT$40,000-80,000 depending on panel distance and whether the building's management committee approves; it is a real ownership cost but a one-off capital item, not maintenance, so it appears in neither purchase.onroad_fees nor maintenance. Public Supercharger-only ownership is viable but raises running cost; energy cost is out of scope here.

purchase.source: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY on 2026-08-12 by direct fetch of the U-CAR model page (https://newcar.u-car.com.tw/tesla/model%203/7036/overall, HTTP 200): the spec table reads 'Model 3 Long Rage RWD 174.99' and 'Model 3 Performance 233.79', the car-series header reads '2 車型 174.99 - 233.79 萬', and the body text states '現階段車系劃分為 Long Range RWD 後驅車型 174.99 萬，以及 Performance 車型 233.79 萬' plus '改款 Model 3 的入門車型，在 2026 年調整由 Long Range RWD 單馬達後輪驅動車型取代'. Independently confirmed by electrify.tw's launch article, whose headline reads '售價 174.99 萬、續航 711 公里'. NT$1,749,900 is correct - no correction needed. On-road fees built from the 2026 TW fee table: 監理固定規費 NT$1,250 (號牌費 600 + 行照費 200 + 檢驗費 450) + 領牌代辦手續費 ~NT$1,500 (published band 800-1,500).
purchase.notes: Full TW trim name is 'Long Range 後輪驅動' (Long Range RWD), the 2026 single-motor entry car that replaced the 2024-2025 後輪驅動 (RWD) trim in January 2026: WLTP 711 km, 0-100 km/h 5.2 s, 250 kW charging, NCA pack ~82 kWh gross. The trim name is misleading for depreciation purposes - despite the 'Long Range' badge it sits in the ENTRY price slot (1,749,900), not where the old Long Range AWD sat (1,999,900-2,234,000). discounts = 0 because Tesla Taiwan is a fixed-price, no-haggle direct seller: there is no dealer cash discount to negotiate. Tesla adjusts the list price instead, and the TW price history proves it - Long Range went 1,972,900 (2021) -> 2,234,000 (2022 peak) -> 1,999,900 (2024 煥新版), a 234,100 official cut, and the 2025 RWD sat at 1,699,900. LIVE LIST-CUT RISK, now priced into the residual curve rather than left as prose: electrify.tw's 2026-05-16 analysis states that with zero tariff on US-built passenger cars confirmed, this exact trim could fall from 1,749,900 to about 1,532,900 ('若美製車進口關稅從 17.5% 降為 0%，售價可從 174.99 萬台幣降到約 153.29 萬台幣'), and a Model 3 Standard variant (能源署 filing 'Model 3 HBMRB', 256 hp, 661 km WLTC, filed 2026-04-16) is projected at 1,350,000-1,530,000. onroad_fees 32,000 = 規費 1,250 + 代辦 1,500 + 隔熱紙/window film ~18,000 (Tesla TW ships the car without film and essentially every TW buyer adds it) + 腳踏墊, 車牌框, charging accessories and delivery-day sundries ~11,250. Optional 自選車牌 (2,000) and 動產擔保設定費 (3,500, cash buyers exempt) are excluded. Paint, wheels and driver-assistance are options, not fees, so they are excluded from real_cost: 星空灰/珍珠白/深藍 +37,500, 烈焰紅 +75,000, 19吋 Nova 輪圈 +62,500, 黑白內裝 +37,500, EAP ~111,000, FSD ~222,000. Tax and insurance excluded by design.
