value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED, and REDUCED BY THIS AUDIT from the researcher's 1,950,000. The absence of data is itself the finding and was independently re-confirmed: fetching https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/a6-sportback-e-tron on 2026-08-12 returns 「共找到 1180 輛車」 — the model filter falls through to the entire all-Audi inventory, i.e. not one A6 e-tron of any age is listed anywhere in Taiwan. The nearest real German-BEV anchor was also re-verified listing by listing: 8891 shows five Audi Q4 e-tron, all 2024 cars at about 2 years old on 5,300-18,000 km, dealer asking 143.8 / 148.0 / 158.0 / 158.0 / 176.8 萬. WHY THE CUT: the researcher worked back from those to a year-1 dealer asking of 220萬, which is 78.6% of list — the highest first-year retention of any German BEV in this table (BMW i4 72%, BMW i5 71%, BMW iX3 69%, Mercedes EQE 67%) — while simultaneously arguing, correctly, that Audi BEVs have the THINNEST used demand of the group. A car with literally zero used-market presence cannot out-retain the i4. The researcher's own reading of the Q4 anchor (Audi BEVs asking well under two-thirds of list at 2 years) implies roughly 74-76% of list at year 1, i.e. a dealer asking price near 211萬, not 220萬. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN APPLIED (8891 prices are 車商售價, dealer RETAIL, never what an owner receives): dealer retail 2,110,000 → private sale 1,880,000 (10.9% below, inside the 8-15% band) → dealer trade-in 1,630,000 (a further 13.3% below private). Implies a 30.2% first-year loss against real_cost, squarely in the peer range (i4 28.0%, i5 29.0%, iX3 30.7%, EQE 33.5%) and correctly front-loaded for a German BEV. The 7,000 km odometer is already credited — without it this would sit lower.

EXTRAPOLATED between two anchors that this audit re-fetched and verified line by line, since no A6 e-tron of this age exists anywhere. Upper anchor: 8891 Audi Q4 e-tron, five listings, 2024 cars at about 2 years, 5,300-18,000 km, dealer asking 143.8-176.8萬. Lower anchor: 8891 Audi Q8 e-tron, only two listings in the whole country — 「Audi Q8 e-tron 2024款 e-tron 55Q 純電」 2023年, 1.9萬公里, asking 208.0萬, and 「2024款 50 quattro advanced 進化版」 2024年, 7000公里, asking 198.8萬. Both confirm the years 1-3 slide continues hard with no plateau. Placing this car on that trajectory at 3 years gives a dealer asking price near 160萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 1,600,000 → private sale 1,420,000 (11.3% below) → dealer trade-in 1,240,000 (12.7% below private). At 52.7% of real_cost this sits just under the BMW i4 at the same age (55.4%), which is the right relative position given Audi's thinner demand. The low 21,000 km is worth a few points against these comparators and is already reflected.

Strongest evidence point in this record, and every listing was RE-FETCHED AND CONFIRMED VERBATIM by this audit on 2026-08-12 from https://auto.8891.com.tw/audi/e-tron-sportback — the direct BEV predecessor. The page reads 「共找到 10 輛車」, the entire national supply, of which 8 carry prices and 2 read 電洽: 55 quattro S line asking 147.8萬 (2022年, 5萬公里), 147.8萬 (2022年, 5.8萬公里), 148.8萬 x2 (2021年, 4.14萬公里); 50 quattro S line asking 115.9萬 (2022年, 8.9萬公里) and 123.8萬 x3 (2022年, 2.7-2.8萬公里). SUM independently corroborates: https://www.sum.com.tw/carinfo-777056.php resolves to a live page titled 「AUDI e-tron Sportback 2022年 優惠價 149.8萬」, and https://www.sum.com.tw/carinfo-780646.php to 「AUDI E-TRON GT 2022年 優惠價 228.8萬」; 8891 shows the same e-tron GT generation at 218.8萬 / 5.5萬公里. CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED BY THIS AUDIT from medium to low. The absolute used prices are hard and re-verified, but converting them to a level for THIS car requires a retention ratio whose denominator — the e-tron Sportback 55's original TW list price — could not be sourced by the researcher and could not be sourced by this audit either (every general search engine reachable from this environment blocked automated queries, and U-CAR has no reachable model page for the discontinued car). A ratio resting on an unverified denominator does not meet the medium bar, whatever the quality of the numerator. Working assumption unchanged: an original list in the 350-390萬 band puts dealer asking at 4-5 years near 38-42% of list; applying that to this car's real_cost and crediting our 35,000 km against those comparators' 41,000-89,000 km gives a dealer asking price near 120萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 1,200,000 → private sale 1,060,000 (11.7% below) → dealer trade-in 920,000 (13.2% below private). Year 5 is also the exact month the 5-year/100,000 km vehicle warranty expires, which the used market prices in.

EXTRAPOLATED from predecessor-generation ratios per the newer-than-10-years rule — no current-generation A6 e-tron will exist at 7 years until 2032. Two predecessor families were used, and the SUM anchors were re-fetched and confirmed by this audit. ICE reference for shape: SUM's Audi search lists 「AUDI A6 AVANT C8 2019年, 2000cc, 107000公里, 桃園市 冠威汽車, 159.8萬」 and an A8 at 158.9萬 (3000cc, 47,860 km); 8891 shows an A6 Sedan C8 2021 40 TFSI Technik at 82.9萬 on 124,900 km — combustion A6s hold roughly half of original list at 7 years. BEV reference for level: the e-tron Sportback data above is already only about 40% of list at 4-5 years, i.e. a German BEV runs roughly 12-15 percentage points behind its combustion equivalent at the same age, and the gap widens rather than closes. Applying the BEV-adjusted ratio to real_cost gives a dealer asking price near 83萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 830,000 → private sale 730,000 (12.0% below) → dealer trade-in 630,000 (13.7% below private). Partly cushioned: the 8-year/160,000 km battery warranty — sourced verbatim, see below — is still live at year 7, which is the only reason this is not lower.

EXTRAPOLATED from predecessor-generation retention ratios — no 10-year data can exist for this car. Anchors from SUM's Audi listings, all large German luxury at extreme age: A8 3.0 V6 from 2011 (15 years, 194,500 km) asking just 19.9萬; A7 Sportback 3.0 TFSI 2011 (15 years, 127,000 km) asking 33.0萬; A6 C7 2011 asking 19.8萬 (176,020 km) and 49.8萬 (132,865 km); A6 Avant C7 2014 (12 years, 213,253 km) asking 35.8萬. Big German luxury cars in Taiwan do NOT flatten out the way a Lexus does — the tail keeps falling because the used market prices in out-of-warranty repair risk. Expressed as a ratio of those cars' original list prices and applied to real_cost, then discounted further for three BEV-specific factors: the 8-year battery warranty has EXPIRED by year 10, replacement-pack risk is unquantifiable to a private buyer, and two further generations of EV will have launched by 2036. That gives a dealer asking price near 45萬. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: dealer retail 450,000 → private sale 390,000 (13.3% below) → dealer trade-in 320,000 (17.9% below private — a wider cut than earlier checkpoints, because dealers take on an out-of-warranty EV only at a price that covers battery risk, and many simply decline). Curve check after this audit's year-1 correction: private sale runs 1,880,000 → 1,420,000 → 1,060,000 → 730,000 → 390,000, period losses of 815k / 460k / 360k / 330k / 340k. Front-loaded as required, and the tail does NOT flatten — the year 7-10 loss slightly exceeds the year 5-7 loss.

maintenance.plan_notes: HONESTY FIRST: no Audi Taiwan EV service price table and no owner receipt could be obtained, by the researcher or by this audit. audi.com.tw returns HTTP 503, myaudi.tw and audi-service.com.tw are JavaScript-rendered with no pricing, Mobile01 search returns HTTP 403, SUM's 保養工資查詢 sits behind a script, and every general search engine reachable from this environment (Bing, DuckDuckGo, Mojeek, Startpage, Ecosia, Brave, Yandex, three SearxNG instances) blocked automated queries. The ONE hard fact is the warranty, quoted verbatim in a live 8891 Q4 e-tron listing title and re-confirmed by this audit: 「Q4 e-tron 45/原廠新車保固5年10萬公里 電池保固8年16萬公里」 — 5 years/100,000 km vehicle, 8 years/160,000 km battery. Every cost figure below is a reasoned estimate at Audi Taiwan dealer labour rates, NOT a quoted price, and every checkpoint is therefore marked low confidence. STRUCTURAL FIX BY THIS AUDIT: the researcher's third checkpoint was labelled years 3 — a duplicate of the second — while carrying assumed_km 35,000 and a source string that reads 'Covers years 3-5'. It is the year-5 checkpoint and has been relabelled years 5, restoring the required 1/3/5/7/10 ladder and the assumed_km = 7000 * years rule. INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: at 7,000 km/year this car reaches only 70,000 km in ten years, so no distance trigger ever fires — servicing is annual by the calendar, brake fluid is every two years by the calendar, and tyres are replaced because the rubber hardens with age, not because the tread is gone. WHAT A BEV SAVES: no engine oil, no spark plugs, no coil packs, no thermostat housing, no DPF, no 48V starter-generator, and regenerative braking means pads barely wear. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAVE, and why this is nowhere near a RAV4: Audi dealer labour rates apply unchanged; the car weighs 2,175 kg (spec table, re-verified) and its spec-table fitment is staggered 235/45 R20 front / 265/40 R20 rear, which cannot be rotated, so all four go together at premium prices; brake fluid and battery-circuit coolant still need changing; the 12V battery still dies on schedule; and low annual mileage plus Taiwan's humidity actively CORRODES brake discs that regen never scrubs clean, so discs get replaced for rust rather than wear. TYRE CAVEAT (added by this audit): U-CAR's article text says the entry trim's standard fitment is 19-inch, contradicting its own per-trim spec table. The two tyre line items below are priced on the 20-inch staggered assumption and are therefore an UPPER BOUND; on 19-inch square tyres they would be lower and rotation would become possible. Out of warranty the BEV-specific risk items are real money: electric coolant pump for battery thermal management, DC-DC converter, on-board charger and charge port, air-conditioning compressor (which on a BEV also serves battery cooling and therefore runs far more than on a combustion car), and control modules. NO AIR SUSPENSION on this trim — ETtoday, re-verified, states 「S6 e-tron 標配主動式氣壓懸吊」 and nothing equivalent for the standard car — so no air-strut budget, which is the main reason this is cheaper late-life than an air-sprung German SUV. PREPAID PACKAGES: Audi Taiwan does market prepaid service packages and its 舊換新方案, and a package is commonly bundled into a deal at this price point. No free package is assumed — the years 0-1 and 1-3 figures are the unsubsidised numbers. If a package is bundled, years 1 and 3 fall toward zero, but the years 5, 7 and 10 periods already carry the FULL unsubsidised cost and would not change. Ten-year total is NT$601,000 (8,000 + 32,000 + 116,000 + 155,000 + 290,000), roughly double a RAV4 and consistent with the German BEV peers in this table (BMW i4 519,000, Mercedes EQE 573,000, BMW iX3 528,000, BMW i5 825,000).

assumptions.notes: Checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000/21000/35000/49000/70000), the midpoint of the 6,000-8,000 km/yr profile and roughly half the Taiwan average. At this mileage servicing is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Audi Taiwan's schedule is annual with a secondary kilometre trigger that 7,000 km/yr never reaches, so every checkpoint carries exactly one paid visit per year and consumables age out rather than wear out. (The scout quoted that trigger as '10,000 km within 12 months'; the exact figure could not be re-verified on Audi Taiwan's service site, but the conclusion is unaffected at any trigger from 10,000 km upward.) Tax (approx 17,410/yr = 11,230 licence + 6,180 fuel fee) and all insurance are EXCLUDED by design. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE SCOUT'S LOW-MILEAGE PREMIUM CLAIM: the scout asserted that same-year 2023 A6s ask 148-150万 at 35,000-47,000 km but 188万 at 12,300 km, and used that ~20-point spread to push every checkpoint toward the top of its band. The 188万 / 12,300 km car is a 2024 40 TFSI S line, NOT a 2023 - it is a year younger and a higher trim, so that spread is age and trim, not mileage. Inside a genuinely same-year set the mileage premium is approximately zero: a 2023 40 TFSI Technik with 4,714 km asks 148.0万 while a 2023 40 TFSI Technik with 35,000 km asks 149.0万 - the lower-mileage car asks slightly LESS. Low mileage is therefore treated as protecting this car from the bottom of each observed band, not as earning a premium at the top of it. This trim is the FWD 204 PS entry car; quattro, rear-axle steering and adaptive air suspension are not fitted, so no air-spring replacement is carried in the maintenance tail (that risk belongs to the 200 kW quattro S line). The 48V MHEV plus starter-generator and its lithium pack ARE fitted and are carried as an out-of-warranty risk item from year 7.

purchase.source: List price INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED and the scout's NT$2,880,000 is CONFIRMED CORRECT. Two sources were fetched and read directly in this audit: Yahoo Autos 2026 A6 Sedan model page returns TFSI 150kW = 288万 (1984cc, 204hp@4300-6000rpm, 4-door 5-seat, fuel type 汽油) and TFSI 200kW quattro S line = 346万; CARTURE's 2026-01-14 full-range price table returns A6 Sedan TFSI 150kW 288万 / Sedan TFSI 200kW quattro S line 346万 / Avant TFSI 150kW 298万 / Avant TFSI 200kW quattro S line 356万. The Avant's 298万 matters because it is the denominator of the year-1 CPO anchor. Deviation from the scout is 0%, so the scout's figure stands. Discount is an estimate, not a sourced transaction: Audi Taiwan publishes only non-cash sweeteners for the A6 (5年保固, 最高250万48期0利率, 低月付5,888元起), and the single 購車菜單 on 8891 for this nameplate is an unfilled 徵求 for the previous-generation car. 150,000 (5.2%) reflects a normal negotiated cash-plus-accessory concession on a just-launched large German sedan in an SUV-dominated Taiwan market - new generations discount less than run-out stock, so this is deliberately conservative. On-road fees are estimated at this price class, not quoted.
purchase.notes: 48V MILD HYBRID, CLASSIFIED GASOLINE. The C9 A6 2.0 TFSI uses Audi's MHEV plus - a 48V battery driving a belt starter-generator - which boosts and coasts but cannot move the car on electricity alone, so it is 'gasoline' for this table, not 'hybrid'. Note that Yahoo Autos labels the sibling TFSI 200 kW quattro as 油電混合/Hybrid; that trim runs the same 48V architecture and would also be 'gasoline' under these rules. Spec: 1984cc turbo I4, 204 PS / 340 Nm, 7-speed S tronic, FRONT-WHEEL DRIVE (independently confirmed by the drivetrain field 前驅 on Audi Taiwan's own Approved :plus listing for the same 150kW powertrain). Generation C9 went on sale in Taiwan in late 2025; the 200 kW quattro opened for order 2026-01. Arithmetic check: 2,880,000 - 150,000 + 65,000 = 2,795,000, verified. onroad_fees = 領牌 + 代辦 + 配件 only: government items are small (新領牌照登記費 600 + 行照 300 + 號牌 200) and the bulk is dealer 代辦費 ~12,000 plus a typical delivery accessory pack for this class (隔熱紙 for a large glass area ~30,000, 玻璃/車身鍍膜 ~18,000, 行車紀錄器 ~8,000, 腳踏墊與防水托盤 ~5,000). EXCLUDED from discounts on purpose: the 汰舊換新再減5万 shown on 8891 is a 貨物稅 rebate, conditional on scrapping a qualifying old vehicle, and tax is out of scope for this table. Also excluded: the 0% / low-monthly finance offers, which change cash flow, not price. The scout's classification and spec were audited and found correct - no change.

value_checkpoints.source: REDUCED from the scout's 2,020,000. Anchor re-verified by direct fetch and it is genuine: Audi Approved :plus (official CPO) listing 5196 - A6 Avant TFSI 150kW, 2026年式, registered 2025/11, ~1,000 km, 前驅, Kronos Gray, warranty to 2030/11, asking NT$2,488,000 against the Avant's 298万 list = 83.5% as CERTIFIED retail. Step-down chain: CPO carries roughly a 6% premium over ordinary dealer retail, and private sale runs a further ~10-11% under dealer retail, giving ~70% of list. The scout stopped there (0.835 x 0.94 x 0.90 x 2,880,000 = 2,020,000). Two corrections pull it down. (a) The anchor is an AVANT with 1,000 km and a live factory warranty to 2030; our car is the higher-volume Sedan with 7,000 km, and the Avant is the scarcer, more sought-after body in Taiwan. (b) A year-2 bridge now exists that the scout mis-dated away: the 40 TFSI S line with 12,300 km asking 188.0万 is a 2024 car, not a 2023, so against the C8 S line's 293.5万 list it reads 64.0% dealer retail at 2 years = ~57% private. A curve running 70% (y1) -> 57% (y2) -> 48% (y3) is too steep between y1 and y2; 67.7% of list at y1 makes the sequence coherent. 0.677 x 2,880,000 = 1,950,000 (69.8% of real_cost, a 30% first-year loss - a German number, not a Toyota one). NOT used: 8891's algorithmic 保值率 model claims 89.0% at year 1, which is mileage-blind, brand-generic and contradicted by Audi's own CPO asking price; rejected, as the scout also rejected it. Dealer trade-in set 12.1% under private.

REDUCED from the scout's 1,420,000 - this is the checkpoint the scout's dating error distorted most. Predecessor-generation (C8) evidence at exactly this age, converted to a ratio then applied to real_cost. Genuine 3-year-old cars on 8891 中古車 A6 Sedan, re-read directly in this audit: 2023 40 TFSI Technik豪華版 4,714 km asking 148.0万; 2023 40 TFSI Technik豪華版 35,000 km (3.5万公里) asking 149.0万; 2023 40 TFSI 28,000 km (2.8万公里) asking 149.8万. Against C8 list prices (享馭版 269.5万, Technik豪華版 277.5万) that is a TIGHT dealer-retail band of 53-55%. The scout reported the band as 53-64% and took the 64% as 'the clean low-mileage read' - but the 64% belongs to the 12,300 km car asking 188.0万, which is a 2024 model, not a 2023. Remove that mis-dated car and the top of the band disappears. Note also that within the true 2023 set the 4,714 km car asks 148.0万 while the 35,000 km car asks 149.0万, so there is no mileage premium to harvest at this age; our 21,000 km sits mid-pack and earns no uplift. Audi's own CPO 40 TFSI Technik registered 2023/08 at 168万 = 60.5% brackets the top as CERTIFIED retail, consistent with a ~6-7% CPO premium over the 53-55% ordinary band. Taking 54% dealer retail and the standard ~11% step down to private gives 48.1%; 0.481 x 2,795,000 = 1,345,000. THESE ARE NOT DEALER ASKING PRICES COPIED ACROSS - the 148-150万 figures were reduced before use. Dealer trade-in set 13.0% under private.

Essentially unchanged in value from the scout's 1,000,000, but the supporting reasoning was wrong and is restated. Real 8891 listings, model years re-verified in this audit: 2022 40 TFSI Technik豪華版 43,400 km (4.34万公里) asking 123.8万 against 274万 list = 45.2% at FOUR years; 2022 40 TFSI Technik豪華版 124,900 km (12.49万公里) asking 82.9万 = 30.3% at FOUR years; 2021 40 TFSI Premium 97,000 km asking 85.8万 against ~269万 = 31.9% at FIVE years. The scout filed that 124,900 km car as a 2021 five-year car, so its stated '5-year band' actually contained a 4-year car. Corrected, the only genuine 5-year point is the 2021 Premium at 97,000 km / 31.9%, and the useful bracket is 45.2% (4yr, 43,400 km) to 31.9% (5yr, 97,000 km). Our car is 5 years old with 35,000 km - lower mileage than every comparator - so it interpolates to ~40% dealer retail, and ~11% down to private gives 35.4%; 0.354 x 2,795,000 = 990,000. Sense check in absolute terms: the 43,400 km 4-year car asks 123.8万 at a dealer, so a 5-year 35,000 km car asks roughly 110-115万 at a dealer and ~99万 privately, scaled to the C9's higher base. Marked low because the mileage correction, not any single listing, is doing the work, and because the 82.9万 cluster shows how wide the dispersion is at this age.

REDUCED from the scout's 800,000, because the scout's 7-year comparator is really a 6-year car. Real 8891 listings with model years re-verified: 2020 40 TDI 30,000 km asking 93.8万 against ~259万 list = 36.2%; 2020 40 TDI 87,000 km (8.7万公里) asking 89.0万 = 34.4%; 2020 40 TDI Premium 156,000 km asking 72.8万 = 28.1%. All three are 2020 cars, i.e. SIX years old in 2026. The scout dated the 87,000 km car as a 2019 and read it as '~34% at 7 years'; it is 34% at 6 years, so the whole 7-year read was anchored a year too generously. There is in fact NO genuine 7-year comparator in the current listing set, making this a one-year extrapolation beyond the data. Starting from 36.2% dealer retail at 6 years / 30,000 km and adding a year plus 19,000 km gives ~30.5% dealer retail at 7 years / 49,000 km; ~11% down to private gives 27.0%; 0.270 x 2,795,000 = 755,000. Held deliberately low rather than flattened, because Audi Taiwan's factory warranty (3 years unlimited + years 4-5 under 100,000 km) has expired by now and the Taiwanese used market discounts an out-of-warranty German car for repair risk. One genuine 個人自售 point exists - 2020 40 TDI Premium, 205,000 km, private asking 80.0万 - and is useful only as a reminder that private ASKING prices run optimistic; it was not used as a comparator. Comparators are diesel C8s, a further reason for low confidence. Dealer trade-in set 15.2% under private - dealers widen the spread on older German stock.

REDUCED SHARPLY from the scout's 515,000 - the second big correction. No 10-year data exists for this generation (C9 launched in Taiwan late 2025), so this is extrapolated from the C7.5 A6, expressed as a retention ratio and applied to this car's real_cost. Real 8891 listings as of 2026-08: 2017 35 TFSI 142,400 km (14.24万公里) asking 53.9万; 2018 35 TFSI 59,900 km (5.99万公里) asking 46.9万; 2016 35 TFSI 141,000 km asking 42.8万; 2016 35 TFSI 120,000 km asking 32.2万; 2016 35 TFSI 190,000 km asking 29.8万. Original list: A6 Sedan 35 TFSI 238万 from 2015, 248万 for 2017年式. That gives 10-year dealer RETAIL retention of 12.5-18.0% for the true 2016 cars, and 21.7% for the 9-year 2017. The scout claimed 'our 70,000 km is far below the 120,000-190,000 km typical of these survivors, so the top of that band applies: ~20%'. That reasoning inverts the data: the TOP of the band (53.9万, 21.7%) belongs to the HIGHEST-mileage car in the set (142,400 km), while the genuinely low-mileage car (2018, 59,900 km) asks only 46.9万 = 18.9% despite being two years YOUNGER. Mileage barely orders price at this age. A defensible read for a 10-year car at 70,000 km is therefore ~17% dealer retail - above the 13-18% of the 2016 survivors on mileage, but bounded above by the 8-year 59,900 km car's 18.9%. Private after the usual ~11% step down is 15.1%; 0.151 x 2,795,000 = 420,000. Absolute sense check that the scout's figure fails: at 515,000 a private seller of a 10-year C9 would be getting MORE than a dealer asks for the newer, similar-mileage 2018 C7.5 (46.9万) - internally inconsistent. At 420,000 the car sits just under that dealer ask, which is where a 2-year-older private car belongs. Dealer trade-in set 17.9% under private; at this age many dealers will only wholesale the car. Low confidence by construction: two generations removed, and the C9 carries far more electronics (48V MHEV plus, twin OLED displays) than the C7.5 1.8T, which if anything argues the real tail is worse, not better.

maintenance.plan_notes: Scheduled-service figures come from Audi Taiwan's own published price tool, service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw ('保養透明 安心啟航'), queried per service year. The tool was re-fetched in this audit and CONFIRMED to exist and to work as described - it returns a roughly NT$1,000-wide price band per model / 年式 / 使用年份, and states that quoted prices are reference figures for 定期保養 under normal use, with the final amount depending on inspection. The specific per-year query the scout ran could NOT be reproduced here, so the figures below are reported-but-unreproduced and every checkpoint is capped at medium confidence. The C9 A6 is not yet in that database, so the closest available petrol A6 was used: A6 Avant, 2019年式, 45 TFSI quattro (same 1984cc EA888 2.0 TFSI family, same 定期保養 schedule) - note this is a quattro, so it is not a perfect proxy for a FWD car. Per-year midpoints used: y1 12,400, y2 13,600, y3 16,800, y4 13,600, y5 12,400, y6 30,200 (the big one: 自動變速箱油, 火星塞, 皮帶與調整器), y7 9,300, y8 9,300, y9 13,400, y10 9,300. INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN at this profile: the schedule is annual with a secondary kilometre trigger that 7,000 km/yr never reaches, so each checkpoint carries exactly one paid visit per year and nothing is saved by driving less. WARRANTY SHAPES THE EARLY PERIODS: Audi Taiwan gives 3 years unlimited mileage plus years 4 and 5 if under 100,000 km, and the current A6 campaign advertises 5年保固. Our buyer is at 35,000 km by year 5, so years 1-5 carry scheduled servicing and wear parts only - no repair cost. That subsidy ends there, and the years 5-7 and 7-10 periods deliberately carry the FULL unsubsidised cost: out-of-warranty repair risk, Audi dealer labour rates, 18-19 inch tyres and large brakes. Audi Taiwan's table covers scheduled servicing ONLY - tyres, brake pads and discs, the 12V AGM battery, the 48V lithium pack and the belt starter-generator, suspension wear and any repair are added on top from Taiwan parts-and-labour pricing for this class. Ten-year total is 482,000, about 48,000/yr; the scheduled portion alone is only ~140,000, so roughly 70% of lifetime maintenance is items the official table does not show. That total is far above a Japanese equivalent of this size (a Camry-class car runs roughly half), which is the correct shape for an out-of-warranty German luxury sedan. Excluded by scope: tax, insurance, fuel, tyres damaged by road hazard.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr; all checkpoints use 7,000 km/yr (7k/21k/35k/49k/70k), far below the TW average of 12,000-15,000. At this mileage every service interval is TIME-driven (Audi long-life service is 1 yr / 15,000 km, so the calendar always triggers first) and tyres age out on rubber degradation (~5-6 yrs) rather than tread wear. Tax and insurance are excluded by design: U-CAR lists this car's annual 燃料稅 6,180 + 牌照稅 11,230 (1,984cc bracket) = 17,410/yr, verified 2026-08-12 and NOT included in any figure here. LIQUIDITY WARNING that drives every confidence rating: the A7 Sportback is close to absent from the TW used market. Independently re-swept on 2026-08-12 (all 30 pages of auto.8891.com.tw/audi): 8 A7 Sportback listings with disclosed prices out of ~726 parsed Audi cars, of which only TWO are the current C8 generation with a visible price; a separate check of SUM 汽車網's full Audi inventory returned ZERO A7 mentions, and Audi Taiwan's own Approved :plus certified-used stock holds no A7. So the resale curve rests on a handful of listings and carries wide error bars in both directions - a seller may wait months for a buyer, which is itself a real cost not modelled here.

purchase.source: List price INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED on 2026-08-12 against two sites, both showing 372.5萬 for this exact trim: U-CAR newcar (https://newcar.u-car.com.tw/audi/a7%20sportback/6519/overall - table row 'A7 Sportback 45 TFSI quattro享馭版 | 372.5 | 1,984 | 汽油 | 直列4汽缸 | 七速自手排 | 四輪驅動 | 265 hp | 12.6 km/l') and Yahoo Autos 2025 model page (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-a7-sportback-2025 - trim block '45 TFSI quattro享馭版 372.5 | 1984cc | 265hp'). NT$3,725,000 CONFIRMED, no correction needed. Discount and on-road fees are estimates, reasoned in notes.
purchase.notes: POWERTRAIN - the classification trap, and it is 12V not 48V. U-CAR's spec text for this exact variant describes a '12V 輕型複合動力系統' built from a belt-driven starter-generator (BSG), a DC-DC converter and a 12V lithium battery, giving up to 5 kW of recuperation and start-stop down to 22 km/h. The 48V system in the A7 range belongs to the 55 TFSI V6, not this car ('A7 Sportback 55 TFSI 則搭載 3.0 升雙渦輪增壓 V6 引擎，搭配 48V 輕型複合動力系統'). Either way it cannot move the car on electricity alone, so this is 'gasoline'. Yahoo Autos mislabels this trim's 動力型式 as 油電混合 - verified on the page 2026-08-12, and that label is wrong. Powertrain detail: 1,984cc inline-4 TFSI turbo, 265 hp @ 5,250-6,500 rpm, 7-speed S-tronic, quattro AWD, 12.6 km/L combined, 1,815 kg, 5,021 mm long. Tyres are 245/45 R19 per U-CAR's spec table (the 255/40 R20 in that table is the 55 TFSI's) - this is a 19-inch car, which matters for the maintenance model. DISCOUNT (NT$320,000, 8.6% off list) - run-out pricing. Evidence: the C8 was revealed Oct 2017 and launched in Taiwan 2019-08-22, so the generation is ~9 years old; Yahoo carries a 2025 A7 Sportback page but requesting the 2026 page returns HTTP 404 (verified 2026-08-12) while A6 Sedan, A6 Avant, A8 and Q3 all have 2026 pages; and Audi's replacement A6 / A6 e-tron family is already on sale in TW. A slow-selling German liftback in run-out, in a bodystyle Taiwanese buyers do not want, supports a discount well above the 5% a fast-moving model would get. Audi Taiwan also runs a standing 舊換新 trade-in programme. 8.6% is deliberately conservative; a determined buyer at model-year end could plausibly do better. Note the 'lineup is down to two trims' framing needs care: U-CAR shows two A7 trims (372.5 / 414.5萬) because it files RS7 separately, while Yahoo's 2025 A7 page shows three (372.5 / 414.5 / RS7 Performance 785萬). ON-ROAD FEES (NT$75,000) = 領牌 + 代辦 (~NT$18,000) + delivery accessories appropriate to a 372萬 car (PPF / ceramic coat, window tint, dashcam, mats: ~NT$57,000). Scaled to price; excludes tax and insurance per the table's design. MODEL YEAR: labelled 2026 to match the rest of this batch because the car is on sale in Taiwan today, but TW catalogues still list it as the 2025 model year and no 2026 A7 page exists. Treat it as a run-out C8, not a fresh model year.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED from the Audi TW year-1 pattern, not from an A7 listing - no 1-year-old A7 exists on the TW market (the youngest C8 A7 found in the 2026-08-12 sweep was a 2022-registered car). Method: comparable near-new low-mileage Audis on 8891 show dealer RETAIL asks around 70% of list at 3,000-11,000 km (e.g. A4 Avant 2022 40 TFSI advanced, 11,000 km, 128.0萬 against a ~209萬 list). The A7 must sit below that: a 1-year-old competes directly against a discounted new one at 348萬, and the buyer pool for a run-out liftback is tiny. Implied dealer retail ~273萬 (73% of list); took 12% off retail for the private 自售 figure of 240萬 (8891 asks are 車商售價, never what an owner receives), then a further 14% off private for dealer trade-in. That is a 31% loss of real_cost in year one - steep, as a German luxury car should be, and nowhere near Toyota-like retention.

PARTLY ANCHORED. C8 A7 45 TFSI listings at age 3 exist on 8891 but are listed 電洽 (price withheld), so they fix the age/mileage point without giving a number - my own 2026-08-12 sweep confirms this by returning no age-3 A7 with a disclosed price. I therefore anchored on same-age Audi siblings from the same sweep and interpolated by price class, because retention falls as list price rises: Q5 2023 40 TFSI Technik 豪華版, 44,800 km, 122.9萬 (~51% of list); A6 Sedan 2022 40 TFSI Technik, 125,500 km, 82.9萬. The A7 at 372.5萬 sits above these, giving ~53% dealer retail = ~199萬. Our car also has only 21,000 km, well under the 40,000-130,000 km on the real comparables, which supports the upper half of the range. Adjusted to private sale at 12% below dealer retail (175萬) and dealer trade-in a further 15% below private. Cross-check: a real 2022-registered (age 4) A7 45 TFSI quattro享馭版 with 130,000 km asks 149.8萬 dealer retail, and a 21,000 km age-3 car sitting ~33% above that very-high-mileage car is consistent. Years 1-3 carry the steepest loss, as expected for this segment.

INTERPOLATED between the year-3 estimate and the year-7 real anchor, with one real A7 bracketing point re-verified in my own 2026-08-12 sweep: a 2022-registered (age 4) A7 Sportback 45 TFSI quattro享馭版 with 130,000 km asks 149.8萬 dealer retail on 8891 (新北市). That car has 3.7x our assumed mileage, so a 35,000 km car must sit clearly above it - used ~172萬 dealer retail. Private sale at 12% below retail = 151萬 (8891 figures are 車商售價, not owner proceeds); dealer trade-in a further 15% below private. Note the curve is deliberately flattish from year 3 to year 7: the thin TW A7 market is dominated by mileage rather than age, which the real listings show directly - the 47,000 km 2019 car asks MORE (155.8萬) than this 130,000 km 2022 car (149.8萬).

STRONGEST ANCHOR IN THIS RECORD - a real, near-perfectly matched listing, independently re-verified on 2026-08-12: Audi A7 Sportback 2019款 45 TFSI quattro 2.0L, registered 2019 (age 7), 47,000 km, asking 155.8萬 DEALER RETAIL, 高雄市. Same generation, same 45 TFSI quattro drivetrain, age 7 vs our 7, 47,000 km vs our 49,000 - and at 6,714 km/yr it is almost exactly this buyer's usage profile, so it is a genuine low-mileage comparable, not a mileage-blind average. Its original list price is now DOUBLE-SOURCED at 349萬 (U-CAR's 2019-08-22 launch report AND Yahoo Autos' 2019 and 2020 A7 model pages, which both show '45 TFSI quattro 349萬 | 1984cc'), giving 44.6% dealer-retail retention. FULL ADJUSTMENT CHAIN, stated honestly: scaling 44.6% to our higher 372.5萬 list implies ~166萬 dealer retail; I then applied a -9% nameplate/negotiation markdown to ~151萬 (single dealer asks on rare cars negotiate down, and by the time our car is 7 the A7 nameplate will be several years discontinued with a replacement generation on sale); then -12% from that dealer-retail level to the private 自售 figure of 133萬; then -15% from private for dealer trade-in = 113萬. Total gap from the scaled dealer ask to private sale is therefore ~20%, of which 12 points are the standard dealer-retail-to-private adjustment and 9 points are the named nameplate risk - the two are separate and are not both 'the dealer margin'. This is the one checkpoint with a like-for-like A7 data point, hence 'medium'.

PREDECESSOR-GENERATION EXTRAPOLATION - no 10-year-old C8 exists (the C8 launched in TW in Aug 2019, so the oldest is 7). CORRECTED: the prior version of this record applied a retention ratio against an ESTIMATED ~300萬 C7 list price which it could not verify. I verified it. Yahoo Autos' archived model pages show the C7 A7 Sportback 40 TFSI quattro - 1,984cc / 252 hp, the direct 2.0L predecessor of our 45 TFSI and precisely the car used as the age-10 comparable - listed in Taiwan at 340萬 (2017 page) and 341萬 (2018 page), NOT ~300萬. Real age-10 comparable, re-verified in my own 2026-08-12 8891 sweep: A7 Sportback 2016款 40 TFSI quattro 2.0L, registered 2016, 57,000 km, 78.8萬 dealer retail, 台南市 - the closest match on generation-role, engine and low mileage. Retention = 78.8/340 = 23.2% of list at age 10 (the old record's 26% was an artefact of the too-low denominator). Applying 23.2% to our 372.5萬 list gives ~86.3萬 dealer retail at 57,000 km. Mileage-adjusting to our 70,000 km using the two same-age C7 50 TFSI listings that differ only in mileage (70,000 km 76.8萬 vs 110,000 km 68.8萬, i.e. ~2萬 per 10,000 km) subtracts ~2.6萬, giving ~84萬 dealer retail. Private sale at 12% below that = 740,000; dealer trade-in a further 15% below private = 630,000. Note the prior record claimed 'two independent routes agree at ~96-98萬' - they were not independent, both used the same unverified 300萬. The tail keeps falling rather than flattening, which the C7 data confirms: age 13 (2013, 3.0 TFSI, 110,000 km) 45.8萬 and (2013, 2.8 FSI, 130,000 km) 29.8萬, with no Lexus-style plateau. Confidence stays 'low' because it is still a cross-generation extrapolation, but the single weakest link - the unverified predecessor list price - is now closed with a real source.

maintenance.plan_notes: SCHEDULE IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Audi's long-life service is 1 year / 15,000 km; at 7,000 km/yr this car never reaches the mileage trigger, so it is serviced annually on the calendar and reaches only 70,000 km at 10 years. The owner pays for 10 services while accumulating under 5 services' worth of wear - low mileage does NOT scale the bill down proportionally. TYRE SIZE CORRECTED: U-CAR's spec table gives 245/45 R19 for the 45 TFSI 享馭版; the 255/40 R20 in the same table belongs to the 55 TFSI. The prior version of this record budgeted 20-inch tyres at NT$60,000-70,000 per set, which overstated this trim - a 245/45 R19 premium set in Taiwan runs roughly NT$50,000-55,000. That saving has been reallocated to genuine out-of-warranty risk in the 5-7 year window, which was previously under-budgeted to the point that the year-7 period cost fell BELOW year-5. WARRANTY ASSUMPTION (flagged, not verified): assumed Audi Taiwan's standard 3-year unlimited-mileage new-car warranty, so years 0-1 and 1-3 carry routine servicing only, and every period after year 3 carries the FULL unsubsidised cost including out-of-warranty failures. www.audi.com.tw returns HTTP 503 to every fetch attempt (re-confirmed 2026-08-12), so the warranty term and all figures below are informed estimates for a German luxury dealer network in Taiwan, not quotes from an official table. If Audi TW bundles a prepaid service package, the year 0-3 figures would fall and the later ones would not change. WHY THIS IS MUCH HIGHER THAN A JAPANESE EQUIVALENT: Audi dealer labour rates, 19-inch tyres replaced on age rather than tread, oversized brakes on an 1,815 kg car, a wet-clutch 7-speed S-tronic needing its own oil-and-filter service, and EA888-family risk items after warranty - water pump / plastic thermostat housing, coil packs, PCV and valve cover. Two batteries are budgeted, not one: the main AGM starter battery plus the separate 12V lithium battery feeding the mild-hybrid BSG. Air suspension is NOT budgeted - it is not standard on the TW 45 TFSI 享馭版 (U-CAR lists 獨立五連桿 front and rear) - but if a particular car was optioned with it, add NT$60,000-120,000 per corner-pair in the 7-10 window. There is no DPF and no 48V starter-generator on this variant, so those two common German risk items do not apply. Ten-year total ~NT$660,000, roughly 2.5-3x a Japanese equivalent.

checkpoints.source: Estimated, and deliberately the largest period - a 7-10 year-old German luxury liftback out of warranty is where the real money goes, and pricing it like a RAV4's tail would be wrong. Three annual services plus a second complete tyre set (age again, not tread - the car has still done only 70,000 km in total). The water pump and plastic thermostat housing are a well-documented EA888 wear item landing squarely in this window, and coil packs typically fail as a set around this age. Suspension dampers and bushings are included because 10-year-old German chassis components perish on time in Taiwan's climate regardless of mileage, and an MMI/module line is budgeted because the electronics on this generation are a real out-of-warranty exposure. Total 10-year maintenance across all five periods is ~NT$660,000, roughly 2.5-3x a Japanese equivalent over the same period - that gap is the honest picture, not a rounding artefact.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. Every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Because mileage is so low, servicing is TIME-driven, not km-driven: the car needs an annual visit regardless, so the owner makes 10 workshop visits over 10 years but only reaches 7 km milestones (10k through 70k). Tax (牌照稅 NT$15,210 + 燃料稅 NT$7,200 per year) and insurance are excluded by design. LOW-MILEAGE PREMIUM — APPLIED ONLY WHERE IT IS NOT ALREADY IN THE COMPARABLE: at years 3, 5 and 7 the comparables carry 45,000-53,000 km against this car's 21,000-49,000 km, so a premium is warranted and stated. At year 10 it is NOT applied, because the anchor comparable is itself a 71,000 km car — essentially identical to this car's assumed 70,000 km — so a further premium would be double-counting (this was the main correction made to the researcher's record). IMPORTANT CONTEXT: Audi confirmed in March 2026 that the D5 A8 has stopped taking orders worldwide, with no successor until roughly 2030 (co-developed with the next Porsche Panamera on MSB61w). Anything bought in Taiwan today is remaining stock of a discontinued flagship, which makes the discount bigger and the residual worse than a mid-cycle car.

purchase.source: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND UNCHANGED — NT$4,500,000. Confirmed by two separate sources fetched directly: KingAutos 2024-09-21 (kingautos.net/359178) and Storm.mg (storm.mg/lifestyle/5241335) both state Taiwan Audi raised the A8 range by NT$120,000 for the 2024 model year, taking the short-wheelbase 55 TFSI quattro to NT$4,500,000 and the A8 L to NT$5,680,000. The A8 launched in Taiwan in May 2022 at NT$4,380,000; KingAutos' own lineup table and Yahoo Autos' 2023 trim page still show that stale pre-2024 figure and were NOT used. NAMING NOTE: both 2024MY articles name the NT$4,500,000 car 'A8 55 TFSI quattro S line Black', while 8891 still labels 2024 used cars '55 TFSI quattro 享馭版'; the assigned trim label is retained but the two names refer to the same NT$4,500,000 short-wheelbase car. Discount of NT$500,000 (11.1%) reflects end-of-life clearance: the D5 stopped taking orders globally in March 2026, and Taiwan Audi's March 2026 promotion sheet (auto-online, fetched and read) lists A3/A5/A6/Q3/Q5/Q7/Q8/e-tron and does not mention A8 at all. This remains the least-evidenced number in the record — no published A8 購車菜單 was found — but for unsold flagship stock in a market that moves a handful of A8s a year it is realistic and arguably conservative.

POWERTRAIN CLASSIFICATION: this car carries Audi's 48V MHEV (輕型複合動力) belt-alternator starter system. It cannot move the car on battery alone, so it is correctly classified 'gasoline' here, and this was checked rather than inherited — Audi's own Approved :plus listing states '48V Mild hybrid' and the Yahoo 2021 copy says '48V輕型複合動力系統'. Note that KingAutos, 8891 and SUM all mislabel it '油電混合(HEV)' in their spec tables — that is a data-entry convention on their side, not a series hybrid. onroad_fees NT$90,000 = 領牌 + 代辦 ~NT$20,000, top-tier full-car window film ~NT$45,000 (large glass area on a flagship), paint coating ~NT$25,000. Scaled to the price class; tax and insurance excluded. Taiwan's 特種貨物及勞務稅 (luxury tax) on cars was abolished in 2016, so no extra levy applies above NT$3M.

UNCHANGED — verified independently and the listings are real. CORRECTED — the researcher's NT$700,000 / NT$590,000 double-counted the low-mileage premium and is revised down by ~21%. EXTRAPOLATED: no genuine 10-year data exists for the current D5 generation, which only launched in Taiwan in 2018, so per method this uses the PREDECESSOR D4 generation's retention ratio applied to this car's cost. Real D4 data verified on the 8891 page fetched directly: an A8 50 TFSI quattro at 71,000 km asks NT$580,000 and one at 112,000 km asks NT$498,000 — both are 2016 cars (the researcher recorded them as 2015; a 2016 car is in fact exactly ten years old in 2026, so the comparable is better than claimed). THE KEY FIX: the NT$580,000 car is a 71,000 km car, essentially identical to this car's assumed 70,000 km at year 10, so its 13.7% ALREADY IS the low-mileage figure — the researcher's further +20% premium on top was double-counting. Applying 13.7-14% with no extra premium gives ~NT$625,000 dealer-retail equivalent; private = 12% below = NT$550,000; trade-in = 15% below private = NT$465,000. Cross-check: real asking prices fall from NT$1,050,000 for a 7-year-old D5 to NT$580,000 for a 10-year-old D4, a ~45% drop, and this checkpoint drops 50% from year 7 — appropriate for an orphaned flagship carrying air suspension and 48V electronics with no factory successor. Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

maintenance.plan_notes: Built from Audi Taiwan's OFFICIAL published service price table (service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw), whose underlying data endpoint was fetched and read directly during this check. The exact variant row 'Audi A8 / 55 TFSI quattro / Petrol' (2021) was CONFIRMED VERBATIM: 10,000 km NT$13,900-14,900 / 20,000 km NT$24,400-25,400 / 30,000 km NT$17,700-18,700 / 40,000 km NT$24,400-25,400 / 50,000 km NT$13,900-14,900 / 60,000 km NT$100,200-101,200 / 70,000 km NT$13,900-14,900. Midpoints are used. The separate 'Audi A8 L 55 TFSI quattro Premium' (2022) row at NT$9,500-10,500 also exists and was confirmed, but it is a different, long-wheelbase model line and is treated as a lower bound only; the exact short-wheelbase variant match is used. The service matrix drives those steps: oil + oil filter + cabin filter every 10,000 km; brake fluid + SPARK PLUGS every 20,000 km; air filter every 30,000 km; AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION OIL every 60,000 km — which is why the 60,000 km visit is NT$100,700 and, at 7,000 km/year, lands at year 8.6, squarely in the 7-10 year window. AT ONLY 7,000 km/YEAR THE INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: the car needs an annual service regardless, so there are 10 visits across 10 years but only 7 km milestones; the 3 extra visits are time-based oil-and-filter services billed at roughly the base rate. WARRANTY — CORRECTED: the researcher assumed a 五年原廠保固 running to year 5 and therefore carried NO repair allowance in the 3-5 year window. Fetching Taiwan Audi's March 2026 programme (auto-online) shows the A8 IS NOT LISTED in it — the table covers A3/A5/A6/Q3/Q5/Q7/Q8/e-tron only. The 5-year cover cannot be assumed for A8, so this record works from standard cover expiring around year 3 and adds an out-of-warranty allowance from the 3-5 year window onward. Later-period items reflect what actually breaks on this car in Taiwan: the standard adaptive AIR SUSPENSION (an entire Taiwanese repair industry exists around Audi/A8 air struts — CG 氣壓避震器 and M&B Power both document A8 front-strut leaks as routine work), the EA839 3.0 TFSI water pump / thermostat housing / coil packs, the 48V mild-hybrid lithium battery and belt starter-generator, and two sets of 265/40R20 tires (Michelin PS4S at this size runs ~NT$11,500-15,000 each fitted in Taiwan). AIR SUSPENSION ALSO CORRECTED: the researcher budgeted two struts at NT$50,000 total using independent-specialist rates only, which is the cheapest possible path on this car's single most notorious failure item; it is re-weighted to NT$90,000 to blend specialist and dealer OEM pricing. Sanity check: NT$727,000 over 10 years = ~NT$72,700/year, consistent with and slightly above the PTT owner consensus of '年抓5萬/yr' for an out-of-warranty A8 once tires and the NT$100,700 ATF service are included, and far above any Japanese equivalent — as it should be.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; all checkpoints use the 7,000 km/year midpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km). That is roughly half the Taiwan average, so servicing is TIME-driven (one annual visit) rather than mileage-driven, and the mileage milestones in Audi Taiwan's official price table arrive far later in calendar time than for an average-mileage owner — the 60,000 km major service lands around year 9 rather than year 4. Used-value estimates therefore quote low-mileage listings, which sit above the mileage-blind average for this model, and every value source string names the specific low-mileage comparables used. Annual road tax (牌照稅 NT$7,120 for the 1,498 cc band) and fuel tax (燃料稅 NT$4,800), plus all insurance, are EXCLUDED by design and appear nowhere in purchase, maintenance or selling costs. Fuel/energy cost is also out of scope. Two market facts shape this record. (1) THE 2026 PRICE RESET, now verified trim-by-trim in this pass rather than asserted. Audi Taiwan collapsed the Q2 range from five trims to two with the 2026年式 launched 2026-03-05. Verified on Yahoo Autos model pages I fetched myself: the 2024 lineup was 35 TFSI 享馭版 NT$1,560,000 / Technik 豪華版 NT$1,620,000 / Advanced 進化版 NT$1,740,000 / S-Line 運動版 NT$1,840,000 / SQ2 NT$2,450,000, and the 2022 lineup was 享馭版 NT$1,510,000 / Technik 豪華版 NT$1,570,000 / Technik 旅型特仕 NT$1,670,000 / Advanced 進化版 NT$1,690,000 / S-Line 運動版 NT$1,790,000 / SQ2 NT$2,390,000. The 2026 lineup is Advanced 進化版 NT$1,399,000 / S line 運動版 NT$1,699,000. So the entry price fell NT$161,000 (-10.3%) and the car wearing the 'advanced 進化版' badge fell NT$341,000 (-19.6%) — though the badge moved down the range, so the honest reading is that the 2026 advanced sits between the old 享馭版 and the old 進化版 on content while carrying Matrix LED and the 8.8-inch MMI as standard. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the reviewed record, which stated the previous entry was NT$1,560,000 and implied that was the same trim: NT$1,560,000 was the 享馭版, not the 進化版. Note also that the Carture launch report does NOT itself announce a price cut; the cut is established by comparing the verified 2024 and 2026 lineups, not by any single article. This reset has ALREADY re-priced the live used Q2 market, so the Aug 2026 listings quoted below are post-cut market-cleared prices and the 2026 buyer starts from the lower base. The cut must be counted ONCE, not twice. (2) The Q2 is widely reported to be ending production in 2026 with no direct successor. I could NOT independently verify that claim in this pass (web-search budget exhausted; the Carture launch coverage I re-read makes no mention of it), so it is treated as a soft downward factor on the tail — a single-digit percentage haircut from year 5 on — rather than as an established fact. If the nameplate in fact continues, the year 5-10 values are slightly conservative.

purchase.source: 官方建議售價 NT$1,399,000, re-verified again in this pass on two sources I fetched myself: Yahoo Autos 2026 Q2 model page (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-q2-2026) shows 35 TFSI Advanced進化版 139.9萬 and 35 TFSI S-Line運動版 169.9萬, 1,498 cc, 150 hp; Carture launch report (https://www.carture.com.tw/news/article/39840) shows NT$1,399,000 / NT$1,699,000 with a 2026-03-05 on-sale date and no announced incentive. List price unchanged. Discount and on-road fees are estimates, justified in notes.
purchase.notes: COST BASIS — DIRECT ANSWER TO THE REVIEWER'S QUESTION. real_cost NT$1,382,000 is NOT the list price. It is 1,399,000 - 65,000 discount + 48,000 on-road fees. It lands within 1.2% of list only because the on-road fees very nearly cancel the discount, which is the same arithmetic every sibling record in this batch uses (A3: 1,580,000 - 70,000 + 52,000 = 1,562,000, also 98.9% of list; Q3: 1,910,000 - 40,000 + 45,000 = 1,915,000, 100.3% of list). So the 'list price used as cost while quoting real-world resale' failure mode the reviewer suspected is NOT what happened here — the discount is applied, and the cost basis is constructed identically to the siblings the Q2 was being compared against. The year-1 error was entirely on the resale side and is corrected in value_checkpoints. POWERTRAIN: 1.5 TFSI (1,498 cc) inline-4 turbo petrol, 150 hp, 7-speed S tronic dual-clutch (DQ200 dry-clutch), front-wheel drive. NO 48V mild-hybrid system and no electric drive of any kind — a pure combustion car, correctly classified 'gasoline'. Its only efficiency aid is 主動式汽缸管理 (cylinder-on-demand), which deactivates cylinders but cannot move the car on electricity. Audi Taiwan's Q3 does use a 1.5+48V setup; the Q2 does not, so no 48V starter-generator is carried into the maintenance plan (a real difference from the sibling A3 record in this batch, which does carry a 48V BSG provision). MODEL YEAR: 2026年式, on sale in Taiwan from 2026-03-05, range simplified from five trims to two 35 TFSI trims (advanced 進化版 NT$1,399,000 / S line 運動版 NT$1,699,000) with Matrix LED headlights and an 8.8-inch MMI touchscreen now standard. DISCOUNT NT$65,000: two forces pull in opposite directions. Upward — a slow-selling entry SUV reportedly in run-out, on which Audi Taiwan runs cash-equivalent programmes (low monthly payment plans, body-insurance subsidies). Downward — Audi Taiwan has just taken NT$161,000 off the entry price at the factory level, and a freshly re-priced model normally leaves dealers LESS room to discount, because the cut IS the discount. NT$65,000 is 4.6% of list, in line with the 4.4% used on the mechanically near-identical Audi A3 35 TFSI advanced in this same batch. A real quote could land anywhere from NT$40,000 to NT$100,000; at the top of that range real_cost would fall to NT$1,347,000 and every retention ratio below would rise about 2.5 points. This is an estimate, not a published figure; the launch coverage I verified announces no incentive. ON-ROAD FEES NT$48,000 = 領牌 government fees and plates (~NT$1,500-1,900), dealer 代辦費 (~NT$5,000), and accessories typical for this class (window film ~NT$15,000, dashcam ~NT$10,000, mats/trays ~NT$5,000, paint coating ~NT$11,000). Scales correctly against the batch (A3 at NT$1,580,000 carries NT$52,000). Tax and insurance excluded by design. REAL COST = 1,399,000 - 65,000 + 48,000 = 1,382,000.

value_checkpoints.source: RAISED from NT$835,000 private / NT$725,000 trade-in after re-sourcing this row, which is what the reviewer asked for. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE OLD 60% FIGURE — it was neither a run-out transaction price nor a 領牌車 sale, as hypothesised; it was an AGE-SLOT ERROR. The previous pass anchored year 1 on two SUM listings I re-verified again in this pass (https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/AUDI/Q2?v=4): a 2024 Q2 with 8,000 km at NT$928,000 and a 2024 Q2 with 6,338 km at NT$958,000. In Aug 2026 a 2024 model-year car is roughly TWO years old, not one. Those cars were placed in the 1-year slot at their face value, which silently charged the buyer two years of depreciation in the first year and produced the 60% outlier the reviewer flagged. Both listings are still live and their prices are confirmed — the data was right, the age slot was wrong. RE-DERIVED LADDER, in absolute post-cut NT$ against the current NT$1,399,000 new price: 2 years ~NT$940,000 dealer retail (the two 2024 cars above, both genuinely low-mileage at 3,000-4,000 km/year, exactly the profile of this buyer); 4 years NT$768,000 dealer retail (2022 Q2 35 TFSI, 29,251 km, verified on https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2). Stepping the 2-year point back one year at a typical 11-13% year-two decline for a German compact gives ~NT$1,070,000 DEALER RETAIL asking at 1 year / 7,000 km, i.e. 76% of the NT$1,399,000 list — a normal 1-year-old dealer asking level, and it makes the ladder 76% / 67% / 55% of list at 1 / 2 / 4 years, which is smooth and monotonic where the old figure put 1 year and 2 years at the same place. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED (dealer retail is NOT what the owner gets): private sale = dealer retail minus 11% = NT$950,000; dealer trade-in = private minus 13% = NT$825,000. That is a 31.3% first-year loss against real_cost (68.7% retention) — still the weakest of the three compact Audis in this batch (A3 72%, Q3 73%), which is right for a run-out entry model whose factory price was just cut, but no longer the A8/Q6-e-tron-class collapse the reviewer objected to, and it restores the front-loaded shape: the 1-to-3 step is now 19 points, steeper than the A3's 13 and in line with the Q3's 18. CONFIDENCE stays medium and not high: there is NO 2025 model-year Q2 listed on FindCar, SUM or 8891 in Aug 2026, so no genuine 1-year-old comparable exists — this figure is a one-year step off real 2-year-old listings, not a direct observation.

Not objected to by the reviewer; re-checked in this pass and left unchanged. Anchored on low-mileage mid-age cars re-verified on FindCar (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2): a 2022 Q2 35 TFSI (4 years old) with 29,251 km at DEALER RETAIL NT$768,000, against a 2022 Q2 with 83,000 km at NT$628,000 — the NT$140,000 spread between them is the low-mileage premium this buyer earns. NEW FACT from this pass: the 2022 lineup is now verified on the Yahoo Autos 2022 model page (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/model/audi-q2-2022) as 享馭版 NT$1,510,000 through Advanced 進化版 NT$1,690,000, so that 4-year-old car retains 45-51% of its own original list at dealer retail depending on trim, and 55% of the current NT$1,399,000 new price. Blending the ratio transferred onto the lower NT$1,399,000 base with the absolute market level, and stepping back one year to age 3, gives ~NT$770,000 DEALER RETAIL asking for a 3-year-old 2026 advanced at 21,000 km. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = dealer retail minus 11% = NT$685,000; trade-in = private minus 13% = NT$595,000. Years 0-3 carry NT$697,000 of loss against real_cost, the front-loaded German pattern. The 3-year unlimited-mileage factory warranty expires exactly here, which is part of why the year 3-5 step stays large. Note this row sits at 49.6% of real_cost, BELOW both compact siblings (A3 58.9%, Q3 55.1%) — so the reviewer's impression that the Q2's later figures were 'among the strongest in the brand' holds only against the flagships and BEVs, which fall harder for their own reasons; against its actual peers the Q2 tail is the weaker one, and raising year 1 was the correct fix rather than lowering years 3-10.

Not objected to by the reviewer; re-checked in this pass and left unchanged. Anchored on a real 5-year-old low-mileage facelift car re-verified on both SUM and FindCar: 2021 Q2 35 TFSI with 23,500 km at DEALER RETAIL NT$768,000, with a 2021 Q2 with 50,000 km also at NT$768,000 as a same-age higher-mileage check (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2, https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/AUDI/Q2?v=4) — the two asking the same money despite double the mileage is a reminder that asking prices on this nameplate are noisy. Those cars listed around NT$1,510,000-1,690,000 new, i.e. 45-51% of their own list at 5 years at dealer retail asking, and 55% of the current new price. Applying that to the NT$1,399,000 base gives ~NT$676,000, less a ~5% haircut for the nameplate reportedly being out of production by then, so ~NT$640,000 DEALER RETAIL asking at 5 years / 35,000 km. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = dealer retail minus 11% = NT$570,000; trade-in = private minus 13% = NT$495,000. The comparable is ALSO out of warranty at 5 years, so no extra out-of-warranty penalty is applied on top — that would be double-counting. At 41.2% of real_cost this sits level with the Q3 (41.8%) and below the A3 (47.7%).

Not objected to by the reviewer; re-checked in this pass and left unchanged. EXTRAPOLATED — there is no 7-year-old example of THIS specification, because the 1.5 TFSI facelift only reached Taiwan in 2021-2022. Proxy = same-nameplate, same-generation pre-facelift cars (the Q2 is a single generation, 2016-2026), expressed as a retention ratio of their own original list and then applied to this car's lower base. Aug 2026 DEALER RETAIL asking, re-verified on FindCar and SUM in this pass: 2019 Q2 with 66,048 km NT$528,000; 2019 with 89,000 km NT$508,000; 2019 with 90,000 km NT$458,000; 2019 with 121,945 km NT$388,000; 2019 with 146,516 km NT$378,000 (https://www.findcar.com.tw/datalist.aspx?u=1&q=Audi%20Q2, https://www.sum.com.tw/carsearch/AUDI/Q2?v=4). The mileage gradient across that set is the low-mileage premium made explicit. Those 2019s listed at roughly NT$1,440,000-1,590,000 new, so the best-kept 66,000 km car is at ~35% of list at 7 years. Our car has only 49,000 km — below every one of those comparables — worth roughly +8%, so ~38%, applied to NT$1,399,000 = ~NT$532,000, less ~5% for the dead nameplate = ~NT$505,000 DEALER RETAIL asking. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private = dealer retail minus 11% = NT$450,000; trade-in = private minus 13% = NT$390,000. Not objected to by the reviewer; re-checked in this pass and left unchanged. EXTRAPOLATED, the weakest row in this record. maintenance.plan_notes: The reviewer raised no maintenance objection, so no figure below is changed — but the official baseline was re-fetched and re-verified from scratch in this pass, and it holds. BASELINE IS AN OFFICIAL TABLE. Audi Taiwan publishes per-model scheduled-maintenance pricing at https://service-pricing.audi-service.com.tw. I fetched the data API again and enumerated EVERY Q2 row it returns, which is worth recording because the table is model-year-banded and the bands differ sharply: 2018 Q2 35 TFSI (10k NT$9,400-10,400 / 20k 10,500-11,500 / 30k 14,000-15,000 / 40k 9,900-10,900 / 50k 10,000-11,000 / 60k 19,900-20,900 / 70k 9,400-10,400); 2019 (8,600-9,600 / 9,800-10,800 / 11,500-12,500 / 9,800-10,800 / 8,600-9,600 / 19,900-20,900 / 8,600-9,600); 2020 (8,700-9,700 / 13,700-14,700 / 10,200-11,200 / 13,700-14,700 / 8,700-9,700 / 17,900-18,900 / 8,700-9,700); 2021 (8,700-9,700 / 13,600-14,600 / 10,200-11,200 / 13,600-14,600 / 8,700-9,700 / 17,800-18,800 / 8,700-9,700); and three 2022 rows — 35 TFSI Premium, Premium Plus and S line — all at 10k NT$6,000-7,000 / 20k 7,300-8,300 / 30k 7,600-8,600 / 40k 7,300-8,300 / 50k 6,000-7,000 / 60k 23,800-24,800 / 70k 6,000-7,000. THE 2022 ROWS ARE THE NEWEST Q2 ENTRIES IN THE TABLE and are the ones used here, which is the right choice for a 2026 car: same 1.5 TFSI, same S tronic. Audi Taiwan restructured the schedule at 2022 — routine visits got materially cheaper and the 60,000 km transmission visit got materially dearer. The reviewed record cited exactly these 2022 figures and its own source note already corrected the label to '35 TFSI Premium'; both are confirmed correct. I also re-fetched the official service matrix and confirmed the item schedule: engine oil + oil filter + washers/seals + cabin dust filter every 10,000 km; brake fluid AND spark plugs every 20,000 km; air filter every 30,000 km; automatic (S tronic) transmission oil + sealing plug at 60,000 km, which is why that visit triples in price; V-belt and tensioner at 120,000 km, never reached here. TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: at 7,000 km/year the annual clock always beats the odometer, so the owner makes about one visit per year (~10 visits over 10 years) but only reaches 70,000 km. The 60,000 km major service is crossed at year 8.6, so it falls in the 7-10 window, not at year 4 as it would for an average-mileage owner. That is genuine good news for this buyer and it has not been inflated away — years 1 and 3 really are cheap. Brake fluid on VAG cars is a TIME item (every 2 years) as well as a mileage item, so it recurs on the calendar even when the 20,000 km milestones are years apart. WARRANTY: 3 years unlimited mileage, so years 0-3 carry scheduled servicing only. I found NO confirmed free-maintenance or prepaid service package bundled with the 2026 Q2 — the Carture launch report, re-read in this pass, announces no incentive, free maintenance or extended warranty — so every service below is modelled as fully paid. WHAT THE OFFICIAL TABLE DOES NOT COVER, and what is added here: tyres, brake pads and discs, 12V battery, coolant, suspension wear, and out-of-warranty failure risk. This car's specific exposure is the DQ200 7-speed DRY-clutch S tronic, a well-known VAG weak point whose mechatronic/clutch-pack replacement runs NT$70,000-120,000 at a dealer, plus the EA211 evo 1.5 TFSI water-pump/thermostat housing module, coil packs and age-driven oil-seal leaks. Years 5-10 carry probability-weighted provisions for these. The 10-year total is NT$445,000: the lowest in the German batch, which is right — the Q2 is the smallest and cheapest car in it, wears smaller brakes, and legitimately drops the 48V starter-generator provision its A3 sibling carries — while still sitting in the same league as the A3's NT$506,000 on the identical platform, engine and gearbox. NOT INCLUDED, on purpose: no 48V starter-generator (this is not a mild hybrid), no air suspension (not fitted to the Q2), no DPF (petrol). Later-period labour assumes a realistic mix of Audi dealer and independent VAG specialist; staying 100% at the dealer for 10 years would push the year 7-10 figure roughly NT$30,000-40,000 higher.

Note the 2022-onward Q2 rows price that 60,000 km visit at NT$23,800-24,800 against NT$17,800-20,900 on the 2018-2021 rows — the newer schedule front-loads savings and back-loads this one visit, which is exactly why it lands so heavily in this window. assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; midpoint 7,000 km/year at every checkpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km), roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. It is roughly three months old today, so no used example of THIS generation exists at any age and the year-1 point is necessarily extrapolated. purchase.source: LIST PRICE CONFIRMED, UNCHANGED at NT$1,910,000. The car therefore launched NT$40,000 below its own pre-sale figure, which matters downstream: the window sticker is already sharpened and leaves less room to negotiate. The 8891 新車 page (c.8891.com.tw/audi/q3/Summary.html) was fetched but is fully client-rendered and returned only its title, so it corroborates that the 2026 Q3 is the current listed model but did NOT independently confirm the number. audi.com.tw returned HTTP 403/503 on every attempt and no figure was taken from it. purchase.notes: POWERTRAIN: classified 'gasoline', which is correct under this table's rules and is left unchanged. The 1.5 TFSI evo2 in this 110 kW trim carries a 48V mild-hybrid system (Audi MHEV / MHEV plus) with a belt starter-generator: it recuperates, allows engine-off coasting and smooths stop/start, but cannot move the car on electricity alone, so it is NOT a hybrid here. The kW-based trim nomenclature is itself corroborating evidence — Audi Taiwan applied the same naming to the third-generation Q5 ('TFSI 150 kW advanced 進化版'), whose Taiwan spec sheet does print 48V MHEV plus. A Taiwan-spec Q3 technical page could not be retrieved directly (audi.com.tw 403/503), so the 48V hardware remains probable-but-unconfirmed; it is load-bearing only for one risk line in the 7-10 year maintenance window. DISCOUNTS: NT$40,000 (2.1%) is deliberately modest and is retained. This is the entry trim of a generation three months into its Taiwan life, which is where importers hold price hardest, and the list price already came in NT$40,000 under pre-sale. The launch campaign is structured as sweeteners — financing packages and a 月付9,999 plan — rather than cash off the sticker. For comparison, the Q5 record in this same table uses 3.3% on a generation ten months old; a fresher car gets less. ON-ROAD FEES REDUCED from NT$60,000 to NT$45,000. The prior draft's figure was NT$20,000 higher than the Audi Q5's in this same table despite the Q5 being a NT$490,000 more expensive car from the same dealer network, which inverts the rule that fees scale with price. NT$45,000 = 領牌+代辦 of roughly NT$10,000 (新領牌照登記規費、驗車、車籍代辦) plus about NT$35,000 of near-compulsory accessories at this class (隔熱紙, 行車記錄器, 腳踏墊/門檻條, 鍍膜). Tax and insurance excluded by design. real_cost = 1,910,000 - 40,000 + 45,000 = 1,915,000. LABEL: display trim shortened to fit the field; the full Taiwan designation is Audi Q3 TFSI 110 kW advanced 進化版, the front-wheel-drive entry model in a range that also runs up to TFSI quattro 150 kW S line.

selling_costs.notes: Costs the seller bears to complete a PRIVATE sale; reviewed this pass and left unchanged. The 過戶 regulatory fee itself is small (about NT$1,200) but 代辦 handling pushes it to ~NT$2,500. Pre-sale detailing is the largest line: a German premium SUV has to present well or the private-sale premium over trade-in evaporates, so NT$7,000 for interior/exterior clean, polish and coating is realistic at this class. A paid 8891 自售 listing with exposure boost runs ~NT$2,000. Total NT$11,500 sits in the normal 6,000-15,000 band for this segment and matches the Audi Q5 record's NT$13,000 allowing for the smaller car. A dealer trade-in would avoid the listing fee and most of the detailing, which is part of why the trade-in figures below sit well under private sale. Estimated from typical Taiwan practice, not from a retrieved price list.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED — the third-generation Q3 launched in Taiwan in May 2026, so the oldest example on the road today is about three months old and no one-year-old car of this generation can exist. Derived by working BACKWARDS from real predecessor data rather than from a generic retention rule: 8891 (auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q3, read 2026-08-12) lists a 2024 Q3 35 TFSI 享馭版 at 3,020 km — essentially delivery mileage on a two-year-old car — asking 127.8萬 車商售價, plus 2024 cars at 15,000 km / 119.8萬 and 16,400 km (40 TFSI quattro S line) / 146.8萬. Against an F3 base-family list of roughly 172萬 that near-delivery two-year-old holds ~74% of list at DEALER RETAIL; unwinding one year at the segment's ~10-11%/yr puts year-one dealer retail at ~84% of list. That independently reproduces the 84-86% year-one dealer-retail retention actually OBSERVED on current-generation Q5s in the sibling record, so 84% is used. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN (this is the step that matters — every 8891 figure quoted anywhere in this record is 車商售價, dealer RETAIL asking, never what an owner receives): 84% x 191萬 = 160.4萬 dealer retail; private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 141萬, rounded to 140萬; dealer trade-in (車商收購) = private MINUS 13% = 121.5萬. Cross-checked as an upper bound only against live Audi 原廠認證中古車 stock retrieved from approvedplus.audi.com.tw on 2026-08-12 (Q2 掛牌2024/11 7,679 km 108.8萬; Q5 Sportback 掛牌2025/2 13,801 km 176.8萬) — those are CPO retail asks, which sit ABOVE ordinary dealer retail because they carry a factory warranty, so they cap rather than set this figure. Low confidence: no current-generation used car exists to observe.

UPGRADED to medium — real predecessor listings were retrievable after all. EXTRAPOLATED from the direct predecessor (F3 Q3, TW 2020-2025) using its OBSERVED 8891 車商售價 at this age, read 2026-08-12 across auto.8891.com.tw/audi/q3 pages 1-3. Three-year cohort (2023 cars): 35 TFSI @ 40,000 km = 99.8萬; 35 TFSI advanced @ 70,000 km = 90.0萬; 40 TFSI quattro S line @ 30,000 km = 133.8萬. The 133.8萬 row is deliberately NOT used as the anchor — page 3 identifies it as the top quattro S line trim, so treating it as a base-trim comparable would import a whole trim step as if it were age. Using the two 35 TFSI rows gives a mileage slope of ~0.33萬 per 1,000 km, which extended down to this buyer's 21,000 km lands at ~106萬 for the predecessor. Sanity-checked from the other direction: the 2024 (two-year) 35 TFSI cluster sits at ~120-128萬, and one further year at ~12%/yr gives ~106-113萬. Take 106萬. GENERATION SCALING: this car lists at 191萬 against roughly 172萬 for the late-life F3 base family, a factor of ~1.11, giving ~118萬 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 103.8萬; rounded to 105.5萬 to reflect that this buyer's 21,000 km sits at the very bottom of the observed cohort's mileage range; dealer trade-in = private MINUS 13.3% = 91.5萬. Years 1-3 are the steepest stretch for a German car in Taiwan — retention falls from ~73% to ~55% of real_cost across two years, against ~67-69% for the Lexus NX at the same age in this table. Medium rather than high: the figures are real and per-car, but they are the PREDECESSOR generation and the F3 list price used as the scaling denominator is itself unverified.

UPGRADED to medium. EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor F3 generation's observed five-year cohort (2021 cars) on 8891, read 2026-08-12: 35 TFSI @ 20,000 km = 80.8萬; @ 60,000 km = 75.0萬; 35 TFSI 享馭版 @ 67,000 km = 71.8萬 (all 車商售價). Three cars spanning 20,000-67,000 km give a shallow but consistent slope; this buyer's 35,000 km interpolates to ~79萬 for the predecessor. Note the cohort is genuinely low-dispersion at this age, unlike the Q5's, so a cohort read is safe here. GENERATION SCALING x1.11 = ~87.7萬 dealer retail for this car. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 77.2萬, rounded up to 80萬 because 35,000 km is at the bottom edge of the observed mileage band and this segment does pay a visible premium for it; dealer trade-in = private MINUS 13.8% = 69萬. Year five is where any launch-campaign warranty has lapsed under every reading and the Taiwan market starts pricing repair risk into a German turbo SUV, so the curve does not flatten the way the Lexus NX does at the same age (58.4% of real_cost there against 41.8% here). The 35,000 km reading is roughly half what a typical five-year-old Q3 shows, and that premium is already embedded via the interpolation rather than added again on top. Medium: real per-car predecessor data, but cross-generation transfer with an unverified scaling denominator.

EXTRAPOLATED and INTERPOLATED — the weakest of the mid-life points. No seven-year data can exist for this generation, and the predecessor F3 launched in Taiwan in 2020, so a genuine seven-year F3 cohort (2019 cars) does not appear in the 8891 result set either. The point is therefore bracketed between two observed cohorts read 2026-08-12: the F3 five-year cohort above (2021 cars, ~79萬 at 35,000 km) and the 8U eight-year cohort (2018 cars: @ 70,000 km = 52.0萬; 30 TFSI @ 66,000 km and a stated 2018 band of 45.8-51.3萬 at 54,000-83,000 km). A seven-year F3 at this buyer's 49,000 km sits above the 8U band, because the F3 is a newer and better-equipped generation than the 8U, and below the five-year cohort: ~63-66萬 for the predecessor, take 64萬. GENERATION SCALING x1.11 = ~71萬 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 62.5萬, rounded to 63萬; dealer trade-in = private MINUS 14.3% = 54萬, a wider cut than at earlier ages because dealers increasingly wholesale rather than retail an out-of-warranty German SUV. The German tail keeps falling here rather than levelling — 32.9% of real_cost against the Lexus NX's 45.3% at the same age — because the buyer pool for a seven-year-old Audi SUV in Taiwan thins sharply once the market prices in the failure items itemised in the maintenance plan. Low confidence: this is an interpolation ACROSS two different generations rather than an observed cohort.

EXTRAPOLATED from the GRANDPARENT 8U generation (TW 2013-2018), the only Q3 cohort old enough to be ten years on the road today. Real 8891 車商售價 read 2026-08-12: 2017 30 TFSI @ 77,000 km = 49.8萬; 2017 @ 127,000 km = 39.8萬; 2017 @ 141,500 km = 29.9萬; 2016-2017 band stated as 32.9-41.8萬 at 80,000-140,000 km; 2015 @ 113,000 km = 39.8萬; 2015 30 TFSI @ 121,000 km = 38.8萬; 2015 @ 122,100 km = 36.8萬; 2014 @ 126,300 km = 23.9萬; 2013 2.0 TFSI quattro @ 116,000 km = 19.8萬. The 2017 pair (77,000 km / 49.8萬 versus 127,000 km / 39.8萬) gives a usable mileage slope of ~2萬 per 10,000 km at this age. This buyer's 70,000 km on a ten-year-old car is genuinely exceptional against the 110,000-140,000 km norm visible throughout this cohort, so the estimate sits at the top of the observed band: ~46萬 for the 8U. GENERATION SCALING is larger here (~x1.18) because the 8U listed around 162萬 against this car's 191萬, giving ~54萬 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN: private sale = dealer retail MINUS 12% = 47.5萬; dealer trade-in = private MINUS 15.8% = 40萬, the widest cut in the record because at ten years many Taiwan dealers will only wholesale an Audi SUV rather than retail it, and some will decline the trade entirely — in which case 400,000 is optimistic. Cross-checked against the oldest real Audi price retrieved from Audi's own CPO channel (A4 Avant 掛牌2016/12, 73,355 km, 88.8萬 on approvedplus.audi.com.tw), a larger and more expensive model carrying a factory warranty, which is consistent with a mid-20s-percent private-sale retention for a well-kept ten-year-old Audi and is why this figure was not pushed lower. Retention keeps eroding from 32.9% to 24.8% between years 7 and 10 — no flattening. Low: two generations back, and at this age condition and service history dominate both age and mileage.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. Audi Taiwan's interval is 1 year or 15,000 km, whichever comes first; at 7,000 km/year this car never reaches the distance trigger, so every period below is a count of ANNUAL dealer visits and the car covers only 70,000 km across the whole ten years. Low mileage saves far less than owners expect — oil, filters, brake fluid and coolant all age out on the calendar, and even the tyres are replaced for age rather than wear. The only items genuinely deferred are brake pads and discs. WARRANTY — DOWNGRADED FROM THE PRIOR DRAFT AND NO LONGER LOAD-BEARING. That draft treated a five-year factory warranty (五年原廠保固) as established fact and used it to justify deliberately low years 1-5 figures. It could not be confirmed this pass: audi.com.tw returns HTTP 403/503 on every path, and the UDN result set that was fetched confirms the launch price and pre-sale price but returns no warranty term. Audi Taiwan's long-published standard is 3 years unlimited mileage, with five-year cover normally sold as an extended-warranty product or run as a time-limited launch campaign — which is exactly how the sibling Q5 record in this table treats it. This record therefore assumes years 1-3 covered, years 3-5 probably-but-not-certainly covered, and everything from year 5 fully out of warranty, and it does not rely on any five-year claim. No free scheduled maintenance is bundled into the Taiwan price; Audi TW sells 原廠保養套餐 as an optional prepaid add-on, so every service below is paid. TOTAL REBASED to about NT$392,000 over ten years, down from the prior draft's NT$504,000. The prior figure was internally inconsistent with this same table: it put a 1.5-litre front-drive compact Audi ABOVE the larger, NT$490,000 more expensive 2.0-litre Q5 (NT$404,000) at every later period, from the same dealer network at the same labour rate. The Q3 wears smaller brakes and 18-inch rather than 19-inch tyres and carries a smaller engine, so it must sit modestly BELOW the Q5, not 25% above it. At NT$392,000 it is still roughly 1.45x the Lexus NX (NT$271,000) and 1.6x the Toyota RAV4 (NT$244,000) in this same table, which is the correct German-versus-Japanese outcome. WHAT DRIVES THE LATER NUMBERS: Audi dealer labour in Taiwan runs roughly double a Japanese franchise, and the risk items costed in years 5-10 are the ones this engine family is actually known for — thermostat housing, electric water pump, ignition coils, PCV/valve cover seepage — plus the S tronic dual-clutch service and, uniquely to this powertrain, the 48V lithium battery and belt starter-generator. Air suspension is deliberately NOT costed: it is not offered on the Q3, which sits on a conventional MQB strut/multilink setup. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: no Audi Taiwan service price table could be retrieved (audi.com.tw 403/503) and Mobile01 owner-receipt threads returned HTTP 403, so every figure is a structured dealer-norm build-up, not a quoted invoice — hence all five checkpoints remain low.

checkpoints.source: The first expensive window, and it is consumables rather than repairs. Tyres dominate: at 7,000 km/year the original set reaches only ~35,000 km with tread remaining, but rubber ages out at 5-6 years and is replaced anyway — a set of four in 235/50 R18 for a compact premium SUV in Taiwan runs NT$30,000-38,000, below the NT$36,000-48,000 a 19-inch Q5 set costs. Front pads and the AGM 12V battery typically fall due in the same window. Repairs assumed still covered on the five-year reading and largely covered on the three-year reading, so no explicit failure allowance is carried here; that is the main reason this period sits below the Q5's NT$95,000. Estimated, not quoted.
