assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, well under the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000. All checkpoints use 7,000 km/year (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km). At this mileage the F70's Condition Based Service schedule is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: the engine-oil service falls due on the roughly 2-year clock long before the ~25,000-30,000 km clock, and brake fluid is a fixed 2-year item regardless of distance. Budget about one dealer visit a year. Tires likewise age out (roughly every 5 years) rather than wear out. Because the car is far below average mileage, all resale figures are quoted against LOW-MILEAGE listings, which sit above the mileage-blind average. Taxes (牌照稅 NT$7,120/yr, 燃料稅 NT$4,800/yr — both figures confirmed on the U-CAR spec table and the Yahoo trim page) and insurance are excluded by design and appear nowhere in this record.

purchase.source: FACT-CHECK: I re-fetched the price independently and the researcher's NT$1,850,000 is CORRECT — no change. Yahoo 汽車機車's 2026 model-year page (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/trim/bmw-1-series-2026-120-m-sport) renders 「2026 BMW 1-Series 120 M Sport 185」 with a full 2026 lineup of 120 Sport 157萬 / 120 M Sport 185萬 / M135 xDrive 270萬. Its 2025 sibling page (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/trim/bmw-1-series-2025-120-m-sport) renders 183萬 with a lineup of 155 / 183 / 268萬, and the U-CAR spec table (https://newcar.u-car.com.tw/bmw/1%20series/6976/overall) still carries that same 2025 set (155 / 183 / 268萬). So the +NT$20,000 model-year step across all three trims is real and the 2026 car currently on sale lists at NT$1,850,000. The gap to the original scout figure of NT$1,830,000 is 1.1%, inside the 3% tolerance either way, but 1,850,000 is the correct model year. Discount and on-road figures are estimates, justified in notes.
purchase.notes:
POWERTRAIN: classified 'gasoline', not 'hybrid' — VERIFIED. The 120 uses a 1.5L 3-cylinder turbo (1,499 c.c., 直列3汽缸, 156 hp, 24.5 kgm) driving the front wheels through a 7-speed Steptronic dual-clutch gearbox, with a 48V ISG mild-hybrid system. U-CAR's own text states 國內導入的 120 動力車型…追加了 ISG 48V 輕油電系統，因此後排傾倒前的容積縮減為 300 公升…最主要是後廂下方加入置放 48V 鋰電池組的緣故 — i.e. the 48V lithium pack under the boot floor cuts cargo from 380 to 300 litres. It cannot move the car on electricity alone, so it is 'gasoline' per this table's rule. The same U-CAR passage confirms the sibling M135 xDrive 沒有配備 48V 系統. The 48V starter-generator and its lithium pack are real out-of-warranty cost items and are carried in the 7-10 year maintenance period.

DISCOUNTS NT$80,000 (4.3%): BMW Taiwan (總代理汎德) does discount, and the 1 Series is the slowest-moving end of the range — it fights the A-Class, A3 and Mini Hatch in a shrinking entry-luxury hatch segment, and the lineup carries a cheaper 120 Sport at 157萬 that caps what the M Sport can hold. NT$80,000 is a realistic negotiated cash-plus-accessory-credit outcome on a 185萬 car; it is an estimate, not a quoted figure, and it sits in the same band as the sibling records in this table for entry German cars. Any showroom gift package (hotel stays and similar) is deliberately NOT counted as a cash discount.

ONROAD_FEES NT$65,000: 領牌規費 + 代辦 ~NT$12,000; accessories ~NT$53,000 (window film ~NT$25,000 at the grade BMW buyers fit, dash camera ~NT$12,000, mats/visors ~NT$6,000, paint coating ~NT$10,000). Scaled to the price class. Excludes all tax and insurance.

real_cost = 1,850,000 - 80,000 + 65,000 = 1,835,000 (arithmetic re-checked).

Generation: F70, the 4th-generation 1 Series, on sale in Taiwan since late 2024 — so the car is only about 21 months old in market, which is why the 7- and 10-year points had to be extrapolated from predecessor generations.

selling_costs.notes: Private-sale costs, consistent with the private_sale_price figures used in value_checkpoints, and inside the 6,000-15,000 band for this class. Prep is at the upper end because a German car that photographs poorly loses far more on the asking price than the NT$7,500 saved — buyers in this segment shop on presentation. Excludes any dealer trade-in scenario, where prep would be near zero but the price would be the dealer_tradein_price instead.

value_checkpoints.source: VERIFIED BY FACT-CHECK against a fresh scrape of 8891中古車 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/bmw/1-series/120) on 2026-08-12. I re-parsed the listing cards including their TITLES, specifically to test whether the cheaper 120 Sport had been mistaken for the 120 M Sport — it had not. Genuine 「120 M Sport 1.5L」 F70 cards, 2025 registration, low mileage: NT$1,580,000 / 3,141 km; NT$1,580,000 / 3,134 km; NT$1,580,000 / 3,000 km; NT$1,560,000 / 7,201 km; NT$1,560,000 / 3,000 km; NT$1,520,000 / 3,042 km; NT$1,520,000 / 3,000 km; NT$1,510,000 / 6,000 km. One sits at 7,201 km, almost exactly this checkpoint's 7,000 km. Median dealer retail for a ~1-year-old low-mileage M Sport is therefore about NT$1,545,000. Listing text confirms many are 原廠認證 / BPS cars (「BMW汎德原廠認證車」, 「台南汎德認證中古車」, 「BPS原廠保固」), which carries a certification premium over an ordinary dealer ask. ADJUSTMENT CHAIN (these are 車商售價, not what an owner receives): dealer retail ~NT$1,545,000 → private sale NT$1,335,000, i.e. 13.6% below dealer retail, inside the expected 8-15% private-sale discount → dealer trade-in NT$1,170,000, a further 12.4% below private. Confidence is 'medium' rather than 'high': the dealer-retail observation is strong and directly sourced, but no private-sale transaction data exists, so the private figure itself is a modeled conversion, not an observed price.

CORRECTED BY FACT-CHECK (was NT$1,010,000 / NT$880,000). No genuine 3-year F70 exists — the generation only went on sale in Taiwan in late 2024, so the oldest cars are about 1.7 years old — therefore this remains EXTRAPOLATED, but it is now anchored on two things instead of one. (a) Predecessor F40 at 3 years, verified on 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/bmw/1-series) on 2026-08-12: 118i Edition M, 2023 registration, 20,000 km, asking NT$1,080,000 against a verified NT$1,810,000 list (https://autos.yahoo.com.tw/new-cars/trim/bmw-1-series-2023-118i-edition-m) = 59.7% dealer retail; 120i Edition M, 2023 registration, 26,000 km, asking NT$1,298,000 against a verified NT$2,010,000 list = 64.6%. Mean ≈ 62%, which on this car's real_cost gives NT$1,138,000. (b) The F70's OWN observed 2-year market, which the original record never used: 2024-registered 「120 M Sport 1.5L」 cards on the same 8891 page ask NT$1,450,000 at 6,000-6,600 km (five separate listings), NT$1,490,000 at 3,100 km, NT$1,420,000 at 18,000 km. Reading forward from NT$1,545,000 at ~1.2 years and NT$1,455,000 at ~1.7 years, year 3 dealer retail lands nearer NT$1,200,000-1,250,000. Route (a) alone implied a 21% single-year drop in year 3 after only a ~12% drop in year 2 — an ACCELERATING curve, which is the wrong shape: German depreciation is front-loaded and the rate should decelerate after year 1. I therefore blended the two to NT$1,190,000 dealer retail, then took private sale ~10% below = NT$1,070,000, and dealer trade-in ~13% below private = NT$930,000. At 58.3% of real_cost this now sits in line with the sibling German hatches in this table rather than below them. The F40 numbers are themselves depressed by the F70 replacing them in late 2024 — a generational hit this car will take around 2030-31 too, so part of that effect is deliberately carried forward.

EXTRAPOLATED from predecessor F40 at 5 years, ratio applied to real_cost; the underlying listings were re-verified by fact-check on 8891 (https://auto.8891.com.tw/bmw/1-series) 2026-08-12. maintenance.plan_notes:
HONESTY WARNING, READ FIRST: unlike the resale figures, NONE of these maintenance numbers come from a retrieved source. bmw.com.tw blocked automated fetch, and no 汎德 service price table or Mobile01 owner receipt could be reached with the tooling available (the WebSearch budget for this session was already exhausted before the fact-check began, so only direct URL fetches were possible). Every period_cost below is a build from Taiwan BMW dealer rate norms, so all five are marked low confidence. Treat them as a defensible budget, not as sourced data. The fact-check did NOT revise these figures: they are internally coherent, they rise with age, and at roughly NT$530,000 over ten years they sit above the Japanese equivalents and in line with the other German entry cars in this table — but 'plausible' is not 'sourced'.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY VERIFIED: the 3-year factory warranty. Multiple 2025-registered F70 listings on 8891 advertise 「總代理保固到2028/9」, 「保固至2028年」 and 「新車保固至２０２９年」, which confirms 汎德's 3年不限里程原廠保固 on this generation. This was re-confirmed in the fact-check scrape.

INTERVAL LOGIC: at 7,000 km/year servicing is time-driven, not mileage-driven. BMW's Condition Based Service would otherwise call the oil service at roughly 25,000-30,000 km — over three years away at this mileage — so the roughly 2-year oil clock and the fixed 2-year brake-fluid item govern instead. Budget about one dealer visit a year. Tires age out rather than wear out: a set roughly every 5 years, so one set lands in the 3-5y window and a second in the 7-10y window, and the 70,000 km at year 10 never wears out a third.

SUBSIDISED EARLY PERIODS: the 0-1y and 1-3y figures ASSUME BMW Taiwan new-car deals in this segment bundle BMW Service Inclusive scheduled maintenance over the same 3-year window as the warranty. This could not be confirmed. If the deal does NOT include it, add roughly NT$12,000-15,000 per year to years 1-3. Per the rule that subsidised early periods must be paid for later, every period from year 3 onward carries the FULL unsubsidised 汎德 dealer rate with no package credit.

WHY THIS IS NOT A JAPANESE CAR'S NUMBER: the roughly NT$530,000 ten-year total runs well above a comparable Japanese hatch, and the gap is concentrated after warranty expiry. Dealer labour rates are higher, the M Sport's 18-inch wheels make tires and brakes dearer, and the later periods carry German-specific risk items a Japanese equivalent simply does not have — electric water pump, thermostat housing, coil packs, DCT fluid service, and above all the 48V ISG starter-generator and its lithium pack. No air suspension on this car (standard comfort setup, with an optional non-adjustable M sport suspension), and no DPF since it is gasoline, so those two line items are correctly absent.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000 / 21000 / 35000 / 49000 / 70000). POWERTRAIN: the U06 220i is a 1,499 cc three-cylinder TwinPower Turbo (156 hp @5000 rpm) with BMW's second-generation 48V mild-hybrid starter-generator built into the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox, adding ~19-20 hp of eBoost for 170 hp combined (verified this round on the Yahoo Autos trim page and the KingAutos launch article). It supports engine-off coasting but CANNOT move the car on battery alone, so it is classified 'gasoline' per the table's rule; the 48V hardware is noted in purchase.notes and carried as a maintenance risk item in the 5-7 and 7-10 windows. MILEAGE CONSEQUENCE 1 - RESALE, RESTATED AFTER AUDIT: at every age this car carries roughly 40-55% of the mileage of a typical comparable listing, and a low-mileage premium is real in the 8891 data (2023/2024 Luxury cars at 5,000-7,300 km ask 132-135萬 while the same model years at 40,300-55,000 km ask 99.8-110.9萬). BUT the audit found the 8891 asking prices are BIMODAL WITHIN THE SAME YEAR AND MILEAGE BAND, not a clean mileage curve: a 2024 Luxury at 16,000 km asks 108.0萬 while 2024 Luxury cars at 7,000 km ask 135.0萬, and two 2023 Luxury cars both at 16,000 km ask 108.0萬 and 123.0萬. Quoting only the 132-135萬 top cluster overstates the curve, so this record quotes the CENTRE of the low-mileage band, not its top - see each checkpoint source. It also matters that at 2 years this buyer's car has 14,000 km, so the mileage-correct comparable is the 16,000 km car, not the 7,000 km one. MILEAGE CONSEQUENCE 2 - MAINTENANCE: BMW Taiwan's published interval is 每年或每一萬公里, whichever comes first (verified on the 台北依德 BMW service page). At 7,000 km/year the mileage trigger is never reached, so servicing is strictly TIME-DRIVEN: one annual visit, 10 visits over 10 years. Calendar-aged consumables (tires, brake fluid, coolant, 12V AGM battery) dominate the later windows while mileage-driven wear items (pads, discs) are pushed far out. Tax (牌照稅/燃料稅) and insurance are excluded by design.

purchase.source: LIST PRICE INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED THIS ROUND AND CONFIRMED AT NT$1,780,000 (0% variance, no change). Two Taiwan sources fetched directly: (1) Yahoo Autos TW trim page for the 220i - 建議售價 178萬, 1499cc, 156hp@5000rpm, Steptronic 7-speed dual-clutch, second-generation 48V system; (2) FindCar 找車網 new-car reference page, which lists exactly two trims - 220i at 178萬 and 220i Luxury at 195萬 - confirming both the price and that the plain 220i is the entry trim. Historical drift check (KingAutos, verified): the U06 launched in Taiwan on 2022-03-31 at 172萬 / 189萬, so the lineup has crept up ~6萬 over four years. DISCOUNT CORRECTED UPWARD, 70,000 -> 90,000. The prior figure of 70,000 (3.9%) contradicted its own stated justification: it claimed to sit 'modestly above the one observed 2023 deal', but that deal was 100,000 off 1,930,000 (5.2%), so 70,000 was below it in absolute terms AND in percentage terms, and the same note argued that a model four years into its cycle with a replacement approaching normally discounts MORE, not less. The deal sheet itself was fetched and verified this round and is genuine: WeWanted 菜單 for a 2023 220i Luxury ordered 2023-09-13, 牌價 193萬 / 成交價 183萬, 含配備 / 不含保險 / 不含規費 / 不含利息, with only OEM V-KOOL film and a tank of 95 fuel included. Applying that observed 5.2% to 1,780,000 gives 92,560, rounded to 90,000. This is still deliberately far below the sibling BMW X3 record's 12.0% and that gap is intentional: KingAutos reports 汎德 ran a 600-unit annual quota and took over 250 orders in the first month, so the Active Tourer is allocation-limited and low-volume, and 汎德 does not discount it the way it discounts a volume SUV. The U-CAR page the original scout cited returns HTTP 403 and is NOT relied on or listed.
purchase.notes: real_cost = 1,780,000 - 90,000 + 26,000 = 1,716,000. The small discount cuts both ways and both directions are modelled. It raises real_cost relative to a heavily-discounted rival, but it also SUPPORTS residuals: a used Active Tourer does not have to compete against a new one selling 300,000 below sticker, which is precisely the dynamic that hurts the X3's used values. onroad_fees of 26,000 covers 領牌 + 代辦 (~16,000 - an import, but a 178萬 one, so below the ~18,000 carried for a 249萬 X3) plus roughly 10,000 of accessories the dealer did not absorb (隔熱紙 beyond the OEM film, 腳踏墊, coating). The WeWanted deal sheet states 保險及規費 are 實支實付 and separate, which is why 領牌 is carried in full rather than assumed bundled. POWERTRAIN NOTE: this car has a 48V mild-hybrid starter-generator built into its 7-speed DCT, adding ~19-20 hp of eBoost and enabling engine-off coasting. It is NOT a full hybrid - it cannot drive on electricity alone - so it is classified 'gasoline'. The 48V hardware is not free to own: the lithium 48V battery and the integrated starter-generator are out-of-warranty risk items carried as risk-weighted allowances in the 5-7 and 7-10 maintenance windows. MODEL YEAR NOTE: the record is filed as 2026 because that is what is on sale today, but every price source found is labelled 2024 or 2025 model year and no 2026 price change is evidenced, so 178萬 is carried forward unchanged. Tax and insurance are excluded per the model's design.

刊登費 (8891 / SUM listing)

selling_costs.notes: Items sum to 10,000, matching total - mid-band for this class. Lower than the 13,000 carried for a 2,000,000+ German SUV because a 178萬 compact MPV is a less presentation-sensitive sale: buyers at this price point negotiate on service history and mileage more than on paint finish. The 過戶 government fee alone is only ~1,200-2,000; the balance of that line is 代辦 convenience. Assumes a private sale (自售), which is what private_sale_price represents. A dealer trade-in would incur near-zero selling cost but realise the much lower dealer_tradein_price instead - and for this model that gap matters more than usual, because SUM 汽車網 returned 車輛搜尋結果 共 0 筆 (re-verified this round) and 8891 does not carry the Active Tourer in its main BMW model navigation, so a private seller faces a genuinely thin buyer pool and may wait months.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED, REVISED DOWN FROM 1,285,000. There are ZERO 2025-model-year listings in the entire 38-car 8891 set (year breakdown re-verified this round: 2016:3, 2017:2, 2018:6, 2022:6, 2023:13, 2024:8, 2025:0 - sums to 38), so there is no direct 1-year data point and confidence stays 'low'. WHY THE PRIOR FIGURE WAS TOO HIGH: it was bridged from 2024-MY Luxury cars at 7,000-7,333 km asking 135.0萬, treating that as 'the low-mileage band'. Two problems. (1) The same 2024 model year also has a Luxury at 16,000 km asking 108.0萬 and Luxury cars at 40,300-40,700 km asking 109.9-110.9萬 (mileages verified verbatim on the page as 4.03萬公里 / 4.07萬公里, so 40,300 km not 4,030 km - the original reading of the mileage was correct). A 27萬 gap between a 7,000 km and a 16,000 km car of the same year and trim is listing noise, not a mileage curve, so the 132-135萬 cluster is the TOP of a bimodal distribution, not its centre. (2) At 1 year this buyer's car has 7,000 km but at 2 years it has 14,000 km, so the mileage-correct 2-year comparable is the 16,000 km car, not the 7,000 km one. METHOD USED HERE: take the centre of the 2-year low-mileage Luxury band (~120-125萬 dealer asking, between the 135.0萬 and 108.0萬 poles), convert to the plain 220i cost base (Luxury lists 17萬 higher; the used gap compresses to ~10萬), giving ~113萬 dealer asking at 2 years, and step back one year to ~140万 dealer asking at 1 year. PRIVATE-SALE ADJUSTMENT: -11% off dealer retail asking gives ~1,246,000, set at 1,250,000 = 72.8% of real_cost. dealer_tradein_price is a further ~13% below private sale. Cross-check: 72.8% at year 1 sits just under the German peers in this table (X3 74.2%, GLC200 74.0%, Q5 73.7%) - correctly so, because those are premium SUVs and this is a compact MPV with a demonstrably thin buyer pool. A Toyota-like year-1 figure would be wrong here.

BEST-EVIDENCED POINT IN THIS RECORD, REVISED DOWN FROM 1,085,000. Built from real 2023-MY listings on the 8891 220i Active Tourer page (38 listings, re-fetched this round; 13 of them are 2023-MY). Plain 220i at our buyer's band: 16,400 km asking 122.8萬 (Kaohsiung), 25,000 km asking 118.8萬 (Taipei) - interpolating to 21,000 km gives ~120.5萬. WHY THAT WAS TRIMMED RATHER THAN TAKEN AT FACE VALUE: the two plain-220i asks sit at the very top of what the better-populated 2023 Luxury sample supports, and the Luxury is the MORE expensive trim - 2023 Luxury at 16,000 km asks 108.0萬 in one listing and 123.0萬 in another, and the 2023 Luxury median across all mileages is ~110萬. A plain 220i asking more than the median Luxury of the same year is incoherent, so the plain-220i asks are optimistic. Central estimate adopted: ~118萬 dealer retail asking at 3 years / 21,000 km. Contrast with high-mileage same-year cars, which does validate a genuine low-mileage premium: 2023 Luxury at 50,000 km asks 105.8萬 and at 55,000 km asks 99.8萬. PRIVATE-SALE ADJUSTMENT: -11% off 1,180,000 gives ~1,050,000 = 61.2% of real_cost. METHOD NOTE: retention ratios are computed against each comparable's OWN real cost and then applied to this car's real_cost, never by mixing a list-price numerator with a real_cost denominator - that mismatch is a known way to inflate the early years by several points. Cross-check: 61.2% sits just below the GLC200 (62.3%) and well below the X3 (66.1%) at year 3, which is the right ordering for a compact MPV against premium SUVs.

INTERPOLATED between a real 4-year U06 anchor and the predecessor-derived 7-year point; there are no 2021-MY listings in the set (the data jumps from 2018 to 2022), so this is not directly observed and confidence is 'low'. LOWER ANCHOR, WHICH IS REAL AND WELL-REPLICATED: 2022-MY cars at our mileage band - plain 220i at 30,000 km asking 108.0萬 (Taichung, two listings), plain 220i at 39,000 km asking 108.0萬 (Taoyuan), 220i Luxury at 39,000 km asking 108.0萬 (Taoyuan). Three independent plain-220i listings landing on the same 108.0萬 makes this the most consistent cluster on the page. At 4 years and ~30,000 km - almost exactly this buyer's 28,000 km - dealer retail asking is therefore 1,080,000; less the 11% private-sale haircut that is ~961,000, or ~57% of that car's own real cost (2022 list 172萬, so ~1,676,000 all-in). UPPER-AGE ANCHOR: the 30.9% 7-year figure derived from the F45 predecessor below. Bridging 4 years at 57% to 7 years at 31% puts year 5 at ~47.5%: 0.475 x 1,716,000 = 815,000. The 3->5 slope (61.2% -> 47.5%) is materially steeper than the 1->3 slope, which is the correct shape for a German car whose factory warranty (2+1 years, unlimited mileage, verified on the 台北依德 page) expires at year 3 - the used market starts pricing in repair risk the moment cover disappears. Cross-check against peers at year 5: Q5 42.8%, X3 48.5%, GLC200 51.3%, XC40 46.8%. This car at 47.5% sits inside that band.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION, REVISED UP FROM 505,000 AFTER FINDING THE PRIOR ANCHOR WAS A DUPLICATED OUTLIER. The U06 launched in Taiwan in March 2022, so no genuine 7-year data for this generation can exist and none was invented. The F45 220i Active Tourer (2.0L four-cylinder, 192 hp, 8AT) launched in Taiwan on 2015-03-06 at 建議售價 182萬 - re-verified this round by direct fetch of CarStuff - giving an F45 real cost of roughly 1,766,000 on comparable discount and fee assumptions. THE CORRECTION: the prior version anchored the tail on '2018 220i at 70,000 km asking 39.8萬'. That listing appears SIX TIMES on the page, same dealer, same New Taipei location, identical mileage and price - it is one car spam-listed, not six data points, and it is internally incoherent with the rest of the F45 set: a 2017 car at 87,000 km asks 53.8萬 and a 2016 car at 50,300 km asks 46.8萬, both MORE than this supposedly younger, lower-mileage car. Treating it as the tail anchor understates the curve. The distinct F45 cars on the page are: 2016 at 50,300 km 46.8萬, 2016 at 100,000 km 38.8萬, 2016 at 115,300 km 34.9萬, 2017 at 76,500 km 45.0萬, 2017 at 87,000 km 53.8萬, plus the one duplicated 2018 car at 39.8萬. METHOD: the 2017 pair averages ~49.4萬 at ~82,000 km; mileage-adjusting to this buyer's 49,000 km using the ~1.6萬 per 10,000 km slope implied by the 2016 pair gives ~54萬 at 9 years, and stepping two years younger gives ~62萬 dealer retail asking at 7 years. Less a 12% private-sale haircut: ~545,000, or ~31% of the F45's real cost. Settled marginally lower at 530,000 (30.9%) because the F45 sample is small and noisy and because this generation's DCT and 48V hardware are an unknown out-of-warranty liability. THIS REMAINS THE WEAKEST 7-YEAR RETENTION OF THE GERMAN CARS IN THIS TABLE (X3 37.3%, GLC200 40.7%, Q5 33.5%, XC40 31.5%) and that is the finding, not an error: an entry-level compact MPV is the body style that collapses hardest in Taiwan, and the F45 evidence shows it happening.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION, REVISED UP FROM 340,000 - same correction as the 7-year point. The prior figure was built on the 2018/70,000 km/39.8萬 listing that appears six times on the page as duplicates of a single car, and on an arithmetic slip: the prior text derived 19.0% and then applied 0.196, silently adding ~11,000. THE PROPER ANCHOR IS THE 2016 CARS, WHICH ARE GENUINELY 10 YEARS OLD TODAY: 50,300 km asking 46.8萬, 100,000 km asking 38.8萬, 115,300 km asking 34.9萬. This buyer's 10-year car carries only 70,000 km, so interpolating on mileage between the 50,300 km and 100,000 km cars gives ~43.6萬 dealer retail asking. Less a 12% private-sale haircut: ~383,000, or 21.7% of the F45's ~1,766,000 real cost. Applied to this car's real_cost: 0.213 x 1,716,000 = 365,000, set marginally below the raw interpolation because the buyer pool for a decade-old three-cylinder BMW MPV is very small. Confidence 'low' by construction - this is a cross-generation ratio transfer, honestly labelled as such rather than presented as observed. THE TAIL KEEPS FALLING RATHER THAN FLATTENING, which is the intended German-car behaviour and is visible directly in the F45 data: by year 10 the car is seven years out of warranty and the market prices in electric water pump, timing chain, DCT and 48V-era electronics risk. At 21.3% this is still among the weakest 10-year retentions of the German cars here (X3 23.8%, Q5 22.5%, GLC200 26.6%, XC40 21.0%). Supporting evidence for how thin this market is: SUM 汽車網 returned 車輛搜尋結果 共 0 筆 for the model, and 8891's main BMW navigation does not list the Active Tourer as a body style.

maintenance.plan_notes: INTERVAL IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN, AND THAT GOVERNS THIS WHOLE PLAN. BMW Taiwan's published schedule is 每年或每一萬公里, whichever comes first (quote re-verified this round on the 台北依德 BMW service page). At 7,000 km/year the 10,000 km trigger is never reached, so the car goes in exactly once a year on the calendar - 10 visits across 10 years - and the cost profile is driven by items that age out rather than wear out. WARRANTY: BMW Taiwan's new-car cover is 2+1年不限里程 (3 years, unlimited mileage), verbatim from the same source: 'BMW提供您的新車2+1年不限里程保固服務'. From year 4 onward every window carries the FULL unsubsidised cost including out-of-warranty failure risk, which is why the 3-5 window jumps more than threefold over the 1-3 window. SUBSIDY CAVEAT, DOWNGRADED THIS ROUND: the prior version asserted as fact that scheduled servicing is not bundled free in Taiwan and that 汎德 sells it separately as a prepaid BMW Service Inclusive package, and attributed that to the 台北依德 page. That page does not say it - it covers 保固 and the service interval only - and BMW Taiwan's own Service Inclusive page timed out on every fetch attempt. So it is carried here as a STATED ASSUMPTION, not a sourced fact: years 1 and 1-3 are modelled as paying real cash for scheduled servicing. If a free-servicing package is in fact standard, the year-1 and 1-3 windows (8,000 and 22,000) would fall close to zero and the 10-year total would drop by roughly 30,000. See open questions. WHY THIS IS MATERIALLY MORE EXPENSIVE THAN A JAPANESE EQUIVALENT: 汎德 dealer labour rates, 原廠 AGM batteries rather than flooded lead-acid, brake fluid on a strict two-year calendar, and German-specific risk items a Corolla Cross does not have - electric water pump, thermostat housing, oil filter housing gasket, coil packs, and on this car specifically the 48V lithium battery and the starter-generator integrated into the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox. The DCT is another divergence: this is not the ZF 8AT used in rear-drive BMWs, and a dual-clutch oil service is carried in the 5-7 window. The 10-year total of 400,000 sits between the Volvo XC40 (387,000) and the Audi Q5 (404,000) and below the X3 (462,000) and GLC200 (480,000) - correct for a physically smaller, front-drive, three-cylinder car with smaller brakes and tires - but it is roughly double what a comparable Japanese compact would run, which is the honest answer. CAVEAT: no model-specific Taiwanese service invoice for the Active Tourer could be opened - Mobile01 returns HTTP 403 on every attempt, including the 218i Active Tourer first-service thread. Unit costs are scaled from BMW Taiwan norms for small-displacement models rather than read off a receipt, which is why the mid- and late-window confidences are 'low'.

major_items: 1x annual scheduled service (原廠 oil + oil filter + labour, ~7,000)
wiper blades and fluids
fully within 2+1年不限里程 factory warranty - no parts risk carried
checkpoints.source: One time-triggered annual visit only; the 10,000 km mileage trigger is never reached at 7,000 km/year (interval policy verified on the 台北依德 BMW service page). Priced at BMW Taiwan's small-engine 小保養 rate - the 1.5L three-cylinder uses less oil and has three plugs rather than four, so it sits below the 2.0L four-cylinder rate that owner reports put at 6,000-7,000+ per visit. Year 1 is inside the 3-year unlimited-mileage warranty, so nothing beyond scheduled servicing is carried. Cross-check against this table's other German cars at year 1: X3 10,000, GLC200 11,000, Q5 9,000, XC40 12,000 - this car is correctly the cheapest of the group. Assumes servicing is paid, not bundled free; see plan_notes.

major_items: 2x annual scheduled service (years 2 and 3, ~6,500 each)
brake fluid change at year 2 (~3,000, two-year calendar item)
engine air filter + cabin filter (~3,000)
still under factory warranty - warranty EXPIRES at the end of this window
checkpoints.source: Two annual visits, both still inside the 2+1年不限里程 warranty. Brake fluid is the one item that lands here purely on the calendar - BMW Taiwan owners consistently report 滿二年要換剎車油 regardless of mileage - and filters come due on the second or third service. No wear items yet: at 21,000 km the original pads, discs and tires are all far from replacement. The 22,000 figure is deliberately below the X3 (28,000), GLC200 (31,000) and Q5 (30,000) for the same window, reflecting the smaller engine and cheaper consumables; named items sum to ~19,000 with the balance carried as unspecified consumables. This is the last cheap window - the warranty ends at year 3 and the next window is where the real cost starts.

major_items: 2x annual scheduled service, now UNSUBSIDISED post-warranty (~7,000 each)
first tire set - 4 tires age out on the calendar, not on tread (~28,000 fitted)
12V AGM battery (~13,000 原廠 - AGM required for auto start-stop)
spark plugs x3 (~4,500)
brake fluid at year 4 (~3,000)
coolant change (~4,000)
engine air + cabin filters (~3,500)
checkpoints.source: THE FIRST EXPENSIVE WINDOW, AND THE JUMP IS THE POINT - warranty cover ends at year 3, so both visits here are fully out of pocket and every failure is the owner's. Named items sum to exactly 70,000. The dominant line is tires: at only 7,000 km/year the tread will not be worn out, but rubber hardens and cracks on a 5-6 year calendar regardless of mileage, so a full set is replaced on age around year 5 - exactly the cost a mileage-based model misses. The 原廠 AGM 12V battery is the second big line; AGM is mandatory for auto start-stop and costs roughly double a conventional battery. Spark plugs on a three-cylinder are cheaper than the four-cylinder equivalent. Confidence 'low': the window total is built from BMW Taiwan unit-cost norms rather than a model-specific invoice, because every Mobile01 thread returned HTTP 403.

major_items: 2x annual scheduled service (~7,500 each)
front brake pads + discs (~28,000 原廠)
7-speed dual-clutch transmission oil service (~18,000)
brake fluid at year 6 (~3,000)
one out-of-warranty repair event: coil packs / thermostat housing / oil filter housing gasket (~25,000 expected)
48V lithium battery and integrated starter-generator risk allowance (~13,000 risk-weighted)
filters (~3,500)
checkpoints.source: Four to seven years out of warranty is where German-specific failures start being priced in rather than hoped away; named items sum to ~105,500 against the 105,000 carried. Front pads and discs finally come due - late, at 49,000 km, precisely because of the low annual mileage - but BMW 原廠 pads and discs are roughly double a Japanese equivalent. The DCT oil service is a model-specific item worth calling out: the Active Tourer uses a 7-speed dual-clutch, not the ZF 8-speed torque-converter automatic found in rear-drive BMWs, and a dual-clutch fluid and filter service is both mandatory and more expensive. The 25,000 repair-event allowance is a risk-weighted expected value across the well-known B38 three-cylinder failure set (ignition coils, thermostat housing, oil filter housing gasket leaks), not a certainty for any one car. The 13,000 for the 48V hardware is likewise risk-weighted - a full 48V lithium battery or starter-generator replacement runs far higher, but the probability of needing it this early is modest. Lower than the X3's 162,000 for the same window, which is correct: no xDrive transfer case, no air suspension, smaller brakes and tires. CAVEAT: the 48V module's Taiwanese 原廠 replacement price could not be verified from any published price list, so that line is the least certain in this record.

major_items: 3x annual scheduled service (~8,000 each)
second tire set, again aged out rather than worn out (~30,000)
electric water pump (~30,000 - a well-known BMW failure item)
48V starter-generator / 48V battery risk allowance (~25,000 risk-weighted)
rear brake pads + discs (~26,000)
second 12V AGM battery (~14,000)
suspension bushings and dampers (~25,000)
2x brake fluid (~6,500), second spark plug set (~5,000), coolant (~4,500), filters (~5,000)
checkpoints.source: THE TAIL DOES NOT FLATTEN, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE GERMAN MAINTENANCE PROFILE; named items sum to exactly 195,000. Three annual visits plus a concentration of age-driven failures now seven-plus years past warranty. The electric water pump is the single most-cited BMW big-ticket failure in this age band and is carried at full cost rather than risk-weighted, because on a 10-year-old BMW it is closer to expected than not. The 48V starter-generator and its lithium battery are carried at 25,000 risk-weighted - this is the mild-hybrid-specific exposure a conventional gasoline car does not have, and ignoring it would understate the cost of this powertrain. A second tire set falls due on the calendar again (roughly 5-6 year rubber life at 7,000 km/year), as does a second AGM battery. At 195,000 this window sits just below the X3 (200,000) and GLC200 (210,000) and above the Q5 (170,000) and XC40 (185,000): cheaper parts than a mid-size premium SUV, but no cheaper in risk, and the DCT and 48V hardware add exposure the larger cars' conventional automatics do not carry. Confidence 'low' - a structured expected-value build from BMW Taiwan norms and known failure modes, not observed 10-year invoices, which cannot exist for a generation launched in 2022.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr; every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000), far below the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/yr. Consequences baked into this record: (1) servicing is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven — BMW's Condition Based Service mileage triggers are never reached, so the car gets one annual dealer service regardless of distance; (2) tires and the AGM 12V battery age out rather than wear out, so they are scheduled by calendar (~every 5-6 years for tires); (3) used values are quoted from genuinely low-mileage listings and adjusted upward off mileage-blind comparables, with the adjustment stated in each source string. Tax (牌照稅 NT$11,230/yr + 燃料稅 NT$6,180/yr, both confirmed on the Yahoo Autos trim page) and insurance are EXCLUDED by design and appear nowhere in this record. Not a BEV, so no home-charger installation cost applies. TIRE FITMENT — CORRECTED THIS ROUND: the previous draft asserted a staggered 225/45 R18 front / 255/45 R18 rear fitment and used 'the tires cannot be rotated' as a cost driver. The Yahoo Autos TW spec table lists a single 輪胎尺碼 of 225/45R18 and no rear size; the 255/45 R18 figure came from U-CAR alone and is geometrically implausible (255/45 R18 has a ~27 mm larger rolling diameter than 225/45 R18, and BMW's factory CLAR 18-inch staggered pairs match within a few mm — the real staggered partner for 225/45 R18 is 255/40 R18). The front size 225/45 R18 is confirmed; whether the car is square or staggered at the rear is NOT confirmed. Tire budgets below are therefore sized as 'four 18-inch performance tires at TW dealer/premium-shop rates', which is expensive either way, rather than being justified by an unverified no-rotation claim.

purchase.notes: POWERTRAIN: classified 'gasoline'. The Yahoo Autos TW spec table for the 2026 220i M Sport reads 動力型式 汽油, 引擎型式 渦輪增壓/直列4缸/DOHC/16氣門, 1998cc, 184hp@5000rpm, 30.6kgm@1350rpm, 壓縮比 11, 後輪驅動, 8速手自排, 平均油耗 14.7 km/L, 車重 1490 kg. 48V QUESTION — CORRECTED THIS ROUND: the previous draft asserted positively that this car has NO 48V mild-hybrid system and booked that as 'a genuine positive for later-life maintenance'. That assertion is not supported. Yahoo's 動力型式 field only distinguishes 汽油/柴油/油電混合/電動 and would read 汽油 for a 48V mild hybrid too, so the absence of 48V data on Yahoo is not evidence of absence. www.bmw.com.tw was unreachable from this network on every attempt (independently reproduced this round), so BMW Taiwan's own technical data could not be consulted, and the 2 Series Coupé received a 小改款 (LCI) in this generation — exactly the update in which BMW added 48V starter-generators across much of the B48 range. Whether the TW-spec LCI 220i carries a 48V ISG is therefore UNRESOLVED. This does not change the classification: a 48V mild hybrid is 'gasoline' for this table either way, and a full hybrid it certainly is not. But the maintenance plan no longer books a saving for the ISG's absence; it carries a small contingency for it instead. DISCOUNT (NT$110,000, estimated): BMW Taiwan (總代理 汎德) discounts luxury models mostly as value-in-kind rather than list-price cuts. The 2026-08-11 「BMW仲夏禮遇」 campaign article (verified this round) gives, 全車系, a 晶華酒店集團 three-day/two-night package stated at over NT$30,000 in value plus zero-interest financing, and — on 指定車型 only — ONE of 一年乙式全險, a BMW 原廠保養套裝, or 延長保固. Note the article's per-model sections cover 1系列, 5系列/5系列 Touring, X1, X3 and X6; the 2 Series is not mentioned anywhere in it. The 220i M Sport is the entry car in a very low-volume niche coupe line (only ~32 used 220i Coupé listings nationwide across all model years), which supports a real concession but not a deep one. I model NT$110,000 as the cash-equivalent of the hotel package (~NT$30,000) plus a realistic dealer cash-and-accessory concession (~NT$80,000) on a slow-selling niche coupe. IMPORTANT — NO DOUBLE COUNTING: because the campaign offers the 原廠保養套裝 as an ALTERNATIVE to cash/insurance value on 指定車型, and never names the 2 Series, this record does NOT also assume free factory servicing. The buyer is modelled as taking the cash-equivalent concession here and paying full dealer rates for every service in maintenance below. The previous draft counted both, which understated ten-year cost. ON-ROAD FEES (NT$62,000): 領牌 + 代辦 ~NT$12,000, plus ~NT$50,000 of typical delivery accessories (隔熱紙, 行車紀錄器, 車身鍍膜, 踏墊, 避光墊) scaled to a 212萬 imported car. Tax and insurance deliberately excluded. real_cost = 2,120,000 - 110,000 + 62,000 = 2,072,000.

selling_costs.notes: Costs the seller bears on a 自售 (private sale), consistent with the private_sale_price basis used in value_checkpoints. Sits in the normal 6,000-15,000 band for this class. A dealer trade-in would avoid the listing fee and most of the prep cost, but that is already reflected in the much lower dealer_tradein_price rather than here.

value_checkpoints.source: 8891 中古車 220i Coupe listing page, re-retrieved and re-verified 2026-08-12: exactly one 1-year-old car nationwide — a 2025款 220i M Sport, 1.1萬公里 (11,000 km), 高雄, 車商 asking NT$1,850,000. ADJUSTMENTS MADE (this is a dealer ASKING price, never copied): that car is a 汎德 BPS (BMW Premium Selection) 原廠認證中古車, which carries a certification premium (factory prep + warranty) of roughly 8-10% over ordinary dealer stock, so ordinary dealer retail is ~NT$1,690,000. Private sale then sits a further ~10% below ordinary dealer retail, ~NT$1,520,000, and I add ~NT$30,000 back for our car's lower mileage (7,000 vs 11,000 km) to reach NT$1,550,000 — a total haircut of 16% off the visible asking price, wider than the standard 8-15% band precisely because of the certification layer. Dealer trade-in set ~13% below private sale. This is a 25% loss of real_cost in year one — the steep German first-year hit, and consistent with the other German cars in this batch (BMW 1/3/4 Series and X3 all land at 71-75% year-one retention), not a Toyota-like curve. CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED to low this round: the previous draft called this medium, but it rests on a SINGLE nationwide listing that additionally needed a two-step adjustment — that is the definition of a single weak data point.

8891 中古車 220i Coupe page, re-verified 2026-08-12: six listings of 2023款 220i M Sport at 2.8-2.83萬公里 all asking NT$1,550,000, all in 桃園 and mostly BMW 原廠認證中古車 — almost certainly only one or two physical cars re-posted by different sales staff, so I treat this as ~1 data point, not 6. Bracketed against the genuine four-year cluster below (NT$1,280,000-1,420,000 across 新北/桃園/台中). ADJUSTMENTS MADE: de-certifying the BPS asking price gives ordinary dealer retail ~NT$1,480,000; adding back for our lower mileage (21,000 vs 28,000 km) gives ~NT$1,500,000 dealer retail; private sale ~12% below that = NT$1,320,000. Dealer trade-in ~13% below private. Original 2023 list was NT$2,090,000 (verified this round on the Yahoo Autos 2023 model page), so the market is asking 74% of list at three years while a private seller actually realises ~64% of real_cost — exactly the dealer-retail-vs-private gap that makes copying asking prices wrong. Retention sits above the FWD 2 Series Gran Coupé in this batch, which is deliberate: a RWD enthusiast coupe holds better than the FWD saloon-derived body.

Extrapolated one year beyond the oldest current-generation (G42) cars available. Real anchor re-verified on 8891 2026-08-12: distinct 2022款 220i M Sport (4 years old) across three cities — NT$1,420,000 @ 3.65萬公里 (新北), NT$1,298,000 @ 4.4萬公里 (桃園), NT$1,280,000 @ 6萬公里 (台中), NT$1,298,000 @ 6.4萬公里 (台中), and one 電洽 @ 6.3萬公里 (台中) — so ordinary dealer retail averages ~NT$1,330,000 at four years. ADJUSTMENTS MADE: rolling forward one year gives ~NT$1,215,000 dealer retail at five years, plus ~NT$25,000 back for our low mileage (35,000 km vs the 36,500-64,000 km of the comparables) = ~NT$1,240,000 asking; private sale ~12% below = NT$1,090,000. Dealer trade-in ~13% below private. Cross-check: a 4-year private sale off that cluster would be ~NT$1,180,000-1,200,000, and NT$1,090,000 is a sensible one-year step down from it. The G42 only launched in Taiwan in 2022, so no genuine 5-year car exists yet — this is a one-year extrapolation off a solid four-car cluster, not a fabricated figure.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION — no 7-year-old G42 exists (TW launch 2022). Method: took the real 8891 prices of the F22 2 Series Coupé at exactly 7 years old, converted them to a retention ratio of the F22's own original list price, then applied that ratio to this car's real_cost. Data re-verified on 8891 2026-08-12: 2019款 220i M Sport asking NT$768,000 @ 8.5萬公里 (高雄) and NT$759,000 @ 9萬公里 (彰化). The 2019 list price of NT$1,900,000 for the 220i M Sport 領航版 was re-verified this round on the Yahoo Autos 2019 model page, so the pairing is exact. Raw retention = 768,000/1,900,000 = 40.4% of list as a DEALER ASKING price at ~85,000 km. ADJUSTMENTS MADE: our car has 49,000 km, roughly 36,000 km less, worth ~+15% on a 7-year BMW, lifting asking-equivalent to ~NT$880,000; private sale ~12% below = NT$774,000, i.e. 40.7% of the F22's list price. Applying 40.7% to real_cost NT$2,072,000 gives NT$843,000, rounded to NT$840,000. Dealer trade-in ~14% below private (older cars take a wider dealer haircut). Confidence low: this is cross-generation extrapolation, and by year 7 the car is out of warranty so the used market is pricing in repair risk — which is why the curve keeps falling rather than flattening.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION, same method as year 7. Real F22 data re-verified on 8891 2026-08-12 at 10-11 years: 2016款 asking NT$388,000 @ 13萬公里 (桃園); 2016款 220i 自售 (個人賣家) NT$488,000 @ 19萬公里 (新北); 2015款 NT$498,000 @ 9.4萬公里 (新北); 2015款 NT$438,000 @ 15.3萬公里 (新北). The 2016 220i Sport original list of NT$1,790,000 was re-verified this round on the Yahoo Autos 2016 model page, so the 130,000 km car retains 21.7% of list as a dealer asking price. ADJUSTMENTS MADE: our car at 70,000 km is below every comparable — roughly half the mileage of the NT$388,000 car and below even the 94,000 km 2015款 that asks NT$498,000 — so asking-equivalent is set at ~NT$535,000 (29.9% of the F22 list), then private sale ~12% below at ~NT$471,000 = 26.3% retention of the F22's list price. Applying 26.3% to real_cost NT$2,072,000 gives NT$545,000. Dealer trade-in ~16% below private, since dealers discount hardest on decade-old German cars. REVISED DOWN this round from NT$560,000: the low-mileage premium here is the single largest unverified judgement in the curve, and the previous draft's ~+42% premium over the 130,000 km comparable put this car at 27.0% ten-year retention — the highest of any BMW in this batch (1/3/4 Series, X3 and 2 Series Gran Coupé span 21.0-26.0%), which a niche coupe with a known-weak engine family should not be. Trimming the premium to ~+38% lands it at 26.3%, at the top of the cohort rather than outside it. The tail does NOT flatten the way a Lexus would: the same 8891 listings openly advertise 「水路通病.正時鍊條均已更新」 and 「通病都處理鏈條滑板已換」, i.e. the market is explicitly pricing known cooling-system and timing-chain repairs into decade-old cars of this engine family.

maintenance.plan_notes: HONESTY NOTE: unlike the price and used-value figures, these maintenance numbers are MODELLED, not quoted from a price list. No primary Taiwan BMW service-price table could be reached — www.bmw.com.tw was unreachable from this network on every attempt (independently reproduced this round), and Mobile01 (the usual home of owner receipts) returns 403 to non-browser clients, which was not circumvented. Every maintenance checkpoint is therefore marked low confidence. MATERIALLY REVISED THIS ROUND — the previous draft's ten-year total of NT$430,000 was wrong on two counts. (1) It assumed the 「3年/4萬公里 BMW 原廠保養套裝」 was secured free at purchase, making years 1 and 3 cost only NT$5,000 and NT$18,000. The 2026-08-11 「BMW仲夏禮遇」 article was re-read this round: the package is offered only on 指定車型, as ONE choice among 一年乙式全險 / 原廠保養套裝 / 延長保固, and the article's model sections name 1系列, 5系列, X1, X3 and X6 — the 2 Series appears nowhere in it. Worse, the same draft also booked a NT$110,000 cash-equivalent discount, so the concession was counted twice: once as cash off the purchase and again as free servicing. This record now takes the concession as cash in purchase.discounts and pays FULL dealer rates for every service from year one. (2) The result was internally incoherent against its own batch: at NT$430,000 the 2 Series Coupé had the LOWEST ten-year maintenance of any German car in the set — below the smaller, cheaper, front-wheel-drive BMW 1 Series (NT$530,000), below the BMW 3 Series (NT$485,000) and X3 (NT$462,000), and far below its own sibling BMW 2 Series Gran Coupé (NT$592,000), which shares the same B48 engine. A RWD M Sport coupe on 18-inch performance rubber cannot be the cheapest German car in the batch to maintain. The corrected total is NT$502,000 (~NT$50,200/yr), which sits between the 3 Series and the 1 Series — the right neighbourhood for this car. WHAT IS ACTUALLY SOURCED underneath the model: (a) the campaign terms and their model scope, from the dated 2026-08-11 article; (b) the front tire size 225/45 R18, from the Yahoo Autos TW spec table — note the rear size is NOT confirmed and the previous draft's 255/45 R18 has been dropped as implausible, so tire lines are budgeted as four 18-inch performance tires at TW rates rather than justified by a no-rotation claim; (c) real-world evidence of this engine family's known failure points, from 8891 listing copy on F22 cars advertising 「水路通病」 and 「正時鍊條/滑板已換」 as selling points. STRUCTURE: at 7,000 km/yr the car never reaches BMW's Condition Based Service mileage triggers, so servicing is purely TIME-driven — one annual dealer service every year, ten visits over ten years, and consumables replaced by calendar age. Years 1-3 sit inside BMW Taiwan's new-car warranty so they carry scheduled servicing only and no repair spend; the step up after year 3 is the tires and the first out-of-warranty risk items. One cost this record no longer claims to avoid: the 48V starter-generator. Whether the TW-spec LCI 220i has a 48V mild-hybrid system is unresolved (see purchase.notes), so years 7 and 10 carry a modest contingency for it instead of booking its absence as a saving.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, so every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000) — roughly half the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/yr. At that rate BMW's condition-based service (CBS) is triggered by TIME, not distance: an annual oil service and a two-yearly brake-fluid change arrive long before the odometer asks, and tyres and batteries are replaced on age rather than tread or cycle wear. Powertrain is the B38 1.5L 3-cylinder TwinPower Turbo (156 hp / 240 Nm, 7-speed Steptronic DCT) with a 48V mild-hybrid starter-generator; a 48V ISG only assists and restarts the engine and cannot move the car on battery alone, so this is classified "gasoline", NOT "hybrid". Vehicle licence tax (牌照稅), fuel tax (燃料稅), all insurance and fuel/energy cost are EXCLUDED by design and appear nowhere in purchase, maintenance or selling_costs. Value figures assume a clean, accident-free, single-owner car with full 汎德 service history — which is what a 7,000 km/yr owner would actually have — and are net of the dealer-retail-to-private-sale adjustment described in each checkpoint.

purchase.source: VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. 2026年式 (正26年式) 建議售價 NT$1,900,000, confirmed by direct fetch of 8891 新車頻道 (https://c.8891.com.tw/news/bmw/2-series-gran-coupe/21510), which states 售價為190萬與275萬，分別較之前漲1萬與2萬 for the 220 M Racing Edition and M235 xDrive respectively, the only change being standard AR navigation. purchase.notes: 48V MILD HYBRID, NOT A HYBRID: the 220 Gran Coupé pairs a 1.5L 3-cylinder TwinPower Turbo with BMW's 48V starter-generator (156 hp, 240 Nm, 0-100 km/h 7.9 s, 7-speed Steptronic DCT). The 48V system only assists and restarts the engine — it cannot drive the car on electricity alone — so this is "gasoline". Several Taiwanese outlets write 48V高效複合動力, which reads like "hybrid" in Chinese; that wording does not change the classification. Only one non-M trim is sold in Taiwan; the M235 xDrive Racing Edition (NT$2,750,000) is a separate car. Discount NT$80,000 (~4.2%): 汎德 does not deep-discount BMW, but a 190萬 compact with a 156 hp three-cylinder is a comparatively slow seller against a 320i or a Mercedes A-Class/CLA, so a combined cash discount plus dealer-fitted accessory credit of roughly 4% of list is realistic. This is an estimate, not a quotation, and the plausible range is NT$40,000-120,000. On-road NT$68,000 = 領牌／代辦 ~NT$10,000 (新領牌照登記費、行照、牌照、代辦手續) + 配件 ~NT$58,000 (隔熱紙 ~25,000, 行車紀錄器 ~12,000, 鍍膜 ~15,000, 腳踏墊／防水托盤 ~6,000), scaled to this price class. real_cost = 1,900,000 - 80,000 + 68,000 = 1,888,000. Tax and insurance excluded by design.

selling_costs.notes: Assumes a private sale (自售), which is what private_sale_price represents. A German compact at this age needs a slightly better presentation spend than a Japanese equivalent because buyers scrutinise wheel kerbing, the M brake calipers and interior trim wear; NT$7,000 covers a proper detail plus small wheel/trim touch-up. If the owner instead trades in to a dealer, most of these costs disappear but so does roughly NT$75,000-180,000 of proceeds depending on age (widest at year 1, narrowest at year 10) — that trade-off is why dealer_tradein_price is quoted separately.

maintenance.plan_notes: WARRANTY: BMW Taiwan (汎德) includes 3年不限里程原廠保固 as standard. Note the previous version of this record dated that to 1 June 2024 and cited an explicitly AI-generated U-CAR answer page; the real basis is 汎德's long-standing programme, announced effective 1 June and applied to cars delivered from 1 May 2009 onward (https://news.u-car.com.tw/news/article/10646, https://www.auto-online.com.tw/news/15323). So faults are covered to year 3, but SCHEDULED SERVICING IS NOT. PREPAID PACKAGE — TREATED AS UPSIDE, NOT BASE CASE: a 3年／4萬公里原廠保養套裝 is a recurring purchase incentive (BMW 3 Series 50th-anniversary campaign to end-July 2025, a September 2025 range-wide plan, a January 2026 new-year plan), but it is promotional rather than a standard entitlement and is usually bundled with dealer financing (月付9,900元起 / 月付5,900元起). This record therefore assumes the buyer PAYS for scheduled servicing in years 0-3; if the package is negotiated in, roughly NT$30,000-35,000 moves out of the year-1 and year-3 periods and the ten-year total barely changes. TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN: at 7,000 km/yr the buyer reaches only 21,000 km by year 3 and 70,000 km by year 10, so BMW's condition-based service calls for an annual oil service and a two-yearly brake-fluid change long before the mileage counter asks, and tyres and batteries age out rather than wear out. LATER-PERIOD GERMAN RISK ITEMS carried deliberately: the electric water pump and plastic thermostat housing (a documented BMW cooling-system failure pattern in the 60,000-100,000 km band), ignition coils on the three-cylinder, the 48V lithium battery, and a contingency for the 48V starter-generator itself — none of which a Japanese equivalent carries. COST BASIS: 汎德 publishes no itemised service price table. The only hard dealer figure obtained is a Mobile01 owner report of ~NT$5,000-6,000 for a 30,000 km service with no parts replaced at a BMW dealer; I used NT$8,000-9,000 for a full annual oil-and-filter service to reflect oil, filter and the higher labour on later work. Brake and tyre pricing sanity-checked against BMWCCT, an independent BMW parts retailer (https://www.bmwcct.com.tw/shop/category.php?id=59, TEXTAR/Zimmermann/BMW OEM pads NT$2,100-4,500, discs NT$4,700-9,800 parts-only), uplifted for the M Sport brake package, 18-inch hardware and 汎德 dealer labour. assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. Every checkpoint uses the 7,000 km/year midpoint: 7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km. At this mileage BMW's Condition Based Service (CBS) clock is time-driven, not distance-driven: the annual and 24-month counters trip long before the ~15,000-25,000 km oil interval, and tyres and brake fluid age out rather than wear out. Used values therefore quote LOW-MILEAGE comparables, which in Taiwan sit above the mileage-blind average for German cars. LOW-MILEAGE PREMIUM - SIZED CONSERVATIVELY AFTER RE-CHECK. The prior draft claimed a ~NT$300,000 premium based on 8891 listings read as 94,000-129,000 km asking NT$1,050,000-1,088,000 against low-mileage cars at ~NT$1,350,000. On re-fetch of the same 8891 index the mileage fields did not reproduce (the same listings returned as 7,000-12,900 km), so those exact mileages are NOT reliable. What DOES reproduce across independent sources is the shape: a 2021 G20 320i M Sport at 64,104 km asks NT$1,268,000 (SUM), a 2021 at 80,000 km asks NT$1,198,000 (8891), a 2020 at 76,603 km is privately offered at NT$1,130,000 (Facebook Marketplace), and FindCar's whole G20 320i band runs NT$1,176,000-1,348,000. A genuine low-mileage premium of roughly NT$100,000-150,000 at 5-7 years is supported; NT$300,000 is not. Years 5, 7 and 10 have been trimmed accordingly. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: 牌照稅 (NT$11,230/yr for 1,998cc) and 燃料稅 (NT$6,180/yr) per the Yahoo Autos spec page, plus all insurance, fuel, parking and tolls. One structural assumption is stated explicitly because it moves years 7 and 10: the 2026 car is a late-life G20 LCI and the Neue Klasse-based successor is expected around 2027-2028, so a car bought at the END of a generation depreciates faster than the 2019 G20 used as the year-7 comparable, which was bought at the START of one. Years 5-10 are shaded down roughly 5% below what the raw comparables imply.

purchase.notes: POWERTRAIN - PLAIN GASOLINE, NO 48V. Independently confirmed on the Yahoo Autos spec sheet, which was fetched in full and contains no electric-motor, ISG or mild-hybrid entry anywhere in the 320i M Sport powertrain block. KingAutos likewise flags only the M340i xDrive as 油電混合(HEV), attributing an 11hp electric motor to it - that 11hp figure is the signature of a 48V starter-generator, which confirms KingAutos does surface 48V systems when present and did not surface one for the 320i. So the Taiwan 320i is a conventional B48 turbo four, correctly classified 'gasoline', and there is genuinely NO 48V starter-generator to budget for in the 7-10 year window. (Note: this is a case where the classification rule and the hardware agree - even had 48V been fitted, the correct classification would still be 'gasoline', since a mild hybrid cannot move the car on battery alone.) DISCOUNT - NT$120,000 (4.8% off list). The 3 Series is a steady seller for 汎德, not a slow-moving model, so cash off is moderate; the realistic package is roughly NT$60,000-80,000 dealer 折讓 plus NT$40,000-60,000 of accessories and 領牌 absorbed by the dealer. The campaign 3年/4萬公里原廠保養套裝, the 乙式險 year and any 4th-year extended warranty are deliberately NOT counted as cash discount - they are non-cash, and counting them here as well as in the early maintenance periods would double-count. ON-ROAD FEES - NT$65,000 = 新領牌照規費 and 車牌/行照 (~NT$800) + 代辦/交車服務費 (~NT$8,000) + accessories and PDI typical at this class (front/rear dashcam, ceramic coating, window film, floor mats, mudguards) ~NT$56,000. Scales with the NT$2,490,000 price point. Tax and insurance are excluded from real_cost by design. Arithmetic check: 2,490,000 - 120,000 + 65,000 = 2,435,000.

I re-fetched the 8891 320i index (https://auto.8891.com.tw/bmw/3-series/320i) independently and the one-year-old anchor reproduced cleanly: a 2025 320i M Sport at 9,000 km asking NT$1,980,000 dealer retail (車商售價) and a second 2025 320i M Sport at 2,379 km asking NT$1,968,000 - the latter was NOT reported in the prior draft but confirms rather than contradicts it. Two listings clustered at NT$1,968,000-1,980,000 make this the best-evidenced checkpoint in the record. Our car at 7,000 km sits between the two comparables. DEALER-RETAIL TO PRIVATE-SALE ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale set 12.6% below the NT$1,980,000 dealer retail asking price = NT$1,730,000, within the 8-15% band, because a dealer on a nearly-new German car carries certification, reconditioning and a warranty period in that spread. Dealer trade-in (車商收購價) set a further 13.3% below private = NT$1,500,000. These are NOT listed asking prices. Retention 71.0% of real_cost after one year, i.e. a 29% first-year loss - a German figure, not a Toyota one.

UNCHANGED, BUT ON A WIDER AND PARTLY DIFFERENT EVIDENCE BASE. My own fetch of the 8891 320i index (https://auto.8891.com.tw/bmw/3-series/320i) surfaced three-year-old comparables the prior draft omitted: a 2023 320i M Sport at NT$1,680,000, a 2023 320i at NT$1,498,000, and 2023 320i Korean parallel-import cars at NT$1,528,000 - the import status matters, as 平行輸入 cars sell below 總代理 cars and should not anchor a 總代理 curve. It also surfaced TWO 2024 320i M Sport listings at NT$1,598,000 and one at NT$1,798,000, which the prior draft did not report; a two-year-old car at NT$1,598,000 caps how high a three-year-old 總代理 car can reasonably be placed. NOTE ON MILEAGES: the mileage fields on this index did not reproduce consistently between fetches, so I anchor on model year and price and treat the quoted kilometre figures as unreliable. Taking the 總代理 M Sport cars only, three-year dealer retail lands at roughly NT$1,550,000-1,600,000; I use NT$1,600,000. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private sale 15% below dealer retail = NT$1,360,000; dealer trade-in a further 13.2% below = NT$1,180,000. Shaded to the bottom of the band because those 2023 cars were early-LCI whereas the 2026 car will be a run-out-generation car by 2029. This is the steep German years-1-to-3 leg: 55.9% of real_cost retained privately at year 3, where a low-mileage Lexus or Toyota equivalent would hold roughly 70%.

LOWERED from NT$1,190,000 / NT$1,020,000. The prior draft set a five-year DEALER RETAIL anchor of NT$1,380,000, which is above the observed ceiling of the entire G20 320i used market. Independent data gathered this session: FindCar's G20 320i band runs NT$1,176,000-1,348,000 across all G20 model years (https://www.findcar.com.tw/q/g20%20bmw%20320i); SUM 汽車網 lists a 2021 320i M Sport G20 總代理 at 64,104 km for NT$1,268,000 dealer retail; 8891 lists a 2021 320i M Sport at 80,000 km for NT$1,198,000 dealer retail; and a 2020 320i M Sport G20 at 76,603 km is offered on Facebook Marketplace at NT$1,130,000 against an original NT$2,290,000 list - a private ask, and note how far below the dealer-retail curve it sits. Our car at 35,000 km carries a genuine low-mileage premium over the 64,000-80,000 km comparables, but that premium is worth roughly NT$60,000-100,000, not the NT$300,000 the prior draft assumed. Five-year dealer retail is therefore set at NT$1,330,000, just under FindCar's observed ceiling. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private 12.8% below dealer retail = NT$1,160,000; trade-in a further 14.2% below = NT$995,000, widened because the car is out of its factory warranty and dealers begin pricing repair risk. Retention 47.6% of real_cost.

LOWERED from NT$1,050,000 / NT$880,000, and the prior draft's headline source claim did not survive re-checking. It cited FindCar as showing a well-equipped 2019 M-Sport averaging NT$1,388,000; my own retrieval of FindCar's G20 320i data returns a band of NT$1,176,000-1,348,000 across four vehicles, so NT$1,388,000 exceeds that source's own observed maximum and cannot be used as a seven-year anchor. Genuine same-generation seven-year data does exist and is used: the 2019 G20 320i M Sport launched in Taiwan at NT$2,290,000 建議售價 (U-CAR articles 48128 and 48781, both read via search snippet - news.u-car.com.tw returns HTTP 403 to direct fetch; a second independent search this session re-confirmed the 229萬 figure). Against real listings, six- and seven-year-old G20 320i M Sport cars at normal mileage transact around NT$1,050,000-1,270,000 dealer retail. Our car at 49,000 km is genuinely low-mileage for its age, so seven-year dealer retail is set at NT$1,160,000, then shaded ~5% for the end-of-generation effect described in assumptions.notes. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private 12.9% below dealer retail = NT$1,010,000 (41.5% of real_cost); trade-in a wide 15.8% below at NT$850,000, because an out-of-warranty seven-year-old BMW is a risk purchase for a dealer. The tail does NOT flatten here the way a Lexus would.

LOWERED from NT$570,000 / NT$445,000. EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION - no genuine 10-year data exists for the G20, which only launched in Taiwan in late 2019, so real prices for the F30 320i at 10 years old today are used instead. From the 8891 320i index (https://auto.8891.com.tw/bmw/3-series/320i), 2016-2017 F30 320i cars ask NT$470,000-499,000 dealer retail at high mileage; FindCar (https://www.findcar.com.tw/q/2016%20bmw%20320i%20f30) shows a 2016 F30 320i at 88,986 km for NT$558,000 dealer retail; Carousell shows a 2016 F30 320i at 130,000 km for NT$448,000. A 70,000 km 2016 F30 320i M Sport sedan therefore maps to roughly NT$610,000 dealer retail - genuinely low mileage for a decade-old car, but the premium at this age is small in absolute terms because the whole price band has collapsed. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private ~10% below dealer retail, then shaded ~5% for the end-of-generation effect and the G20's heavier electronics content, giving NT$550,000 (22.6% of real_cost). Trade-in set 20% below private at NT$440,000 - wider than the usual 10-15% guidance, which is deliberate: a decade-old German sedan is close to a wholesale/auction proposition for a Taiwanese dealer. CAVEAT CARRIED FORWARD AND RE-TESTED: the F30 320i M Sport's original Taiwan list price still could NOT be independently verified. I ran a fresh search specifically for the F30 price and it again collapsed onto the G20 launch article ('大改款3系列新增320i M Sport之選，定價229萬元' describes the 2019 大改款, i.e. the G20). So the F30 denominator remains assumed, not sourced, and this checkpoint stays LOW confidence. The tail keeps falling rather than flattening, which is the correct German shape and is consistent with the maintenance exposure below.

maintenance.plan_notes: SERVICING IS TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. At 7,000 km/year BMW's Condition Based Service annual counter and the 2-year brake-fluid counter trip long before any distance interval, so this plan bills one dealer visit per year regardless of kilometres, and ages consumables out on the calendar (tyres and the 12V AGM battery at ~5-6 years, not at a wear threshold). MATERIAL CORRECTION versus the prior draft: THE PREPAID SERVICE PACKAGE IS CAMPAIGN-ONLY, NOT STANDARD. The prior draft modelled years 0-3 at NT$3,000 and NT$12,000 on the assumption that the 3年/4萬公里原廠保養套裝 always applies, marked both checkpoints HIGH confidence, and simultaneously listed the package's standard-vs-campaign status as an unresolved open question - an internal contradiction. Searching this specifically resolves it against that assumption: the package appears only in dated, time-limited campaigns (a June 2025 低月付 campaign, a September 2025 '全車系加贈原廠保養套裝，燃油車型享3年/4萬公里保養禮遇' campaign, and a 3 Series 50th-anniversary campaign), with BEVs upgraded to 4年不限里程 in the September wave. It is a promotional gift tied to specific purchase windows, not a permanent entitlement. The related claim that BMW Taiwan gives 3年不限里程 warranty to cars registered from 2024-06-01 also did NOT reproduce - the retrievable material points to a 3年/4萬公里 factory warranty for combustion cars, with unlimited-mileage terms attaching to BEVs. At 7,000 km/year the buyer reaches only ~21,000 km by year 3, so a 40,000 km cap would not bind in practice and the warranty conclusion is unaffected; but the record should not assert an unverified 不限里程 term. Years 1 and 3 are therefore raised to probability-weighted central estimates between the package-applies case (NT$3,000 / NT$12,000) and the no-package case (NT$12,000 / NT$26,000), and both are downgraded from HIGH to MEDIUM confidence. PRICE BASIS - now anchored on a real owner receipt rather than a range: a 2020 G20 320i M Sport owner reports NT$10,222 including tax for a scheduled annual/11,000 km service at an authorised dealer, and a separate G20 320i thread references a 三萬六 (NT$36,000) service invoice for heavier work. That validates NT$11,000-12,000 per annual visit post-package at dealer rates; an independent specialist would be roughly 40% cheaper but is not assumed. NO 48V SYSTEM - the 320i is a conventional B48 turbo four with no 48V starter-generator (verified on the Yahoo Autos spec sheet, which has no ISG entry, and on KingAutos, which flags only the M340i as HEV), so unlike the mild-hybrid cars in this batch there is no ISG/48V battery replacement risk in the 7-10 year window. That is a real, verified saving, not an omission. YEARS 5-7 REBALANCED: the prior draft billed NT$88,000 for years 5-7 against NT$105,000 for years 3-5, i.e. maintenance FELL as the car aged out of warranty, which is the wrong shape. Ignition coils and the first oil-filter-housing/valve-cover weep were deferred entirely to years 7-10; a share is moved forward, restoring a monotonic rise. The late periods carry the B48/G20 items that genuinely bite in Taiwan: electric water pump and thermostat housing, oil filter housing and valve cover gaskets, ignition coils, and front suspension control-arm bushings. Ten-year total lands near NT$485,000 - roughly double an equivalent-age Japanese D-segment sedan, which is the correct shape for this car.

The annual-service rate is now anchored on a real receipt rather than a range: a 2020 G20 320i M Sport owner reports NT$10,222 including tax for a scheduled service at an authorised dealer, consistent with the NT$8,000-12,000 band in Mobile01 owner threads (https://www.mobile01.com/topicdetail.php?f=275&t=5485763). checkpoints.source: RAISED from NT$88,000 to NT$112,000. The prior draft had maintenance FALLING from NT$105,000 (years 3-5) to NT$88,000 (years 5-7) - i.e. the car got cheaper to run in the first window with no warranty and no service package, which is the wrong shape and breaks the expected rise with age. The cause was that ignition coils and the first oil-leak gasket work were deferred entirely to the 7-10 window; on a B48 at 6-7 years those routinely appear earlier, so a share is moved forward (coils NT$14,000, early gasket weep NT$10,000). The remaining structure is retained and is not generic: the electric water pump and the plastic thermostat/coolant housing are the best-documented recurring B48/G20 weak points, and a dealer replacement in Taiwan runs roughly NT$25,000-35,000 in parts and labour, consistent with the 三萬六 (NT$36,000) service invoice referenced in a G20 320i owner thread. Budgeting exactly one such failure event across two years is a deliberate middle estimate - some cars see none, some see two. Annual dealer service rate per owner reports (https://www.mobile01.com/topicdetail.php?f=275&t=7262216). NOTE: there is NO 48V starter-generator on this car, so unlike the mild-hybrid cars in this batch no ISG replacement is budgeted.

checkpoints.source: ADJUSTED from NT$250,000 to NT$240,000, reflecting that the ignition-coil set has been moved forward into the 5-7 window rather than double-counted here; the residual electrical/alternator risk reserve is raised slightly to compensate. A three-year window with no warranty and no service package, on a car two generations old by 2036. Costed at authorised-dealer rates, anchored on the NT$10,222 owner-reported annual service receipt and the NT$36,000 heavier-service invoice referenced in G20 320i owner threads (https://www.mobile01.com/topicdetail.php?f=275&t=5485763). This period is deliberately heavy and is the honest half of the German ownership story: NT$240,000 over three years, versus roughly NT$70,000-90,000 for an equivalent-age Japanese D-segment sedan. The drivers are calendar-aged consumables coming round a second time, the well-known G20 front control-arm bushing wear, and the B48's oil-leak gasket set - all items an out-of-warranty owner pays in full. This also explains why the year-10 resale tail keeps falling rather than flattening: the used market prices in exactly this repair exposure. Confidence medium: the individual part prices are grounded in Taiwan dealer rates, but which failures actually occur in a given three-year window is probabilistic.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the Taiwan average (~12,000-15,000). All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7000 / 21000 / 35000 / 49000 / 70000). Two consequences run through the record. (1) Resale: every used comparable used here is a genuinely low-mileage listing read off 8891's 420i Coupe inventory page, not a mileage-blind average, and each source string names the listing and the adjustment applied. (2) Maintenance: at 7,000 km/yr the BMW Condition Based Service clock is driven by TIME, not distance - the annual oil service, the 2-year brake fluid change, filters, coolant, the 12V battery and tyre age-out all land on the calendar long before any mileage trigger. The included 3-year/40,000 km BMW Taiwan service package is therefore never mileage-capped for this buyer: 3 years only reaches 21,000 km. Conversely low mileage does NOT protect the later years - rubber, coolant, battery and the B48 water-pump/thermostat/gasket cluster are age-driven and arrive on schedule. Tax and insurance are excluded by design. Fuel and parking are not modelled.

purchase.source: LIST PRICE CONFIRMED, NO CHANGE. NT$2,690,000 verified this round independently of the prior researcher: BMW Taiwan's own launch release states '420i Coupé M Racing Edition 建議售價：269萬元' and '430i Coupé M Racing Edition 建議售價：322萬元', corroborated by UpToGo ('BMW 4-Series Coupe 420i M Racing Edition：新台幣 269 萬元起'), CARLINK ('269萬元起、新年式BMW 4系列全車系鋒格升級') and TVBS/ETtoday ('全車系建議售價自269萬元起'). Deviation from the researcher's figure is 0%, so the price stands. DISCOUNT RAISED, 110,000 -> 160,000 (5.9%). The researcher's 110,000 (4.1%) is implausibly low for BMW Taiwan: the audited BMW X3 record in this same batch documents a real PTT 菜單 of ~12% off list on a 2,490,000 car, and BMW is the heaviest discounter of the German three in Taiwan. I did not raise it to X3 levels because the evidence genuinely differs in two ways: the 4 Series Coupé is a low-volume halo body style rather than a volume SUV fighting GLC/Q5 on price, and the M Racing Edition is a pre-bundled value edition. My searches for current BMW Taiwan promotions returned incentives delivered as 0% financing over 48 months (up to 1,800,000), 一年乙式全險 and a hotel package rather than headline cash, which is consistent with narrower cash room but not with 4%. 160,000 is a judgement anchored between the two, and is flagged in open questions as unverified.
purchase.notes: Full model name is '420i M Racing Edition (Coupé)'; trim shortened to '420i M Racing Ed. Coupé' (23 chars) for the display limit. POWERTRAIN: 'gasoline' is correct. The 420i runs the B48 2.0L turbo four. The prior researcher asserted the Taiwan 420i has NO 48V system at all (only the M440i) and used that to strike the 48V starter-generator out of the later maintenance windows; I could NOT independently confirm that claim this round, so I have not relied on it. The classification is unaffected either way - a 48V mild hybrid cannot move the car on electricity alone and is 'gasoline' under this table's rules - but the maintenance plan no longer claims the 48V risk item is absent, and the year 7-10 electrical provision is worded to absorb a starter-generator if one is fitted. M Racing Edition content over base M Sport: adaptive LED headlights, laser taillights, M Sport advanced package, red M brake calipers, smoked headlight treatment, gloss-black window frames and rear spoiler. ON-ROAD FEES 65,000 = 領牌 + 代辦 ~15,000 plus ~50,000 of delivery accessories at this class (隔熱紙, 行車紀錄器, 腳踏墊, 鍍膜). This is at the top of the plausible band and roughly double the 35,000 carried by the X3 record in this batch on a similarly priced car; a coupé's large glass area and this buyer's likely coating spend justify the gap, but it is the softest number in this block after the discount. Tax and insurance deliberately excluded. real_cost = 2,690,000 - 160,000 + 65,000 = 2,595,000.
