selling_costs.notes: Assumes the owner sells privately (自售), which is what private_sale_price in value_checkpoints represents. Detailing is set at the higher end of the usual range because a 180 萬 German car self-listed against dealer-prepared stock has to present well to hold its asking price. If the owner instead trades in at a dealer, selling costs collapse to roughly the 過戶 line alone — but the proceeds drop to dealer_tradein_price, which is a far bigger loss than the NT$11,500 saved. Total sits inside the normal 6,000-15,000 band for this class.

value_checkpoints.source: No 1-year-old (2025) B 180 進化版 listings exist in the TW used market yet, so this is stepped back from the nearest real data and is the least anchored point in the record. Real dealer ASKING price re-verified on SUM 汽車網 (2026-08, fetched and parsed directly): 2024 W247 B 180 @ 42,060 km = NT$1,099,000 against a 1,790,000 list, i.e. 61.4% dealer retail at 2 years — but at ~21,000 km/yr, roughly 3x this buyer's rate. A 1-year car at only 7,000 km sits above that; dealer retail is put at ~NT$1,420,000 (79% of list). private_sale_price = that dealer asking price MINUS 10% (NT$1,275,000), because 車商售價 includes the dealer's margin, warranty and reconditioning; dealer_tradein_price = a further 14% below private (NT$1,095,000). Year-1 loss is 27.4% of real_cost — the German entry-luxury pattern in Taiwan, not a Japanese one. RESIDUAL RISK, stated openly: the implied year-1 dealer retail of 79% of list sits 17.5 points above the observed year-2 point, which is a steep single-year step; if the run-out clearance on this discontinued model is heavy in late 2026, the true year-1 private price could land NT$50,000-80,000 lower.

Best-supported checkpoint. Real 3-year-old same-generation, same-facelift dealer ASKING prices independently re-verified 2026-08: SUM 汽車網 2023 W247 B 180 @ 43,000 km = NT$1,088,000 (confirmed by direct fetch and parse of the 34-listing result set); FindCar 找車網 (datalist q=B180) 2023 B 180 @ 43,696 km = NT$1,128,000. Median ~NT$1,088,000 against the 2023 facelift list of 1,770,000 = 61.5% dealer retail at ~43,000 km. This buyer's car has only 21,000 km, so a low-mileage premium lifts dealer retail to ~NT$1,160,000 (64% of the 1,800,000 list). private_sale_price = dealer asking minus 11% (NT$1,030,000); dealer_tradein_price = a further 14% below private (NT$885,000). Private sale is 58.7% of real_cost at 3 years — the steep years 1-3 German drop. Confidence DOWNGRADED from 'high' to 'medium' by this fact-check pass: the underlying figures are only two or three dealer ASKING listings, and the number actually recorded is the product of two modelled conversions (a low-mileage premium and a dealer-to-private haircut) for which no observed private-sale transaction data exists. Real asking prices do not make a modelled private price high-confidence.

REVISED DOWN by this fact-check pass (was 860,000 / 735,000). No 2021 W247 listings surfaced, so this is bracketed between real neighbours. The key comparator — which the original pass missed — is SUM 汽車網 2020 W247 B 180 @ 39,800 km asking NT$868,000, verified by direct fetch: that is a 6-year-old car driven ~6,600 km/yr, i.e. almost exactly this buyer's usage profile, and it retains 50.8% of its ~1,710,000 original list as DEALER ASKING. Interpolating between the verified 3-year point (61.5% of list at 43,000 km) and that 6-year point (50.8% at 39,800 km) puts a 5-year car at ~55% of list; mileage is already comparable between those anchors so only a small low-mileage adjustment applies, giving dealer retail ~NT$950,000. private_sale_price = dealer asking minus 11% (NT$845,000); dealer_tradein_price = a further 15% below private (NT$720,000). Private sale = 48.1% of real_cost. Warranty expired at year 3, which the market now prices in. The revision also removes the flat spot in the depreciation rate that the original curve carried.

MATERIALLY REVISED DOWN by this fact-check pass (was 765,000 / 650,000) — this was the record's main defect. Real 7-year-old same-generation dealer ASKING prices, independently re-verified 2026-08. SUM 汽車網: 2019 W247 B 180 @ 68,389 km = NT$838,000; @ 77,869 km = NT$898,000; @ 118,694 km = NT$738,000. FindCar: 2019 @ 80,000 km = NT$958,000; @ 75,381 km = NT$758,000; @ 153,000 km = NT$580,000. Median excluding the 153,000 km outlier is ~NT$838,000 at ~77,000 km, against the 2019 list of 1,630,000 = 51.4%. The original pass set dealer retail at NT$865,000 while claiming to apply two haircuts — but NT$865,000 sits ABOVE the observed median, so the stated haircuts never actually bit, and the resulting private price of NT$765,000 was only ~3% under real dealer ASKING prices. That is the dealer-retail trap. Corrected build: take the 51.4% mileage-typical retention, apply it to this car's 1,800,000 list (NT$925,000), add ~6% for 49,000 km versus the comparators' ~77,000 km (NT$980,000), then apply the haircuts the evidence genuinely demands — (a) these are 車商售價 asking prices on ageing stock, systematically optimistic versus what transacts; (b) today's 2019 asking prices are inflated by Taiwan's post-2021 used-price run-up, which cannot be assumed to persist to 2033; (c) by 2033 the W247 is an orphan, the line is dead with no successor, and the out-of-warranty 1.3 M282 plus 48V BSG carries repair-risk discounting that the pre-facelift 2019 car did not. Net dealer retail ~NT$810,000 (45% of list). private_sale_price = minus 11% (NT$720,000); dealer_tradein_price = a further 15% below private (NT$615,000). This also fixes the broken curve shape: the original ran -10.1%/yr, -8.6%/yr, then FLATTENED to -5.7%/yr across years 5-7 before re-accelerating to -13.2%/yr, which is not a real depreciation shape.

EXTRAPOLATED — the W247 launched in Taiwan in June 2019, so no genuine 10-year data for this generation exists and none was invented. Method: take the PREDECESSOR W246 B 180 (1.6 M270) at 10 years old today, express it as a retention ratio of its own original list price, then apply that ratio to this car's real_cost. Real 2016 W246 B 180 dealer ASKING prices re-verified on SUM 汽車網 by direct fetch, 2026-08: NT$438,000 @ 120,091 km, NT$438,000 @ 110,000 km, NT$458,000 @ 124,516 km — median ~NT$445,000 at ~118,000 km. (The original pass also cited NT$468,000 @ 132,886 km and NT$298,000 @ 178,634 km; neither was present in the live 34-listing result set on re-fetch, so only the three verified rows are relied on here. FindCar independently shows 2016 B 180 at NT$438,000 and NT$458,000, consistent.) W246 B 180 original TW list ~1,550,000 (泳輪汽車 records 'about 150 萬'; a SUM ad for a 2018 運動版 with AMG 套件 states 新車 168 萬). Adjusting the median up ~18% for our 70,000 km car gives ~NT$525,000 = ~34% dealer retail. Applied to this car's 1,800,000 list that yields ~NT$610,000, then haircut to ~NT$570,000 dealer retail because the M282 1.3 (Renault co-developed) has a weaker out-of-warranty reputation than the M270 1.6, the 48V BSG is an expensive orphan part, and the B-Class line is discontinued with no successor. private_sale_price = minus 12% (NT$500,000); dealer_tradein_price = a further 14% (NT$430,000). Private sale = 28.5% of real_cost. The tail keeps falling (-11.4%/yr between years 7 and 10) rather than flattening the way a Lexus does.

maintenance.plan_notes: Servicing is TIME-DRIVEN, not mileage-driven, for this buyer. Mercedes-Benz Taiwan's interval is every 10,000 km OR every 12 months, whichever comes first (比迪行銷 text re-verified by direct fetch: '賓士的保養週期通常會是每 10,000 公里或每年一次（以先到者為準）'); at 7,000 km/year the clock always wins, so the car gets exactly one workshop visit per year and never reaches a mileage-triggered service early. Warranty: Taiwan Mercedes gives a 3-year unlimited-mileage factory warranty as standard (原廠保固 3 年不限里程), which is why years 0-3 carry routine servicing only and no repair risk. Extended warranty covering years 4-6 is SOLD SEPARATELY by authorised dealers and is NOT assumed here — so periods 5, 7 and 10 carry the full unsubsidised out-of-warranty cost, which is where the German-versus-Japanese gap actually opens up. Prepaid 保養套餐 packages are also offered by Mercedes dealers; buying one would shift some of the year 1-5 cost forward at a discount, but no such package was confirmed as standard on the 進化版, so none is assumed. Cost basis (all ranges re-verified by direct fetch of the 比迪行銷 page): Mercedes TW dealer Service A (小保養) NT$8,000-15,000 and Service B (大保養) NT$15,000-30,000 'even higher if it includes 火星塞、變速箱油'; consumables from the same source — tires NT$5,000-15,000 each (this car runs 17-inch wheels, so the low end), brake pads at 30,000-50,000 km with pads+discs NT$15,000-40,000 per set, AGM battery NT$8,000-15,000 lasting 2-4 years, engine/gearbox mounts NT$10,000-25,000, conventional dampers NT$20,000-40,000 per set. Independent shops run roughly half the dealer rate (泳輪汽車 documents a B 180 小保養 under NT$4,000, 'less than half the Mercedes dealer price'); dealer pricing is used throughout because this owner keeps the car serviceable and resaleable. Later periods deliberately carry German-specific risk items: 水龜/thermostat housing and electric water pump, ignition coils and plugs, engine and gearbox mounts, suspension bushings, and the 48V belt-driven starter-generator itself, which is a costly orphan part on a discontinued model. No DPF (petrol) and NO AIR SUSPENSION — the 比迪行銷 source warns that 氣壓式避震器 repairs run tens of thousands per corner, but the B-Class runs conventional steel springs, so that line item is correctly absent. Ten-year total is NT$496,000 (revised up from NT$475,000 by this fact-check pass), roughly double what a comparable Japanese hatchback would absorb over the same distance and in line with the same-drivetrain A 180 and CLA 180.

Chassis-bushing and alignment work was added and the risk basket lifted accordingly. This is a probability-weighted expected value, not a quoted repair — no owner receipts for a 7-year-old W247 were found, hence the low confidence.

The 48V BSG line is a modelled expected value: no TW repair-price data for a belt-driven starter-generator on the M282 was found, and it becomes an orphan part once the B-Class line ends. Explicitly NO air suspension line — the source flags 氣壓式避震器 as a very expensive failure, but the B-Class uses steel springs — and NO DPF, since this is a petrol car. Extrapolated, not sourced from receipts. Unchanged by this fact-check pass.

sources.name: CarBuzz — Mercedes-Benz B-Class Is Dead After The Current Generation
sources.note: INDEPENDENTLY RE-FETCHED AND READ by this fact-check pass, which CORRECTED how it was characterised. By Ian Wright, published 2026-03-13. The article confirms the B-Class dies after the current generation with no successor, but on timing it says only that the 2023 facelift 'makes it LIKELY the B-Class will go out of production later this year or early next year' — i.e. late 2026 or early 2027, speculative. The original research pass rendered this as production 'confirmed to end around June 2026', which is more specific and more certain than the source supports. The discontinuation itself is sound and still justifies (a) the run-out discount on the new car and (b) the extra haircut on the 7-year and 10-year residuals; only the June 2026 date has been removed.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/yr, far below the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000. Every checkpoint uses assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000/21,000/35,000/49,000/70,000). Two consequences. (1) Used values are quoted against LOW-MILEAGE comparables, not the mileage-blind average. My own scrape of 8891 confirms the premium is real: a 2014 C 200 Avantgarde with 50,000 km asks 550,000 while a 2015 C 200 Avantgarde with 155,000 km asks only 449,000 — the older but low-km car is worth 22% more. Within the current generation the same effect appears: a 2023 C 180 with 33,000 km asks 1,398,000 (64.4% of its original list) while 2022-2023 C 200s with 65,000-66,000 km sit at 59-61%. I apply roughly +5 percentage points of retention for this buyer's mileage. (2) Maintenance is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Assyst Plus triggers on '10,000 km or 1 year, whichever first', so this owner always hits the calendar trigger and never the mileage one. POWERTRAIN: EQ Boost is a 48V belt-driven integrated starter-generator (ISG) adding 22 hp of assist to the 1.5L turbo. It cannot move the car on electricity alone, so it is classified 'gasoline', NOT hybrid. Tax (牌照稅/燃料稅) and insurance are excluded by design and appear nowhere in these figures.

purchase.source: List price INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED in this audit against two separate U-CAR surfaces, both fetched directly with a browser user-agent. (1) The U-CAR C-Class model page's live 售價(萬) spec table: C 180 星耀版 225, C 200 星耀版 261, C 300 星耀版 305 — with 1,496 c.c. / 204 hp / 九前速手自排 / 後輪驅動 on the C 200 row. (2) A separate U-CAR answer page independently states 'C 180 星耀版為 225 萬元，C 200 星耀版為 261 萬元，C 300 星耀版為 305 萬元'. NT$2,610,000 CONFIRMED, no change. Discount and on-road figures are market estimates, not quoted prices.
purchase.notes: TRIM LABEL CORRECTED IN THIS AUDIT. The record arrived labelled 'C 200 星耀版 (Avantgarde)'. That is factually wrong: the Taiwan C 200 has carried the AMG Line package as STANDARD equipment since the 23/24 model-year update, and the Avantgarde variant was deleted at that point (KingAutos, 2023-09-29: '23/24年式C200將AMG Line套件列為標配', and for the Estate '取消舊款入門且售價(240萬元起)較親民的C200 Avantgarde車型'). No Avantgarde C 200 has been on sale in Taiwan since 2023. The trim is now 'C 200 星耀版'; the id is left unchanged so the table key stays stable. The original record also contradicted itself by justifying its maintenance costs with 19-inch AMG wheels and AMG sports suspension while calling the car an Avantgarde. 48V MILD HYBRID, CLASSIFIED GASOLINE: U-CAR states the whole range carries EQ Boost providing 22 hp of extra assist. The C 200 pairs a 1,496 cc inline-4 turbo (204 hp, 9G-Tronic, RWD) with a 48V ISG. No electric-only driving, so 'gasoline' per the table's rule. The 2026 星耀版 update added the 夜色套件 (gloss-black mirror caps, window trim and grille), 19-inch AMG wheels and MBUX augmented-reality navigation — the 19-inch wheels matter later, because they make tire replacement materially more expensive than on the 18-inch C 180. DISCOUNT (150,000, 5.7%): W206 launched in Taiwan in Dec 2021, so the combustion C-Class is late-cycle in 2026, and the Electric C-Class was revealed in April 2026 — a known replacement depresses the outgoing car. Taiwanese Benz dealers routinely give 120,000-180,000 cash on a late-cycle C-Class, so 150,000 is realistic rather than optimistic. ON-ROAD (65,000): 領牌+代辦 about 10,000, accessories about 55,000 (window tint, dashcam, ceramic coating, floor mats, sunshade), scaled to this price class. Commodity tax and VAT are already inside the Taiwan list price. PRICE-NARRATIVE NOTE: the U-CAR model page's prose says the 2026 星耀版 rose 10,000 over the 25年式, which read literally implies 2,580,000. The gap is a uniform 30,000 across all three trims, i.e. a later across-the-board adjustment the prose was never updated for — U-CAR's own separate answer page and the live spec table both say 261萬, so 2,610,000 stands.

Detailing is the biggest item because a low-mileage German luxury car only realises its low-mileage premium if it presents that way; on this class 8,000 for paint correction and interior work is normal rather than lavish. value_checkpoints.source: INTERPOLATED, no direct listing — and I verified that absence myself rather than taking it on trust. I scraped 8 pages of 8891's Mercedes-Benz used inventory (6,118 cars listed; 41 C-Class Sedan entries recovered) and the newest C-Class Sedan registration present is 2023. There is genuinely no 2024-2026 W206 sedan on the market, so no 1-year comparable exists. This is bounded interpolation between a known year-0 (list 2,610,000) and the year-3 anchor below, using the German-luxury year-1 pattern: dealer retail asking about 79% of list = 2,062,000; private sale = x0.88 = 1,810,000; trade-in = private x0.87 = 1,570,000. Trimmed from the 1,840,000 the original record carried, to stay consistent with the year-3 anchor I re-based below. A 28.3% loss against real_cost in year one is the steep German first-year hit, deliberately NOT Toyota-like retention.

REAL LISTINGS, current generation, RE-SCRAPED AND RE-BASED IN THIS AUDIT. Confirmed present on 8891 today: a 2023 W206 C 200 at 1,499,000 / 66,000 km, and a 2022-registered C 200 at 1,450,000 / 65,000 km. The original record's second anchor (1,538,000 at 53,000 km) does NOT appear in the live data and I could not reproduce it, so it is dropped. DENOMINATOR CORRECTED: the original used a MY2023 C 200 list of 2,430,000; the correct figure is about 2,470,000 — KingAutos reports the 23/24年式 C 200 rose 80,000 to 2,550,000, so the preceding 23年式 was 2,470,000, and FindCar's MY2023 C 200 新車 average of 2,457,000 corroborates. Against 2,470,000 the two real cars retain 60.7% and 58.7% of list as DEALER ASKING at 3-4 years with 65,000-66,000 km. LOW-MILEAGE ADJUSTMENT, now evidenced rather than assumed: a 2023 C 180 with only 33,000 km asks 1,398,000 against its 2,170,000 original list = 64.4%, the best low-km current-generation comparable available. Our buyer is lower still at 21,000 km, so I use 65% dealer asking = 1,696,500; private sale 12% below dealer retail = 1,493,000 -> 1,490,000; trade-in a further 13% below private = 1,300,000. The 1,450,000-1,499,000 listed figures are 車商售價 and are NOT what the owner receives. Confidence lowered from 'high' to 'medium' because one of the two original anchors could not be reproduced.

BRACKETED between real points; reviewed in this audit and left unchanged. W206 is only about 4 model years old, so year 5 is a one-year extension. Upper bracket, verified today: 4-year-old W206s with high mileage — a 2022-registered C 200 at 1,450,000 / 65,000 km and a 2022 C 180 at 1,280,000 / 69,000 km — sit at 58.7% and 59.5% of their original list. Lower bracket, also verified today: a 2021 W205 C 300 星夜版, 60,000 km, asking 1,180,000 against roughly 2,890,000 = 40.8% at 5 years, though that was a run-out model and so is pessimistic. I set year 5 at 52% dealer asking of 2,610,000 = 1,357,000, inside that bracket and nudged up for our 35,000 km. Private sale = x0.88 = 1,190,000; trade-in = x0.87 = 1,040,000. The year3->year5 drop of about 12 points keeps German mid-life decline steep; it does not flatten.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION — no 7-year-old W206 exists (launched Dec 2021). SOURCE REPLACED IN THIS AUDIT with a data point I verified myself. The original leaned on a 2019 C 300 進化版 at 1,098,000 that I could not find in the live listings. What IS present on 8891 today: a 2019-registered W205 C 200 進化版, 89,200 km, asking 819,000. Its original list was 2,270,000-2,310,000 (a dealer listing quotes 新車價227萬 for the 2019式 C200進化版; FindCar's MY2019 C 200 新車 average is 2,310,000), so that is 35.6% of list as dealer asking at 7 years — on a car with 89,200 km. Our car will have 49,000 km, far below that, so applying the roughly +5 point low-mileage premium evidenced in assumptions gives 41% of 2,610,000 = 1,070,000 dealer asking. Private = x0.88 = 940,000; trade-in = x0.87 = 820,000. Values unchanged from the original record, but they now rest on a listing I confirmed rather than one I could not. Out of warranty by now, and the used market prices in repair risk on a 48V Benz, which is why the tail keeps falling.

EXTRAPOLATED FROM THE PREDECESSOR GENERATION, same method as year 7; all points below re-confirmed in my own 8891 scrape. Real W205 points at age 9-12: 2017 C 200 Exclusive, 130,400 km, 619,000 against roughly 2,320,000 = 26.7%; 2016 C 200 Exclusive, 107,000 km, 598,000 against roughly 2,260,000 = 26.5%; 2015 C 200 Avantgarde, 155,000 km, 449,000 against roughly 2,150,000 = 20.9%; and critically a 2014 C 200 Avantgarde with only 50,000 km asking 550,000 against roughly 2,110,000 = 26% at TWELVE years — the low-km car holds the same ratio as cars two and three years younger, which is what quantifies the low-mileage premium at roughly +5 percentage points. I applied 31% of 2,610,000 = 809,000 dealer asking for our 70,000 km car. Private = x0.88 = 710,000; trade-in = x0.87 = 620,000. Explicitly extrapolated, not observed. Note the tail does not flatten: years 7 to 10 shed another 24% of remaining value.

maintenance.plan_notes: At 7,000 km/yr the schedule is TIME-driven, never mileage-driven: Mercedes Assyst Plus calls service at 10,000 km OR 1 year whichever comes first, so this owner services annually on the calendar and alternates Service A (小保養) with Service B (大保養). Taiwan dealer pricing used: Service A 8,000-15,000 (I use 12,000-15,000 for a C-Class 4-cyl), Service B 12,000-30,000 (18,000-22,000 basic with brake fluid, higher when plugs/transmission fluid fall due). WARRANTY, re-verified in this audit: Mercedes-Benz Taiwan's standard new-car cover is 3 years unlimited mileage, and the 4th-6th year extension is a separately PURCHASED option, not standard. The basic warranty covers defects only — routine servicing is still PAID from year 1, so no early-period subsidy is applied. Prepaid service packages (保養套餐) exist but are an optional purchase and are deliberately not netted off. The extension is NOT assumed, so years 4-10 carry the FULL unsubsidised cost including out-of-warranty risk. (Current dealer promotions bundle a one-year warranty extension and first-year 乙式 insurance, but a promotion is not a standard entitlement, so it is excluded.) Why this must exceed a Japanese equivalent: dealer labour rates, 19-inch AMG wheels making a tire set 48,000-52,000 rather than 20,000-25,000, larger brakes, and genuine German risk items — thermostat housing, electric water pump, coil packs, and above all the 48V ISG starter-generator, a mild-hybrid-specific part that costs 60,000-120,000 to replace and has no counterpart on a naturally-aspirated Toyota. Ten-year total is 540,000, averaging 54,000/yr — roughly double a RAV4, which is the correct relationship. The schedule was reviewed line by line in this audit and left unchanged; it sits slightly above the GLC 200's 480,000, which is defensible given the 星耀版 runs 19-inch AMG rubber, though the two cars share an engine family and could reasonably be closer.

checkpoints.source: Tire set 32,000-45,000 per the Taiwan guides, pushed to 48,000 because the 2026 星耀版 runs 19-inch AMG wheels (low-profile rubber, not the 18-inch base fitment) — a spec confirmed in this audit from U-CAR's own 星耀版 description. Brake pads 15,000-30,000 quoted at 30,000-50,000 km; took the low end since 35,000 gentle km is easy on pads. The step up from 32,000 to 103,000 is the warranty expiring plus the first tire set landing in the same window — at this mileage tires are replaced on AGE (5-6 years), not wear.

Fully out of warranty: the 25,000 risk line is a probability-weighted allowance for the German items the brief calls out — thermostat housing, electric water pump, coil packs — not a certainty of failure.

Second tire set, 19-inch AMG — 52,000
48V ISG starter-generator / mild-hybrid module, risk-weighted — 35,000
Electric water pump / thermostat housing — 20,000
Coil packs + spark plugs — 12,000

Suspension bushings / dampers (age, not mileage) — 40,000
12V battery — 11,000

checkpoints.source: Suspension 30,000-60,000 and major electrical 15,000-80,000 per the Taiwan dealer guides; second tire set on age again. The 35,000 for the 48V ISG is the mild-hybrid-specific line the brief asks for: a full replacement runs 60,000-120,000 in Taiwan, weighted down for the chance it survives. Deliberately NOT a RAV4-like tail — a 9-year-old Benz out of warranty is where the money goes, and low mileage does not protect rubber, coolant, batteries or 48V electronics, all of which fail on age.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use the 7,000 km/year midpoint, so assumed_km = 7,000 x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). At this mileage Mercedes' 1-year-or-10,000 km service interval is triggered by TIME, not distance, so the car is serviced annually and never reaches a mileage-based interval early; consumables such as tyres and brake fluid age out rather than wear out. Licence tax (牌照稅), fuel tax (燃料稅), insurance and fuel are deliberately EXCLUDED from every figure per the table's design. Powertrain is classified 'gasoline' per this table's rule that a 48V mild hybrid is not a hybrid — see purchase.notes for the corrected technical description of the system. Resale figures assume the car stays in the low-mileage band, and every used-market anchor used below is a LOW-MILEAGE listing rather than a mileage-blind average, because low-mileage cars sell above that average in Taiwan.

purchase.source: List price INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED and CONFIRMED at NT$1,920,000. Primary evidence is a first-hand fetch of UDN 汽車 (autos.udn.com/autos/story/124115/9391149), which loads and quotes all four variants verbatim: 「Mercedes-Benz CLA 200 with EQ Technology，建議售價 187 萬元起」／「CLA 250+ with EQ Technology，建議售價 220 萬元起」／「CLA 180，建議售價 192 萬元起」／「CLA 220，建議售價 225 萬元起」. Corroborated by search-result snippets from U-CAR (headline 「純電187萬、燃油192萬元起」, body 「燃油車型則具備CLA 180以及CLA 220兩款車型，新車售價分別為192萬元以及225萬元」), Auto-Online, TVBS 地球黃金線 and a PTT repost, all giving CLA 180 = 192萬. CAUTION FOR FUTURE EDITORS: the 8891 launch article states only the band 「價格帶落在187～225萬間」 and gives no per-variant table, so an automated read of it can wrongly attribute 187萬 to the CLA 180 — 187萬 is the electric CLA 200 with EQ Technology. mercedes-benz.com.tw timed out on every attempt, so the official brand page was again not read first-hand.
purchase.notes: 48V MILD HYBRID — CLASSIFIED 'gasoline' FOR THIS TABLE. Powertrain is the M252 1.5L turbo four, 136hp / 20.4kgm, 0-100 km/h in 8.8s, driving through an 8-speed dual-clutch automatic. CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR RESEARCH: this generation's 48V unit is NOT a belt-driven starter-generator that only does torque fill and stop/start. The electric machine (~27-30hp) is integrated INSIDE the 8-speed DCT, and Mercedes markets low-load 'electric sailing' on it, so the claim that it 'cannot move the car on electricity at all' is factually wrong. The classification is still 'gasoline', because this table's rule places all 48V mild hybrids (Mercedes EQ Boost/ISG, BMW 48V, Audi MHEV) in 'gasoline' and reserves 'hybrid' for full/series hybrids — but the verdict now rests on the table's rule rather than on an incorrect technical claim. The integrated 48V motor also matters for cost in the other direction: it is buried in the gearbox, which makes it an expensive out-of-warranty failure item, budgeted probability-weighted in the years 7-10 window. Discount of NT$40,000 (~2.1%) is deliberately modest: the car is five months into a brand-new generation and Mercedes-Benz Taiwan already cut NT$70,000 off every variant versus the pre-order price at launch (8891: 「各車型均較預售價再降7萬」), which absorbed most of the negotiating room. For comparison the run-out A 180 in this dataset carries a 3.6% discount; a fresh CLA should not. On-road fees of NT$65,000 = 領牌與規費 ~NT$10,000 + 代辦費 ~NT$5,000 + delivery accessories ~NT$50,000 (隔熱紙, 行車紀錄器, 鍍膜, 腳踏墊, 車美仕小件); this is 3.4% of list, matching the 3.3% used by the A 180 sibling record in the same dataset. Tax and insurance excluded by design. real_cost = 1,920,000 - 40,000 + 65,000 = 1,945,000.

selling_costs.notes: Private-sale costs for a car in this class. 過戶 regulatory fee plus an agent to handle it runs about NT$2,500; pre-sale detailing (wash, polish, interior clean, minor scratch touch-up) is worth about NT$6,000 on a NT$1.9M German car because presentation moves the price materially; listing plus a paid exposure boost on 8891 is about NT$2,500. Total NT$11,000 sits in the normal 6,000-15,000 band and matches the NT$12,000 used by the A 180 sibling record. A dealer trade-in avoids most of this but at a far lower price, which is why both exit routes are quoted separately in value_checkpoints.

value_checkpoints.source: REVISED DOWN from a prior estimate of NT$1,460,000 (76% retention), which was too high for a German car in year 1. No C174 data can exist — the car launched in Taiwan on 2026-03-19, five months ago. Anchor is the direct predecessor at the same age: 8891 中古車 currently lists a MY2025 C118 CLA 200 at NT$1,700,000 @11,100 km (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/cla/cla200). Against the facelift CLA 200 list of NT$2,090,000 that is 81.3% DEALER ASKING retention; cutting 11% to reach a private-sale figure gives 72.4%. Applying 72% to NT$1,920,000 gives NT$1,380,000, i.e. an implied dealer asking of about NT$1,550,000. Cross-checks: the A 180 platform sibling in this dataset uses 70.3% at year 1, and a brand-new CLA 180 can be bought for about NT$1,880,000 net of discount, so a one-year-old must sit clearly below that. Two effects partly cancel — the MY2025 predecessor is a run-out model (depresses it) while the C174 is a fresh generation with waiting lists (supports it) — so the predecessor ratio is used as-is. Confidence stays low: this rests on a single predecessor listing and zero data for the actual car.

REVISED UP from NT$1,150,000. Anchored on REAL listings of the direct predecessor at exactly this age and this mileage. 8891 中古車 currently shows MY2023 C118 CLA 200 (facelift, Taiwan list NT$2,090,000, verified via U-CAR 「正式售價分別為209萬及214萬元起」) at NT$1,498,000 @19,500 km, NT$1,458,000 @20,000 km and NT$1,450,000 @20,000 km, with higher-mileage cars falling to NT$1,388,000 @56,000 km and NT$1,250,000 @50,000 km. The prior research used a NT$1,420,000 dealer anchor, which is BELOW this low-mileage cluster — wrong direction, given the buyer profile explicitly calls for low-mileage listings. Correct low-mileage dealer asking is about NT$1,470,000. These are 車商售價 (dealer RETAIL asking), not what an owner receives; cutting 11% gives a private sale of about NT$1,308,000, i.e. 62.6% retention of that car's list. Applying 62% to NT$1,920,000 gives NT$1,190,000 (implied dealer asking about NT$1,337,000). Dealer trade-in a further 13% below private sale. The ~38% three-year loss is the German pattern and is far steeper than a Japanese equivalent.

REVISED UP from NT$900,000 (47%), which was internally impossible: the prior record's own five-year figure sat BELOW what real six- and seven-year-old predecessors are actually asking. Interpolated between two real anchors on the direct predecessor. Upper anchor is the year-3 MY2023 cluster above (62.6% private). Lower anchor is 8891's MY2020 C118 CLA 200 at NT$1,058,000 @53,000 km — against the pre-facelift list of NT$1,880,000 (confirmed at launch, 「售價188萬起」) that is 56.3% dealer asking, so 50.1% private at SIX years, on a car carrying more mileage than ours would. A MY2019 at NT$990,000 @117,000 km is consistent with it. Five years therefore lands near 50%, not 47%: 0.50 x 1,920,000 = NT$960,000, dealer trade-in 13.5% below. Held at exactly 50% rather than the 53-54% a straight interpolation would give, because the predecessor cluster is spec-inflated (AMG Line, heavy options) and because the C174 will be mid-cycle with a facelift on sale by 2031. Deliberately noted: MY2022 listings (NT$1,580,000-1,668,000 at ~10,000 km) ask MORE than same-condition MY2023 cars, which is a COVID-era pricing artefact and was excluded rather than used to lift this figure.

EXTRAPOLATED from the PREVIOUS generation, as required — no C174 and no C118 car is seven years old at a comparable point. Uses the C117 CLA (Taiwan list taken as ~NT$1,890,000 for CLA 200; see open questions, this denominator could NOT be verified first-hand and directly scales the answer). 8891 shows MY2018 C117 cars, now eight years old, asking NT$688,000 @79,000 km, NT$659,000 @113,000 km and NT$588,000 @119,000 km. Our car would be at only ~56,000 km at eight years, so a ~8-10% low-mileage premium over the NT$688,000 car gives a dealer asking near NT$750,000; cutting 11% for private sale gives about NT$665,000, i.e. ~35% eight-year retention. Interpolating back to seven years gives ~40%, and 0.40 x 1,920,000 = NT$770,000. Held at 40% rather than the ~45% the newer C118 six-year point would imply, because the C117 is the only generation with real data at this age and the used market openly prices in out-of-warranty repair risk once the 3-year factory warranty is long gone — the curve keeps falling here rather than flattening the way a Lexus would. Dealer trade-in a further 14% below private sale. Sibling cross-check: the A 180 record uses 36.7% at year 7.

EXTRAPOLATED from the PREVIOUS generation, and the best-evidenced point on the curve after year 3. Real C117 listings on 8891 today at almost exactly our assumed mileage: MY2016 (ten years old) asking NT$630,000 @64,000 km and NT$658,000 @69,000 km, against NT$558,000 @120,000 km for a high-mileage example. Our car at ten years has ~70,000 km, so the NT$630,000-658,000 pair are direct analogues and NO speculative low-mileage premium is needed — this corrects the prior method, which applied a 15% premium to the 120,000 km car and only coincidentally landed in the same place. Low-mileage dealer asking is therefore about NT$645,000; cutting 11% gives a private sale of about NT$574,000, i.e. ~30.3% retention of that car's ~NT$1,890,000 list. Applying 30% to NT$1,920,000 gives NT$575,000. A MY2016 at NT$246,000 was excluded as an outlier (almost certainly accident-damaged or a finance headline). Dealer trade-in cut a full 15% below private sale, the widest gap on the curve, because dealers price aged out-of-warranty German stock defensively. Confidence stays low despite the good listing cluster, because the C117 list price used as the denominator is unverified.

maintenance.plan_notes: At 7,000 km/year the service clock is TIME-driven, not mileage-driven: Mercedes' interval is 1 year or 10,000 km whichever comes first, and this car never reaches 10,000 km in a year, so it goes in annually and alternates Service A (小保養) with Service B (大保養). Taiwan dealer pricing aggregated from cost guides and Mobile01 owner posts puts Service A at NT$8,000-15,000 and Service B at NT$15,000-30,000; ~NT$11,000 and ~NT$20,000 are used for this 1.5L entry model, rising in later windows as out-of-warranty labour and parts prices climb. WARRANTY: Mercedes-Benz Taiwan gives 3 years UNLIMITED mileage from delivery, which covers manufacturing and assembly defects but NOT routine servicing — Taiwan does not bundle free scheduled maintenance as standard, so years 0-3 still carry full service invoices and are merely free of repair risk. Verified caveat: Mercedes-Benz Taiwan does periodically run campaigns that throw in a 3年保養套裝 on CLA-class cars, and dealers separately sell 4th-6th-year extended warranty and prepaid service packages at early-bird rates. Neither is assumed here, so every window carries the full unsubsidised cost; if a launch-period free service package applies, years 1 and 3 are overstated by roughly NT$46,000 combined. Consumables are placed by AGE, not distance: first tyre set at year 5 (aged out at only 35,000 km), first 12V AGM battery around year 4-5, front brakes years 3-5, rear brakes years 5-7, second tyre set and second battery in years 7-10. Later windows carry the German out-of-warranty risk items this class actually suffers: ignition coil packs, thermostat housing, electric auxiliary water pump, dual-clutch transmission fluid service, and the 48V electric machine — which on this generation is integrated inside the 8-speed DCT rather than belt-driven, making it a NT$60,000-90,000 job if it fails; it is budgeted probability-weighted, not as a certainty. No air suspension is fitted to a CLA 180, so that item is excluded rather than padded in. CORRECTION vs the prior research: the gearbox is an 8-speed dual-clutch, not the older 7G-DCT, and per-corner tyre and brake pricing was overstated for a car on 225/45R18 — those unit costs were trimmed to match the A 180 platform sibling, which quotes NT$32,000-34,000 per tyre set for the same size. Ten-year total is NT$509,000, against NT$502,000 for that A 180 sibling, NT$480,000 for the GLC 200 and about NT$185,000 for a Toyota Camry over the same 70,000 km — roughly 2.7x the Japanese equivalent, which is the honest answer for this car.

The Assyst Plus service computer sets the A/B code from time, mileage and driving pattern, and at 7,000 km/year the annual trigger always comes first. Brake fluid falls inside the Service B package at the 2-year mark. No wear parts due yet at 21,000 km. Matches the NT$35,000 the A 180 sibling record uses for the same window.

First tyre set — 4x 225/45R18 premium tyres fitted, ~NT$34,000 (aged out, not worn out, at only 35,000 km)
Front brake pads + discs, ~NT$24,000

Coolant change and miscellaneous, ~NT$8,000
Factory warranty expires during this window (end of year 3)
checkpoints.source: Two dealer services plus age-driven consumables. Tyre cost taken at NT$8,000-9,000 per corner fitted for 18-inch premium rubber, giving ~NT$34,000 a set — trimmed from a prior NT$40,000, which overstated a CLA-sized fitment; the A 180 sibling record quotes NT$32,000 for the same 225/45R18. Front pads and discs at a Mercedes dealer trimmed to ~NT$24,000 on the same basis. AGM batteries for this platform run about NT$12,000. This is the first window carrying real wear cost and the first outside warranty, which is exactly where the German cost curve separates from a Japanese one.

major_items: Service B (year 6) + Service A (year 7) at full out-of-warranty rates — ~NT$31,000
Spark plugs, 4 cylinders, ~NT$8,000
Rear brake pads + discs, ~NT$22,000
Out-of-warranty risk budget ~NT$30,000: ignition coil packs, thermostat housing, sensors
Coolant, brake fluid, A/C service, ~NT$10,000
No air suspension on a CLA 180, so that common German line item does not apply
checkpoints.source: Two dealer services plus wear and early out-of-warranty failure items. Supported by Taiwan cost guides noting the 60,000 km major cycle (transmission fluid, spark plugs, belts) can push a single visit past NT$40,000, and by an owner report of a ~NT$230,000 bill at 7.5 years covering brake discs, pads, water pipes and belts. Risk items are probability-weighted, not assumed certain. Itemised Taiwan dealer pricing for coil packs and thermostat housing could not be found in any source, so those figures are estimates and this window is marked low.

major_items: Three dealer services across the window (B + A + B), ~NT$53,000 at aged-car rates
Second tyre set, ~NT$36,000
Front brake pads + discs, second replacement, ~NT$26,000
Second 12V AGM battery, ~NT$13,000
48V electric machine integrated in the DCT — NT$60,000-90,000 if it fails, budgeted at ~NT$32,000 probability-weighted
8-speed dual-clutch transmission fluid and filter service, ~NT$18,000
Electric auxiliary water pump + thermostat housing, ~NT$28,000
Coil packs, sensors, suspension bushings and dampers, ~NT$30,000
Coolant, brake fluid, miscellaneous, ~NT$12,000
checkpoints.source: Extrapolated out-of-warranty cost for a 7-10 year old Mercedes in Taiwan, built item by item rather than as a lump sum. Grounded in Taiwan dealer cost guides (大保養 NT$16,000-25,000 rising past NT$40,000 at major cycles, one owner quoted NT$58,000 for a comprehensive service before additional cooling work) and the ~NT$230,000 / 7.5-year owner report. Two corrections to the prior research applied here: the gearbox is an 8-speed dual-clutch, not a 7G-DCT, and the second tyre set and front brake job were trimmed to CLA-appropriate unit costs. The 48V machine is the specific mild-hybrid risk item for this powertrain and is worse than a belt-driven starter-generator because it sits inside the transmission; no Taiwan source gives itemised pricing for it, so both the failure cost and the weighting are estimates, and this window is marked low.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year, far below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/year. All checkpoints use assumed_km = 7000 * years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000). Because low-mileage cars sell above the mileage-blind average, every value checkpoint is anchored on LOW-MILEAGE 8891 listings of the closest siblings (2023 EQA 250 at 10,200 km, 2023 EQB 300 at 16,000 km), not on the whole listing spread. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: tax and insurance. Also EXCLUDED from maintenance (but a real ownership cost): home charger installation - a 7-11 kW wallbox in a Taiwanese apartment building typically runs NT$40,000-80,000 including the Taipower meter application and riser wiring, and can exceed NT$100,000 if the building must first pass a collective-housing EV charging permit; budget it separately. Taiwan BEVs are 牌照稅-exempt through 2030 and the 貨物稅 reduction is understood to be already inside the NT$1,870,000 list price, so neither is a further saving to model here (this audit could not re-fetch the official page to confirm the 貨物稅 wording - mercedes-benz.com.tw times out from this network - so it is reported as the researcher's reading, not as re-verified fact). Electricity cost is not modelled. At 7,000 km/year the servicing schedule is TIME-driven, never mileage-driven: the car never reaches a mileage trigger before a calendar one.

U-CAR model page fetched directly on 2026-08-12 (direct curl returns HTTP 200; WebFetch and the r.jina.ai proxy are both 403-blocked by Cloudflare, so a proxy failure is not evidence the page is fake): the CLA with EQ Technology line reads '187 - 220 萬, 2 車型', with the model table listing 'CLA 200 with EQ Technology 187 / 純電動 / 後輪驅動' and 'CLA 250+ with EQ Technology 220'. Corroborated by the official mercedes-benz.com.tw page title '187萬起！擁有全新 Mercedes-Benz CLA | 台灣賓士' dated 2026-03-19 as indexed, by TVBS '187萬入手豪華電車！賓士全新大改款 CLA 台灣開賣 售價降7萬' (2026-03-24) and by Mobile01 '【採訪】再降7萬，純電與油電齊發！Mercedes-Benz全新 CLA 187萬' (2026-03-19). Four independent confirmations, 0% deviation. Discount and on-road figures are modelled estimates, justified in notes.
purchase.notes: Full official Taiwan model name is 'CLA 200 with EQ Technology' (shortened in the trim field to fit the display-label length limit). SPEC RE-VERIFIED from the U-CAR model page: 純電動 (full BEV) on the new MMA platform, 單永磁同步馬達後輪驅動 (single permanent-magnet motor, RWD), 224 hp, 34.2 kgm, 58 kWh usable battery, 542 km WLTP. Correctly classified 'bev'. It is NOT the 48V mild-hybrid CLA: the combustion CLA 180/220 (1.5L turbo + 48V 輕油電, 8-speed DCT, front-wheel drive, NT$1,920,000/NT$2,250,000) is a separate car and is classified 'gasoline' in its own record. The 800V architecture, 85 kWh pack and 792 km WLTP belong to the CLA 250+ at NT$2,200,000, not to this 200. PRICE HISTORY, which matters for residuals: Taiwan Mercedes published a pre-sale price of NT$1,940,000 in October 2025, then launched on 2026-03-19 at NT$1,870,000 - a NT$70,000 official cut before the first customer deliveries, independently confirmed by both the TVBS ('售價降7萬') and Mobile01 ('再降7萬') launch headlines. That cut is already inside the list price and is deliberately NOT double-counted in discounts. It also puts the electric CLA 200 BELOW the combustion CLA 180 (NT$1,920,000). DISCOUNTS: NT$60,000 (~3.2% of list) modelled as the realistic negotiated package - Mercedes Taiwan on a model only ~5 months old typically gives accessory credit and registration support rather than deep cash off, and the headline price was just cut, which absorbs some of the room a stale model would offer. Deliberately more modest than the NT$100,000-200,000 available on slow-moving EQ metal like the EQB and EQE. ONROAD_FEES: NT$55,000 = 領牌規費 and plates ~NT$7,000 + 代辦 agency fee ~NT$4,000 + 配件 ~NT$44,000 (mats, window film, dashcam, paint coating, charging cables - scaled to a NT$1.87M luxury car). Tax and insurance are excluded by design and are not in this figure.

售前整備與美容 (pre-sale prep and detailing)

selling_costs.notes: Costs the SELLER pays to complete a private sale in Taiwan. 過戶 government fee is small (~NT$1,200) plus a 代辦 agent to handle the monitoring-station paperwork. Detailing is set at the higher end of normal because a BEV that has sat on a slow-moving used market needs to present well, and because these figures assume a private sale rather than dumping the car at a 車商 trade-in (where the dealer absorbs prep but pays the much lower dealer_tradein_price instead). Excludes any loan settlement fee. Total NT$12,000 sits inside the normal NT$6,000-15,000 band for this class.

value_checkpoints.source: EXTRAPOLATED, but the researcher's supporting claim was FALSE and is corrected here. The record asserted 8891 shows ZERO listings for the CLA with EQ Technology and that 'the whole Mercedes BEV range shows no 1-year-old cars at all'. The live 8891 CLA board (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/cla, 545 cars, read 2026-08-12) in fact carries 'M-Benz CLA 2026款 CLA 250+ 純電, 2026年, 8,000公里, 217.0萬', flagged 車行勿擾喔！ - i.e. a genuine 個人自售 PRIVATE listing of this exact model line at ~5 months old, asking 98.6% of the CLA 250+'s NT$2,200,000 list. That is an aspirational asking price on a near-new car from a seller anchored to what he paid, not a transacted 1-year value, so it is NOT used to set this figure; it is recorded as a weak UPPER-BOUND signal that argues against going lower than modelled here. The number itself comes from the German-BEV first-year loss pattern applied to the verified NT$1,870,000 list: implied dealer retail asking ~NT$1,440,000 (77% of list), from which private sale is set ~11% BELOW dealer asking (NT$1,280,000) and dealer trade-in a further ~13% below private (NT$1,110,000). The steep 31% first-year loss is deliberate and is corroborated by Mercedes cutting NT$70,000 before deliveries began. Private sale at 68.4% of list sits correctly inside the German BEV band and just below the combustion CLA 180's year-1 position, which is the right relationship. A German BEV holding Toyota-like year-1 value would be wrong.

Derived from real LOW-MILEAGE sibling listings on 8891, every one of which this audit re-fetched and confirmed line by line on 2026-08-12. EQA 250 (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/eqa, 10 cars nationwide, current list NT$2,170,000): 2023 cars asking 140.0萬 at 1.02萬公里, 135.0萬 at 3.7萬公里, 125.0萬 at 4萬公里, 122.0萬 at 1.4萬公里 - low-mileage 3-year dealer retail ~NT$1,350,000 = 62% of list. EQB 300 4MATIC (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/eqb, 11 cars nationwide, current list NT$2,670,000): 2023 cars asking 158.0萬 at 1.6萬公里 and 155.0萬 at 3.15萬公里 = ~59% of list. Applying that 59-62% dealer-retail band to the CLA's NT$1,870,000 gives ~NT$1,120,000 dealer asking. ADJUSTMENT MADE: those are 車商售價 (dealer RETAIL asking, most tagged 實體車行), not what an owner receives - private sale set ~11% below at NT$1,000,000, and dealer trade-in a further ~13% below at NT$870,000. KNOWN LIMITATION, unchanged from the original: the denominators are CURRENT list prices, while the 2023 cars were sold at 2022/2023 prices, so the ratio is a close proxy rather than an exact retention.

EXTRAPOLATED from the older end of the Mercedes BEV curve on 8891, re-fetched and confirmed by this audit 2026-08-12. Bracketing points: a 2022 EQA 250 with 9.5萬公里 asks 99.6萬 (46% of the EQA's NT$2,170,000 list) at ~4 years; 2022 EQB 300s with 7.63萬-13.45萬公里 ask 106.8萬-113.8萬 (40-43% of list). Implied CLA dealer retail at 5 years ~NT$843,000 = 45% of list - set at the upper end of that band precisely because this car has only 35,000 km where the EQA/EQB comparators have 76,300-134,500 km. Private sale set ~11% below dealer asking (NT$750,000), trade-in ~14% below private (NT$645,000). Confidence is low: no Mercedes compact BEV has yet traded at 5 years in Taiwan, and the car is out of its 3-year warranty by this point, which the used market prices in. At 40% of list this sits correctly among the German BEV peers and well below the combustion CLA 180's 5-year position.

EXTRAPOLATED VIA PREDECESSOR-GENERATION RATIO - no 7-year data exists for any Mercedes compact BEV in Taiwan. DENOMINATOR CORRECTED BY THIS AUDIT: the researcher divided by ~NT$3,290,000, but all three EQC cars on 8891 are the 400 4Matic 運動版, whose Taiwan launch price was NT$3,500,000 (NT$3,290,000 corresponds to the cheaper base ELECTRIC ART trim, so the original ratio was computed against the wrong variant and flattered retention). The listings re-confirmed 2026-08-12 (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/eqc, only 3 cars in the whole country): 2020 EQC 400 4Matic 運動版 asking 108.0萬 at 3萬公里, 108.0萬 at 3.6萬公里, and 99.0萬 at 12.9萬公里. Against the correct NT$3,500,000 that is 30.9% dealer-retail retention at 6 years even at 30,000 km, not the ~33% claimed. Extending one year gives ~28% of list, then adding back ~3-4 points because the CLA is a much cheaper car (cheaper cars retain a higher percentage) on a far better and newer platform (542 km vs the EQC's 417 km) gives ~31% = ~NT$580,000 dealer asking; private sale set ~12% below (NT$510,000), trade-in ~15% below private (NT$435,000). The corrected denominator and the added relative adjustment roughly cancel, so the figures themselves are retained. The tail keeps falling rather than flattening the way a Lexus does, because the car is four years out of its 3-year warranty and the market prices in high-voltage repair risk. Confidence low: single weak comparator (3 listings) of a different, larger, discontinued model, and the EQC launch price could not be re-fetched in this session.

CORRECTED BY AUDIT (was NT$230,000 private / NT$190,000 trade-in). The original rested on a single bad anchor: 'a 2016 CLA 200 with 50,000 km asks NT$246,000 on 8891 = 14% dealer-retail retention at 10 years'. Re-reading that board (auto.8891.com.tw/mercedes-benz/cla, 545 cars, 2026-08-12) shows the listing is a 2016 CLA250 (2017款), not a CLA 200, and its title is 【買車送你一年車貸，限時優惠中】 - a financing-hook bait price, and an extreme outlier against every comparable on the same page: 2016 CLA200 at 12萬公里 asks 55.8萬, 2017 CLA200 at 11萬公里 asks 55.8萬, 2015 CLA250 at 11.82萬公里 asks 62.9萬, 2018 CLA250 at 8萬公里 asks 69.8萬, 2014 CLA250 at 5.5萬公里 asks 47.7萬. The real 10-year low-mileage combustion CLA sits at ~NT$550,000-700,000 dealer retail, i.e. ~30-35% of list, NOT 14% - and that is consistent with the combustion CLA 180 record in this same batch. Rebuilt on the correct anchor: take the combustion CLA's genuine ~32% 10-year dealer-retail retention and apply a heavy BEV penalty, because the ~8-year high-voltage battery warranty has lapsed inside this window and a pack replacement approaches the whole value of the car, which the Taiwan used market discounts hard. That gives ~18% of list = ~NT$345,000 dealer asking; private sale ~13% below (NT$300,000), trade-in ~15% below private (NT$255,000) - at this value many dealers will only offer scrap-adjacent money. Private at 16.0% of list still sits at the weak end of the German BEV peer group and is roughly HALF the combustion CLA's 10-year retention, so the BEV penalty is preserved; the tail still falls steeply from 27% at year 7 rather than flattening. Explicitly extrapolated - no BEV of any German brand has reached 10 years old in Taiwan - hence low confidence.

maintenance.plan_notes: TIME-DRIVEN, NOT MILEAGE-DRIVEN. At 7,000 km/year this car never reaches a mileage service trigger before the calendar one, so every interval below is set by time - roughly a workshop visit every year, with the substantive service falling every two years. TOTALS REBASED BY THIS AUDIT: the original 10-year total was NT$512,000, which was higher than the combustion CLA 180's NT$509,000 in this same batch and higher than the far larger Mercedes EQE 300 SUV's NT$469,000, while the plan notes simultaneously claimed the car was 'materially below an equivalent combustion German compact'. Its years 5-7 (NT$125,000 vs the combustion CLA's NT$105,000) and 7-10 (NT$255,000 vs NT$248,000) actually placed the BEV ABOVE the combustion car, which cannot be right: this car has no engine oil, no filters, no spark plugs, no coil packs, no turbo, no thermostat housing, no timing chain, no DPF, no DCT clutch or mechatronic service, and no 48V starter-generator, and regenerative braking spares the pads. The curve is rebased to a 10-year total of NT$375,000 (~NT$37,500/year), which keeps it clearly above the Japanese BEV benchmark in this batch (Toyota bZ4X, NT$200,000) and above the Volvo EC40 (NT$251,500, reflecting Mercedes' higher dealer labour rates and larger wheels), while landing correctly BELOW the German combustion compacts (CLA 180 NT$509,000, A180 NT$502,000, GLA 200 NT$540,000). WARRANTY POSITION (ASSUMED, NOT RE-VERIFIED): Mercedes-Benz Taiwan is understood to give 3 years unlimited-mileage vehicle warranty, 2 years on the 12V battery, and a per-model high-voltage traction battery warranty that for BEVs is typically 8 years. This audit could NOT re-fetch mercedes-benz.com.tw (the host times out from this network, returning HTTP 000), so the warranty and 保養 A/A Plus/B/B Plus service-scheme claims are carried forward as the researcher's reading rather than as facts re-verified here - which is why every maintenance confidence below is now 'low'. Taiwan is understood NOT to bundle free scheduled maintenance, so routine servicing is paid from day one and the 0-1 and 1-3 periods are low but NOT zero: the warranty covers repairs, not consumables. From year 3 the owner carries the FULL UNSUBSIDISED cost at Mercedes dealer labour rates. BEV-SPECIFIC SHAPE: genuinely much cheaper than combustion, but nowhere near zero - the car is heavy and torque-rich so 19-inch tyres wear faster and are dealer-priced; brake DISCS corrode from disuse in humid Taiwan precisely BECAUSE regen means the friction brakes are rarely used; brake fluid and battery/power-electronics coolant still need changing on a calendar schedule; the 12V battery still dies roughly every 4-5 years and immobilises the car when it does; and out of warranty the expensive failures are electronic (on-board charger, DC-DC converter, heat pump, MBUX head unit, HV coolant pump) rather than mechanical. NOTE: home charger installation is an ownership cost but is NOT maintenance and is excluded here - see assumptions.notes.

major_items: First annual inspection (standard check itself is free at a Mercedes dealer; parts and labour billed)
Cabin/AC filter
Wiper blades
Four-wheel alignment and tyre rotation
checkpoints.source: Modelled on the Mercedes-Benz Taiwan service structure (保養 A / A Plus / B / B Plus scheme) plus the 3-year unlimited-mileage warranty. Cost is low because all repairs are warranty-covered and at 7,000 km almost nothing is consumed; it is not zero because Taiwan is understood to bundle no free scheduled maintenance. CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED BY AUDIT from medium to low: Mercedes Taiwan publishes no EQ servicing price table, no owner receipt could be retrieved (Mobile01 blocks automated access), and this audit could not re-fetch mercedes-benz.com.tw at all (HTTP 000, host times out), so even the warranty and service-scheme structure that bounds this figure is unconfirmed. A modelled dealer-rate estimate, not a quote.

major_items: Brake fluid change (2-year calendar item)
Two annual inspections with labour
Cabin/AC filters x2
Wiper blades and alignment
All repairs still covered by the 3-year unlimited-mileage warranty
checkpoints.source: Covers years 1-3 only (not cumulative). Bounded by the assumed 3-year unlimited-mileage Mercedes-Benz Taiwan warranty, which means the owner pays only calendar consumables and labour in this window - brake fluid is the one substantive item. CONFIDENCE DOWNGRADED BY AUDIT from medium to low for the same reason as year 1: the warranty term and the 保養 A/B structure that bound this number could not be re-verified in this session, and Mercedes Taiwan publishes no EQ service price list. Modelled dealer-rate estimate.

major_items: First tyre replacement - four 19-inch tyres fitted at dealer (~NT$38,000); at 35,000 km they age out rather than wear out
12V battery replacement (~NT$14,000) - still dies on a BEV and disables the car
Battery and power-electronics coolant service (~NT$10,000)
Brake fluid change
Two annual inspections at full unsubsidised dealer labour rates
Cabin filters x2, wipers, alignment
WARRANTY EXPIRES at year 3 - this period carries full cost
checkpoints.source: Covers years 3-5 only. REDUCED BY AUDIT from NT$98,000 to NT$78,000: the original carried a NT$46,000 dealer-fitted 19-inch tyre set, which is above the going Taiwan dealer rate for this size (~NT$8,000-10,000 per tyre fitted, i.e. ~NT$38,000 a set), and the period as a whole sat only NT$12,000 below the combustion CLA 180's same window despite the BEV having no oil, filter, plug or DCT service in it. This is still the step change in the curve: the 3-year warranty has lapsed so the owner now pays everything, and the age-driven tyre set plus the first 12V battery both land here. No published price table or owner receipt for EQ servicing could be retrieved (Mobile01 blocks automated access; mercedes-benz.com.tw times out), so these are modelled from market dealer rates rather than sourced quotes - hence low confidence.

major_items: Front and rear brake pads AND discs (~NT$34,000) - discs corrode from disuse because regen means the friction brakes are barely used, a well-known BEV problem in humid Taiwan
Suspension bushings and lower arms (~NT$20,000) - standard German 6-7 year wear item
Heat-pump / air-conditioning service and repair allowance (~NT$12,000)
Coolant service, brake fluid, two annual inspections
Cabin filters, wipers, alignment
Four years out of warranty - no subsidy of any kind
checkpoints.source: Covers years 5-7 only. REDUCED BY AUDIT from NT$125,000 to NT$88,000. The original placed this BEV window ABOVE the combustion CLA 180's equivalent window (NT$105,000), which is not defensible: the combustion car's 5-7 year spend is dominated by the 1.3L turbo, its 48V starter-generator, plugs, coils and DCT service, none of which exist here. It also double-charged a 12V battery at year 7 when one was already fitted at year 5 - a 4-5 year part, so the next one falls in the 7-10 window and has been moved there. Retained in full: brake discs are deliberately charged in this period rather than earlier, because regeneration preserves pad material while promoting disc corrosion, so the failure mode on a low-mileage Taiwanese BEV is rust-driven disc replacement at this age. Loaded for a German car four years past its warranty. Modelled from Mercedes dealer labour rates; no published Taiwan price table for these operations on the MMA platform exists, so this is an estimate, not a quote.

major_items: Second tyre set (~NT$40,000)
Electrical/electronic repair allowance (~NT$45,000) - on-board charger, DC-DC converter, charging port, sensors, MBUX unit; these are the expensive failures on an out-of-warranty German BEV
Shock absorbers, struts and remaining suspension (~NT$35,000) on an 8-10 year old German chassis
High-voltage battery thermal-management electric water pump (~NT$22,000) - a named BEV risk item
Second 12V battery (~NT$14,000)
Three annual inspections, coolant service, two brake fluid changes
HIGH-VOLTAGE BATTERY WARRANTY (~8 years) LAPSES inside this window - the car now carries uninsured pack risk
checkpoints.source: Covers years 7-10 only (a 3-year window), ~NT$58,000/year. REDUCED BY AUDIT from NT$255,000 to NT$175,000. The original was essentially level with the combustion CLA 180's NT$248,000 for the same window, which cannot be right for a car with no engine, gearbox service or 48V ISG; the heat-pump allowance was also being charged twice, once here and once at year 7. Still deliberately risk-loaded rather than flattened: this is the period where the ~8-year high-voltage battery warranty runs out and every electronic module is unwarranted, and German BEV out-of-warranty electronics are the dominant cost, not mechanical wear. At NT$175,000 it remains well above the Volvo EC40's NT$140,000 and far above the Toyota bZ4X's NT$102,000 for the same window. Excludes any allowance for actual traction-battery replacement, which would exceed the car's whole residual value at that age and is treated as a write-off scenario rather than a maintenance line. Fully modelled - no Taiwan cost data exists at this age for any German BEV because none has reached 10 years - hence low confidence.

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; all checkpoints use 7,000 km x years (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000), far below the Taiwan average of ~12,000-15,000 km/yr. Powertrain: U-CAR's launch report confirms the CLE 200 Coupé uses a 2.0L turbo four with 204hp / 32.6 kgm plus a 48V mild-hybrid system giving a 23hp assist, paired with 9G-Tronic and rear-wheel drive. The 48V system CANNOT move the car on electricity alone, so it is classified "gasoline", not "hybrid". Because annual distance is so low, servicing is driven by the TIME leg of the Mercedes 10,000 km / 1 year interval, never the mileage leg — roughly one A or B service every year at ~7,000 km, with brake fluid (2-yearly) and coolant (5-yearly) falling due on the calendar. Tires likewise time out on rubber age (~5-6 years) long before they wear out. Vehicle licence tax (牌照稅), fuel tax (汽燃費) and all insurance are EXCLUDED by design. Financing interest, parking, fuel and tolls are also out of scope. The CLE 200 Coupé rides on steel springs (18" AMG wheels with 加大打孔前碟盤 standard, 19" on higher trims) and has no air suspension, so no air-strut replacement is budgeted — the German out-of-warranty risk shows up instead as coil packs, thermostat housing, electric auxiliary water pump, the 48V starter-generator and suspension bushings.

EXTRAPOLATED — the current CLE generation launched in Taiwan in March 2024 and no genuine 5-year car exists. Method: take real used prices of the PREDECESSOR generation (Mercedes E-Class Coupé C238, which the CLE replaces alongside the C-Class Coupé), express them as a retention ratio of that car's own original list price, then apply the ratio here. Read on 8891 on 2026-08-12: a 2021 E200 Coupé with 60,000 km asks 155.0萬 and 2020 cars with 62,000-77,000 km ask 148.8-149.0萬, against a ~315萬 list = ~47-49% of list at dealer retail at 5-6 years. Those comparables carry 60,000+ km against our 35,000 km, so a low-mileage premium was added. A second, explicit correction the original record missed: the C238 was DISCONTINUED and replaced by the CLE, so its current 4-6 year prices carry an orphaned-generation discount the CLE will not face at the same age — the raw C238 ratio therefore biases this checkpoint low. Net ~55% of list = ~160萬 dealer retail. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale = dealer retail x 0.885 (~142萬); dealer_tradein = private x 0.866 (~123萬). Explicitly extrapolated, not observed.

EXTRAPOLATED from the predecessor E-Class Coupé (C238) via retention ratio — no 7-year data exists for this generation. ADJUSTMENT APPLIED: private_sale = dealer retail x 0.87 (~115萬); dealer_tradein = private x 0.857 (~98.5萬). The drop from 50% of real_cost at year 5 to 41% at year 7 is deliberate: the 3-year / 100,000 km factory warranty is long gone and the used market prices in German out-of-warranty repair risk rather than flattening.

EXTRAPOLATED from predecessor-generation retention ratios — no 10-year data exists for this generation. Real anchors read on 8891 on 2026-08-12: 2017 E200 Coupé (9 years, the C238's own launch year, list 276萬 per U-CAR) spans 61.8萬 at 210,000 km, 82.8-88.0萬 at 220,000-225,000 km, 98.0-99.8萬 at 120,000-160,000 km and 103.8萬 at 83,000 km — i.e. 22-38% of list, with the low-mileage car at the top. The tail keeps falling (50% -> 41% -> 26% of real_cost) rather than flattening, because an out-of-warranty German coupé is priced on repair risk and two-door bodies have the thinnest resale demand in Taiwan.

maintenance.plan_notes: Taiwan Mercedes-Benz servicing is 每10,000公里或每1年，以先到者為準, alternating A 保養 (Service A) and B 保養 (Service B) — both confirmed on the cited whbydcc 保養週期 page. At only 7,000 km/year the interval is TIME-DRIVEN, never mileage-driven: the owner returns roughly once a year at ~7,000 km, and brake fluid (每2年不論里程) plus coolant (5年或10萬公里) fall due purely on the calendar. PRICING CORRECTION versus the original record: the whbydcc cost page states B 保養 at 兩萬到三萬五千元 (NT$20,000-35,000), not the NT$15,000-30,000 originally quoted, and tyaward's dealer column gives A 保養 NT$8,000-12,000, B 保養 NT$12,000-30,000, 煞車油 NT$2,500-4,000, 煞車來令片/碟盤 NT$15,000-30,000 per axle, 懸吊避震 NT$30,000-60,000, 變速箱油 NT$15,000-80,000 and 19吋輪胎四條 NT$32,000-45,000. The original record priced B services at NT$21,000-23,000 and suspension work at NT$26,000 — at or below the floor of those dealer bands for a service that includes brake fluid plus two filters on an E-Class-platform coupé. B services are repriced to NT$25,000-28,000 and suspension to the NT$30,000 band floor, lifting the ten-year total from ~NT$584,000 to ~NT$617,000 (~NT$61,700/year). New-car warranty is the Taiwan standard 3年或10萬公里, so the 1-year and 3-year periods carry SCHEDULED SERVICE ONLY with no repair risk. Mercedes-Benz Taiwan does sell 延長保固 and prepaid service packages, but they are paid options rather than standard on the CLE, so NO subsidy is applied to the early periods and the 5-, 7- and 10-year periods carry the FULL unsubsidised out-of-warranty cost. Later-period risk items are budgeted probability-weighted and are specifically the German ones: coil packs, thermostat housing, electric auxiliary water pump, the 48V starter-generator and suspension bushings. NO air-suspension budget is included because the CLE 200 Coupé rides on steel springs — AIRMATIC/AMG Ride Control is not fitted to this variant. Consumables land where the calendar puts them: tires at years ~5 and ~10 (aged out, not worn out, at this mileage), front brakes around 35,000 km and again near 70,000 km, rear brakes around 49,000 km, the 12V AGM battery around years 6 and 10 (short low-mileage trips are hard on it), spark plugs and 9G-Tronic fluid in the 5-7 year window.

assumptions.notes: 車主年行駛 6,000-8,000 km，遠低於台灣平均 12,000-15,000 km。各檢查點一律用中位數 7,000 km/年（7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km）。此里程下 ASSYST PLUS 保養提示是被「時間」觸發而非里程：依 2ggx 保養費資料，Service A 為 1.5 年或 15,000 km、Service B 為 2 年或 30,000 km，本車約 2.1 年才跑到 15,000 km，所以時間先到，保養每 12-18 個月一次（原研究者寫「每 12 個月」略為高估次數，已修正）。輪胎與煞車油同樣是「放到老化」而非「用到磨耗」。牌照稅、燃料稅、保險依設計一律不計入。動力註記：M254 2.0T 搭 48V ISG（EQBoost）皮帶啟動發電機，無法純電行駛，故分類為 gasoline 而非 hybrid（KingAutos 車型頁把整個 E-Class 標成 hybrid 是指輕油電，不影響本表分類）。非 BEV，無充電樁成本。殘值以「低里程車況良好個體」報價，但重要修正：8891 實際掛牌資料顯示中高齡 E-Class 的里程溢價非常小（見 value_checkpoints），故低里程加成只給 2-4%，不採原研究者隨車齡放大到 10% 的假設。

purchase.source: list_price NT$3,010,000 本次已獨立查證成功（原研究者無法驗證）。KingAutos 國王車訊 2026-04-16 專文「旗艦科技下放！《Mercedes-Benz E-Class》星耀版 最高升級逾18萬配備 全面標配夜色套件」(https://www.kingautos.net/368283) 的價格表逐字列出「E 200 LUXURY 星耀版 3,010,000」，升級配備價值 105,000（AVANTGARDE 夜色套件、19 吋輪圈、黑色頂篷）。第二來源 KingAutos E-Class 車型價格頁 (https://www.kingautos.net/hot/mercedes_benz/e-class) 列出台灣 E-Class 級距：E200 Avantgarde 2,750,000／E200 Luxury 2,930,000／E300 運動版 3,470,000／E300 Exclusive 3,550,000／AMG E53 4Matic+ 4,760,000 —— 2,930,000 + 80,000 = 3,010,000，與星耀版加價幅度完全吻合，交叉驗證成立。udn 車訊 2026-04-15 (https://autos.udn.com/autos/story/7825/9443825) 報導 C-Class／E-Class 星耀版同批上市、225 萬元起（該起價屬 C-Class），佐證上市時點。折讓與領牌費為經銷通路慣例推估，非官方公告。
purchase.notes: 【已修正車型名稱】原記錄寫「E 200 星耀版 (Avantgarde)」並稱其為「Avantgarde 配備的入門車型」，這是錯的。台灣 E-Class 的 Avantgarde 與 Luxury 是兩個不同等級，且 Avantgarde 比較便宜：E200 Avantgarde 2,750,000、E200 Luxury 2,930,000。NT$3,010,000 的星耀版是建立在 LUXURY 上（KingAutos 價格表逐字寫 E 200 LUXURY 星耀版），它既不是 Avantgarde、也不是入門車型。加購的是「AVANTGARDE 夜色套件」，套件名稱與車型等級被原研究者混為一談。id 沿用 mercedes-e200-avantgarde 僅為資料表主鍵，不代表車型等級。車系為 Mercedes-Benz E-Class Saloon (W214)。動力：M254 2.0L 渦輪直四約 204 hp，搭 48V ISG／EQBoost 整合式啟動發電機約 23 hp 電輔助。此 48V 系統僅為輕油電，可怠速熄火重啟、填補扭力斷層與回充，無法純電推進，依本表規則分類 gasoline；48V 硬體列在此處是因為它在 7-10 年會變成保固外的實際成本項。懸吊為傳統鋼簧 AGILITY CONTROL，未配 AIRMATIC 氣壓懸吊（氣壓懸吊屬 E 300／AMG 側選配），因此不提列氣壓避震器更換 —— 這是本車尾段養護比氣壓懸吊德系 SUV 便宜的主因。【已修正折讓】原記錄取 150,000（5.0%）過高：台灣賓士對 E-Class 的操作是以 0 利率與延長保固取代現金折讓，KingAutos 2026-03 購車優惠 (https://www.kingautos.net/367656) 明列 E-Class「160萬 40期 0利率 + 1年延長保固」；且星耀版是 2026-04 才上市的新特仕車，現金空間更小。同批 GLC 200（274 萬）記錄採 50,000（1.8%），E-Class 房車級距買氣弱於 GLC，給稍多空間，取 80,000（2.7%）。【已修正領牌與配件】原記錄取 60,000 與同批基準不一致（GLC 200 於 274 萬車價取 40,000）。本車依車價等比放大取 45,000 = 領牌規費約 5,000 + 代辦約 5,000 + 交車配件約 35,000（隔熱紙、鍍膜、行車紀錄器、腳踏墊、迎賓踏板）。稅金與保險排除。real_cost = 3,010,000 - 80,000 + 45,000 = 2,975,000。

value_checkpoints.source: 改用實際掛牌（原記錄此點無任何來源卻標 medium）。8891 實抓現行 W214 車源：2025 E200 12,900 km 車商開價 2,380,000、2025 E200 14,000 km 開價 2,268,000，均值約 2,324,000。該等 2025 年式 E 200 新車價約 2,930,000（Luxury），real cost 約 2,895,000。車商零售 2,324,000 →【自售調整】扣約 11% 得自售 2,068,000，殘值率 71.4%。將 71.4% 套回本車 real_cost 2,975,000 得 2,124,000，再給 7,000 km 對 13,000 km 的低里程加成約 2%（8891 資料顯示近新車里程溢價本就有限），取 2,160,000。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 13% = 1,880,000。第 1 年帳面損失約 27%，符合德系豪華房車在台灣的前段陡降，且車商零售價未被直接抄進自售價。

【修正原記錄的事實錯誤】原記錄稱「台灣尚無真正 3 年車齡的 W214」而改用 W213 跨代外推；W214 於 2024 年中在台上市，8891 上實際存在 2 年車齡車源，本點因此改以現行世代真實掛牌為錨。實抓：2024 E200 Luxury 20,000 km 車商開價 2,120,000（2 年車齡）。該車新車價 2,930,000、real cost 約 2,895,000；車商零售 2,120,000 →扣約 11% 得自售 1,887,000，2 年殘值率 65.2%。由 1 年 71.4%、2 年 65.2%、5 年 48.1% 的實測序列內插，3 年殘值率取約 59%，套回 real_cost 2,975,000 得 1,755,000，取 1,760,000（21,000 km 與參考車 20,000 km 相當，不另給里程加成）。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 13.5% = 1,520,000。此時仍在 3 年不限里程原廠保固內，對價格有支撐。

以前代 W213 小改款實際掛牌換算殘值率再套用（本車 2031 年才滿 5 年）。實抓錨點：2021 E200 Avantgarde 60,000 km 車商開價 1,368,000。該 2021 年式 W213 小改 E 200 新車價約 2,690,000、real cost 約 2,655,000。本車 5 年時僅 35,000 km，較參考車低甚多，給約 5% 低里程加成得車商零售約 1,436,000 →扣約 11% 得自售 1,278,000，殘值率 48.1%。套回 real_cost 2,975,000 得 1,431,000；因此點僅有單一筆 2021 年掛牌支撐，且該車屬小改款外觀有溢價，保守下修取 1,400,000。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 14% = 1,205,000。這是第一個脫離 3 年原廠保固的檢查點，台灣中古市場自此開始把維修風險計入價格，曲線不會像 Lexus 那樣打平。

【本次最大幅修正，原記錄高估約 14%】原記錄宣稱 2019 年式 W213 E 200 的車商開價約 1,150,000-1,300,000，與實際市場不符。8891 實抓 2019 E200 共 4 筆：11,780 km／889,000、56,100 km／949,000、117,000 km／889,000，另 2018 E200 50,000 km／850,000，實際區間是 850,000-949,000，不是 115 萬-130 萬。取低里程車商零售 900,000。2019 年式 W213 E 200 新車價約 2,620,000、real cost 約 2,585,000；車商零售 900,000 →扣約 11% 得自售 801,000，殘值率 31.0%。套回本車 real_cost 2,975,000 得 922,000，加約 3% 低里程加成取 950,000。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 14.5% = 810,000（保固外德系車商需承擔整備風險，收購折讓隨車齡放大）。注意：同一批資料中 11,780 km 與 117,000 km 的 2019 E200 開價同為 889,000，證實中高齡德系房車的里程溢價極小，原記錄逐年放大到 10% 的低里程加成不成立。

以前代 W213 首批年份（2016，W213 在台上市年）實際掛牌換算。8891 實抓 2016 E200：81,000 km／738,000、110,000 km／668,000、120,000 km／498,000；另 2017 E200 11,700 km／759,000、80,000 km／768,000；2015（前代 W212）則掉到 518,000-598,000、2014 為 478,000-498,000、2013 為 258,000 —— 世代斷點造成的落差遠大於里程。本車 2036 年滿 10 年時屬世代中期車（W214 於 2024 上市，2026 年式為小改前），比今日 2016 首批 W213 更靠近世代尾端，故取車商零售 700,000（介於 2016 低里程 738,000 與 2015 世代斷點之間）。2016 年式 W213 E 200 新車價約 2,530,000、real cost 約 2,495,000；車商零售 700,000 →扣約 11% 得自售 623,000，殘值率 25.0%。套回 real_cost 2,975,000 得 743,000，加約 4% 低里程加成取 770,000。dealer_tradein = 自售再扣約 15.5% = 650,000。尾段續跌未打平：保固外德系豪華房車買家池薄，48V 鋰電池／ISG、電子水泵、變速箱機電、電子系統的大額風險都被計入價格。

maintenance.plan_notes: 台灣賓士原廠（授權經銷）保養，ASSYST PLUS 之 Service A／Service B 交替。【重要修正一：取消原記錄的免費保養假設】原記錄假設台灣賓士隨車附贈 3 年預付保養套餐（星徽保養套餐），把 0-1 年與 1-3 年壓到 3,000 與 12,000。此假設無根據且是本記錄最大的模型錯誤：台灣賓士新車標配的是 3 年不限里程原廠「保固」，定期保養並不免費；星徽保養套餐是「付費預付」方案（先付費換取折扣），不是隨車贈品。實際促銷內容亦可佐證——KingAutos 2026-03 購車優惠對 E-Class 給的是「160萬 40期 0利率 + 1年延長保固」，給的是延長保固而非免費保養。故 0-3 年改採全額自付。官網保固頁本次逾時無法讀取，無法正面證實或證偽，因此採不含免費保養的保守假設並在此明說。【重要修正二：保養週期】原記錄寫「每 12 個月一次」；依 2ggx 保養費資料，Service A 為 1.5 年或 15,000 km、Service B 為 2 年或 30,000 km。本車 7,000 km/年要約 2.1 年才跑到 15,000 km，所以確實是時間先觸發（原記錄結論正確），但實際週期是每 12-18 個月而非每 12 個月，10 年約 7-8 次進廠而非 10 次。輪胎（5-6 年老化）與煞車油（2 年）同為日曆項目而非磨耗項目。單價採 2ggx 的 E-Class 級距區間中位：Service A 約 12,000（區間 10,000-15,000）、Service B 約 24,000（區間 18,000-30,000）。台灣原廠工資約 NT$2,500-3,000/小時，明顯高於日系經銷商，且 E-Class 的大尺寸煞車與 19 吋輪圈 245 級距輪胎相應昂貴。本車為鋼簧 AGILITY CONTROL，未配 AIRMATIC，故不提列氣壓避震器更換（若為氣壓懸吊，7-10 年窗口需另加約 120,000-180,000）。48V ISG 啟動發電機與其鋰電池以期望值方式提列於 7-10 年窗口。【修正三】7-10 年由原記錄的 340,000 下修至 300,000：原記錄在 5-7 年已提列 30,000 冷卻／點火風險，7-10 年又提 45,000「第二輪」冷卻點火，且在僅 70,000 km 下提列 50,000 的完整避震器更換，屬重複與過度提列；本記錄改為冷卻點火第二輪 40,000、懸吊以引擎腳與連桿襯套為主 35,000。10 年合計約 633,000（70,000 km），約為同級日系房車的 2.5-3 倍，且較同批 GLC 200（480,000）高約 32%，符合更大車體、更大煞車輪胎與更完整保固外風險提列的預期。

checkpoints.source: 依 2ggx 賓士保養費整理 (https://www.2ggx.com/賓士保養費/) 的 E-Class 級距 Service A NT$10,000-15,000，取中位 12,000 再加雨刷等耗材。【修正】原記錄此格為 3,000，理由是假設隨車附贈 3 年預付保養套餐；該假設無來源支撐（台灣賓士標配的是 3 年保固而非免費保養，且 2026-03 官方促銷給的是延長保固），故改為全額自付。同批 GLC 200 記錄此格為 11,000，本車為更大級距，13,000 與之一致。2ggx 屬二手整理來源而非原廠價目表，故仍標 low。

assumptions.notes: Buyer drives 6,000-8,000 km/year; every checkpoint uses the 7,000 km/year midpoint (7,000 / 21,000 / 35,000 / 49,000 / 70,000 km). That is roughly half the Taiwan average of 12,000-15,000 km/year, so servicing is TIME-driven (annual/biennial calendar intervals), not mileage-driven, and consumables age out rather than wear out - tires are replaced on age (~every 5-6 years) long before tread depth is reached. On low-mileage pricing: the intent is to quote low-mileage comparables, but the actual 8891 EQA data does NOT show a clean low-mileage premium (the 14,000 km car is the cheapest in the set at 122.0萬 while the 63,700 km car asks 130.0萬), so the used market for this nameplate is too thin for mileage to drive price. Values below are therefore anchored on the upper part of the observed asking range rather than on a computed mileage premium, and this is stated in each source string. EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: tax and insurance (Taiwan currently exempts BEVs from 牌照稅 and 燃料費 - Yahoo Autos shows both as $0 for this car - but they are out of scope either way). ALSO EXCLUDED: home-charger installation. A dedicated 220V circuit / wallbox in Taiwan runs roughly NT$30,000-80,000 depending on distance to the panel, and in an apartment it additionally requires 管委會 approval which may block it entirely; it is a one-off capital installation, not maintenance, so it is deliberately left out of maintenance.checkpoints. Public DC fast charging is likewise not modelled (energy cost, not maintenance).

purchase.source: List price NT$2,170,000 (217萬) independently re-verified by this fact-check by fetching the pages directly. U-CAR 26MY road test states verbatim '配備/電氣性能/電池容量升級，新年式 EQA 250+售價 217 萬' and its own model box shows '1 車型 217 萬'; ETtoday states verbatim '目前台灣EQA售價217萬'. Both read 2026-08-12. The brand's own models.html genuinely does not respond from this environment (curl returns status 000 / timeout), which I re-tested and confirmed, so it is retained in sources[] with an explicit caveat rather than cited as read. CORRECTION TO THE PRIOR RECORD: it claimed Yahoo Autos as a third price verification showing '217 (萬)'. I fetched that page and it carries NO price at all - only 牌照稅 $0 and 燃料稅 $0. That claim was removed; the Yahoo source is kept for the tax-status fact only. Price verification therefore rests on two sources I confirmed verbatim, not three. Discount and on-road fees are estimates, not a published table.
purchase.notes: NOT a hybrid and not a 48V mild hybrid - this is a full BEV, and the '250+' suffix denotes the enlarged battery (usable capacity raised from 66.5 kWh to 70.5 kWh), NOT any hybrid assist system. WLTP range rises from 426 km to 561 km (NEDC 606 km per the Bureau of Energy filing). Single trim in Taiwan; the 250+ replaced the EQA 250 for the 2026 model year at an unchanged 217萬. DISCOUNT (NT$200,000, 9.2% off list) - deliberately larger than the 3-8% a German brand normally concedes in Taiwan, and the justification is now independently verified rather than asserted: I fetched the ETtoday article of 2026-07-30 and it says verbatim that the all-new MMA-platform GLA '象徵GLA與EQA產品線正式整合' - the EQA nameplate is being merged out of existence. The successor GLA 250+ carries an 85 kWh pack, 800V architecture, 320 kW DC charging and 657 km WLTP from EUR 48,599.60 (~NT$1.8m), and the same article confirms Taiwanese dealers were already privately taking orders ('台灣經銷端早已私下排隊接單') for a 2027 arrival, headlined '新台幣200萬有找'. This car is therefore a run-out model of a dying nameplate whose replacement is better and cheaper. That is exactly when Taiwanese Mercedes dealers discount hardest, so a NT$150,000-250,000 package (cash off plus 領牌 absorbed plus accessories) is realistic and I kept the midpoint. For contrast, the same-price current GLA 200 (216萬) is modelled at only a NT$70,000 discount in this batch - correctly, because it is the fresh model, not the run-out one. ON-ROAD FEES CORRECTED from NT$80,000 to NT$55,000: the prior figure was 78% above the same-price sibling (GLA 200 at 216萬 uses NT$45,000 for the identical 領牌+代辦+配件 definition) and was built from a premium-end accessory list (隔熱紙 30,000 + 鍍膜 20,000). NT$55,000 = 領牌/新領牌照登記 and 代辦 (~NT$10,000) + 隔熱紙 (~NT$20,000) + 鍍膜 (~NT$12,000) + 行車記錄器 (~NT$8,000) + 腳踏墊/行李廂墊 (~NT$5,000), keeping a small premium over the GLA 200 because EV buyers at this price do fit more accessories. Tax and insurance are excluded by design and are NOT in real_cost. real_cost = 2,170,000 - 200,000 + 55,000 = 2,025,000.
